    # Part E: Diagnostic Code Libraries

    Home › Configuration › System

    This part holds the settings for code systems and the services that search them. PathScribe does not hold the content of SNOMED CT, ICD, ICD-O, LOINC or CPT itself. Each is maintained by its own standards body and looked up through a service.

    Where the related dictionaries are. The CPT modifier list is the CPT Modifier Dictionary and the charge-code list is the Billing Dictionary. Both are documented in Chapter 8, not here. Code Import (Bulk) below loads billing codes into the Billing Dictionary. It does not import diagnosis codes.

    # Code Systems

    Home › Configuration › System › Clinical Lookups › Code Systems

    3. Business purpose and scope. For each country you serve, says which code systems (ICD-10, ICD-11, ICD-O, SNOMED CT, LOINC, CPT, OPCS-4 and others) are Off, Optional or Required, and from what date. Moving a region from ICD-10 to ICD-11 is a setting here, not a software change. A second card, Licensed terminologies, records the SNOMED CT and ICD-O-3 licences your organisation holds. Real codes entered on Abnormal Trigger Rules are used only while the matching licence is switched on and has not expired. Until then clearly marked test codes are attached.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. The list of countries is the laboratory's own jurisdiction plus the jurisdiction of every active facility, so the facilities are set up first (Facility Dictionary). Skip them and only the laboratory's own country is listed.

    # Terminology Services

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations › Terminology Services

    Status: Built

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Integrations 2. Maintenance item: Terminology Services

    3. Business purpose and scope. A connectivity check. It confirms that PathScribe can reach the coding systems used for code search and AI suggestions: SNOMED CT, ICD-10, ICD-11, LOINC, ICD-O and CPT. There is nothing to add or upload here. Every system is maintained by its own standards body and is not versioned inside PathScribe. The checks run when the screen opens and when you select Test All.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. The correct ICD-10 variant is chosen from your active Governing Bodies: ICD-10-CM for the US (CAP), ICD-10 WHO for RCPath and ICCR, and ICD-10-AM for RCPA. Non-US variants and CPT need a backend proxy. When an API server address is configured, the ICD-10-CM, ICD-11 and LOINC look-ups go through the server, as described in docs/architecture/TERMINOLOGY_PROXY_API.md. SNOMED CT and ICD-O are checked through the server's UMLS route.

    3. Business purpose and scope. Decides which synoptic field and value pairs flag a case as Abnormal, Critical or Malignant. A match is always a suggestion that the pathologist confirms or disputes at sign-out, never an automatic determination. A switch at the top turns abnormal detection off for the whole enterprise.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. A rule can carry real SNOMED CT and ICD-O-3 codes, which are used only while the matching licence is switched on and in date on Code Systems. Until then PathScribe attaches clearly marked test codes. The enterprise switch is a master switch: while it is off, no facility can turn detection on for itself on its Facility Dictionary record.

    # [FORMEDRIXAI INTERNAL ONLY] Governing Bodies

    Home › Configuration › System › Clinical Lookups › Governing Bodies

    🔒 ForMedrixAI Internal Restricted Setting Scope: Internal Service & Deployment Personnel Only. Explanation: This list decides which standards bodies are in force and how long each body says material must be kept. The retention figures it holds are the floor that every department's Retention Override is checked against, and they feed the retention clock on stored blocks, slides and wet tissue. A change by an end user could shorten a legal retention period or switch on a body that does not apply to the laboratory's country, so editing needs the platform capability platform:governing-bodies:manage, held by Superadmin only. Everyone else sees the list read-only with the notice "Super admin access required".

    Status: Built

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Clinical Lookups 2. Maintenance item: Governing Bodies

    3. Business purpose and scope. A governing body is a standards or regulatory body, such as CAP, RCPath, ICCR, RCPA, CAP-ACP, the EU (ISO 15189) or the Korean MSA. Each body is enabled or disabled, covers some jurisdictions, and holds an append-only history of retention figures (days for blocks, slides and wet tissue). A retention figure is used only from an enabled body with at least one version that covers the jurisdiction. Custom bodies can be added.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. This is a starting point. Without a retention version on an enabled body for the laboratory's jurisdiction there is no retention floor, so a department's retention override is not checked. Departments read it (Departments). The ICD-10 variant on Terminology Services follows the active bodies.

    Unverified placeholder figures. Not every seeded figure is a published requirement. The CAP and CAP-ACP wet-tissue figures, all of RCPA's figures (NPAAC publishes Australia's own requirements) and Korea's MSA figure are unverified placeholders: reasonable conservative starting points that ForMedrixAI has not confirmed against the published schedules. The retention window marks every version whose source note says so with an amber badge, UNVERIFIED PLACEHOLDER, next to its source note, and the note names which figure is the placeholder. Do not treat a flagged figure as a legal or accreditation requirement. Before go-live, a records or compliance lead confirms each flagged figure for your laboratory and publishes a new version with the cited source; the badge goes when the note no longer says unverified. The CAP and RCPath block and slide figures carry citations (CAP/CLIA 42 CFR 493.1105 and checklist ANP.12500; RCPath/IBMS G031) which you should still check against the current edition.

    # Tier 3: Workflow Engines and Operational Configuration (Configure Third)

    Tier 3 is the part of Configuration that decides how work moves once the people, sites, devices and dictionaries of Tiers 1 and 2 exist: where a case is routed, which commands and macros a bench offers, how a case is held for review before and after sign-out, and how turnaround and quality are measured. Do it third. Most screens here read a dictionary from Tier 1 or Tier 2 (a facility, a subspecialty, a specimen type) and show an empty picklist until that dictionary is filled.

    Read this before you start. Four things are different from what the product's own screen titles suggest.

    • There is no "Order Entry workflow template" or "Accessioning workflow template". Accessioning behaviour is spread across settings that are documented where they live; Where the accessioning settings live lists them. Not built.
    • Several screens keep their values in the browser of the computer used to set them (Case Routing, Routing Rules, Action Registry, Inking Validation Mode, Follow-Up Tracking, Biopsy-Resection Correlation, Contribution Settings, and the deployment switches on the Voice tab). The screen's status says so. Settings like these are not seen by other workstations until the API server version exists.
    • Digital pathology is mostly a vendor dictionary. PathScribe lists vendors and a viewer launch address; it has no scanner driver, and it does not show slide images itself. See Digital pathology.
    • Almost every sign-out and quality setting has an organisation default and a per-laboratory override. The override is made on the Facility Configuration edit window (Facility Dictionary) or inside the screen.

    Configure Tier 3 in this order. Each setup screen carries a Setup sequence box with the same information, and the builder checks that no screen requires one that comes after it. Screens marked reference are day-to-day pages and are not setup.

    1. Routing Rules: keyword rules that send a case to a subspecialty pool.
    2. Case Routing: the pool-assignment settings and the fuller rule editor.
    3. Action Registry (tab): the commands, their shortcuts and voice phrases.
    4. Action Groups: named bundles of commands for a workstation.
    5. Macros (tab): shared text macros and the Word AutoText import.
    6. Voice (tab): speech recognition switches, personal voice settings and the foot pedal.
    7. Grossing Route Overrides: a fixed grossing route for a facility and specimen type.
    8. Inking Validation Mode: warn or enforce on ink problems.
    9. Vendor Integrations: digital pathology, WSI viewer, image store and gross imaging vendors.
    10. Peer Review Gate: where sign-out waits for a peer review.
    11. Concordance Review Settings: preliminary-versus-final comparison.
    12. Release Buffer: the recall window after sign-out.
    13. Country Signing Rules: national rules per participation type (platform administrator only).
    14. Revision Reasons: which amendment and correction reasons recommend a CAPA.
    15. Tumor Board Rules: what lists a case for a board.
    16. Biopsy-Resection Correlation: the biopsy-to-resection window.
    17. Cytology-Histology Correlation: the cytology-to-biopsy window.
    18. Follow-Up Tracking: warnings and clinician e-mail for follow-ups that have not arrived.
    19. Intraoperative Critical Results: frozen results that go straight to the surgeon.
    20. OR Suite Terminals: operating-room displays and their tokens.
    21. Display Profiles: wall displays for the Facility Ops dashboard.
    22. QA Configuration Center: QA activities, sampling and CAPA triggers.
    23. QA Trend Policy: when repeated discordance is flagged.
    24. TAT Configuration (tab): turnaround targets.
    25. Performance Targets: the numbers a pathologist is measured against.
    26. Cytology QC Rules: who is selected for cytology peer review.
    27. Cytology QC Random Selection Rates: the random sampling percentages.
    28. Cytology Daily Workload Cap: the daily slide limit and the screening day.
    29. Contribution Settings: the My Contribution page.
    30. Feedback: the QA feedback button.
    31. Research Feed: the PubMed headline on Home.

    Reference pages, not part of setup: Batch Management, Embedding Station, Microtomy Workstation, Slide Distribution Station, Home, Lockbox Drop-Off, Quality Assurance, Margin Exception Review and Cytology QC Queue.

    # Routing Rules

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations › Routing Rules

    Status: Demonstration

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Integrations 2. Maintenance item: Routing Rules

    3. Business purpose and scope. A routing rule sends a case to a subspecialty pool by matching words in the specimen description. This screen is the simple editor for the keyword rules: one rule is a pool, a list of keywords, a priority and a note. Rules are checked in priority order and the first match wins. PathScribe ships eight built-in rules (colorectal, upper GI, hepatobiliary and pancreatic, breast, genitourinary, gynaecological, dermatopathology, haematopathology; priorities 10 to 60). Built-in rules can be edited and switched off but not deleted. The same rules are also shown, with more options (specimen-type matching, a performing lab, per-lab fallback pools), on Case Routing; both screens read and write one stored list.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. A rule points at a pool, and a pool is a subspecialty with Pool / Workgroup switched on. Skip the subspecialties and the Route to Pool list is empty, a warning shows, and a rule cannot be saved.

    # Case Routing

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations › Case Routing

    Status: Demonstration

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Integrations 2. Maintenance item: Case Routing

    3. Business purpose and scope. Case Routing decides how a case with no pathologist assigned reaches a subspecialty pool. The screen holds the master switch, the fallback pool (one Global pool and an optional override for each performing lab), the routing rules with specimen-type and performing-lab scoping, a test box, and a button that routes every unassigned case now. The on-screen diagram "How routing works" gives the order: a case arrives, PathScribe checks for a direct assignment (a case that already has a pathologist is left alone), then the lab's own rules, then the Global rules, then the lab's fallback pool, then the Global fallback pool, and if there is none the case is flagged for manual assignment. A pool tagged Default / Catch-All on Subspecialties takes precedence over the fallbacks set here.

    When routing runs. Routing runs when grossing is completed on a case (a STAT case uses the STAT path), only the first time real diagnostic work begins on it. It does not run at accessioning. A case with no specimens is not routed.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. Pools come from Subspecialties (Pool / Workgroup switched on), specimen types from the Specimen Dictionary and performing labs from the Facility Dictionary (facilities with the performing lab role). Skip the pools and the screen shows "No active pools found" and no fallback can be chosen; skip the facilities and the per-lab table and lab picklists are empty.

Add Collaborator (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+0; needs case:team:manage on the case, the same as the Case Team window, and a cytotechnologist cannot be added as a Consultant); Edit Field (Alt+E) and Cancel (Ctrl+Alt+J), which were listed before and now act; Add Addendum; Sign Out and Next; Collaborating Cases (Ctrl+Alt+F, formerly "Filter My Cases"); Go to Row (Alt+7) and Open Case by Accession (Alt+8) on the Worklist; and View Help, which moved from Alt+V to F1 (Alt+V is Full View on the report screen, and the Help button always works). Twenty-nine registered commands still have no screen handler; each is listed with its reason in docs/product/KNOWN_GAPS.md, and a build test fails when a new command is registered with no listener and no listed reason. The collaborator message is an application notice sent on the person's behalf, so it needs no messaging permission; it is stored in English like the review-request message. Known limits. Demonstration: the registry is held in the browser's demonstration store and no server contract for it exists in docs/architecture/. The list of commands is code, not data. The bulk import does not warn about a shortcut that clashes with a command outside the file; only the Edit window checks that.

    # Macros (tab)

    Home › Configuration › Macros

    Status: Built

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab Macros 2. Maintenance item: My Macros (text macros and the Word AutoText import)

    3. Business purpose and scope. A macro is a block of formatted text that expands when someone types its shortcut (for example ;normcolon) in the report editor and presses Space. Macros live at one of three levels: Enterprise (every facility), Facility (one performing lab) or Personal (one person). Anyone can keep personal and facility macros; Enterprise macros and other people's personal macros are for administrators only. This is also where an auto-text library is loaded: Import from Word reads the AutoText and Building Blocks entries of a Word template.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. Facility macros are filed under a performing lab from the Facility Dictionary; skip it and the facility list is empty, so a Facility macro cannot be saved. The editor's font list is fixed in the tab and does not read Approved Fonts.

    # Grossing Route Overrides

    Home › Configuration › System › Lab Materials & Workflows › Grossing Route Overrides

    Status: Built

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Lab Materials & Workflows 2. Maintenance item: Grossing Route Overrides

    3. Business purpose and scope. An override says that, for one facility, one specimen type always uses a named grossing route. After accessioning, PathScribe proposes a grossing template for each specimen. A specimen that matches an active override (same facility and exactly the same specimen type) takes the override's route with 100 percent confidence and is not sent to the AI at all. Everything not listed uses the normal routing.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. The facility comes from the Facility Dictionary and the specimen type must match the type field of a Specimen Dictionary entry exactly (typing offers the known types). Skip the facilities and the Facility list is empty.

    # Inking Validation Mode

    Home › Configuration › System › Lab Materials & Workflows › Inking Validation Mode

    Status: Partial

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Lab Materials & Workflows 2. Maintenance item: Inking Validation Mode

    3. Business purpose and scope. The structured inking check looks at every margin of a case when someone selects Complete grossing and again at sign-out. It finds three kinds of issue: a margin not marked examined (Severity 2), a margin with no ink recorded (Severity 2), and an ink colour code that is not in the active ink-colour dictionary (Severity 3). This screen chooses, for one facility, between Warn Only and Strict Enforce.

    What the code does today (verified in the source). The screen text says Strict Enforce hard-blocks Complete grossing on a Severity 2 issue. The gate that stops Complete grossing does not do that in either mode: - Severity 3 (unmapped ink colour) always blocks Complete grossing. At sign-out it blocks, or asks for an override from a person holding case:inking-gate:override. - Severity 2 at Complete grossing shows a Proceed with Advisory Note confirmation and then lets grossing complete, in both modes. - The only visible difference today is the notice on the Grossing screen: "Strict Enforce: issues shown below will block sign-out until corrected" against "Warn & Advisory: issues shown below don't block sign-out". - If the ink-colour dictionary cannot be loaded the gate refuses to proceed (palette unavailable). The difference between the screen text and the gate is listed for Pete in open-questions/ch4.md.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. The check compares recorded ink colours with the active ink colours. Skip Ink Colors and every recorded ink colour is unmapped (Severity 3), which blocks Complete grossing. Facilities come from the Facility Dictionary.

    Setup sequence · Tier 3, step 8

    Configure first
    Ink Colors, Facility Dictionary
    This unlocks
    None.

    5. Screen.

    6. Field reference.

    Inking validation mode Choice (radio): Warn Only, Strict Enforce Required Warn Only: Severity 2 issues are flagged but never block (the default). Strict Enforce: described on screen as blocking Complete grossing on Severity 2; see "What the code does today" above. Severity 3 always blocks. Warn Only
    Save Button Not applicable Enabled only after a change. Shows "Saved." or "You don't have permission to change this." A change is written to the audit log as "Inking validation mode changed" with the old and new mode. Not applicable

    7. Permissions. Open the screen: screen:configuration:open. Change the mode: config:inking-validation-mode:manage (high risk, audited; checked in the service for that facility). Admin and Lab Director hold it by default. Overriding a Severity 3 stop at sign-out: case:inking-gate:override, held by Admin and Lab Director. Known limits. Partial for the reason above: the mode is saved and shown, but Strict Enforce does not add a hard stop at Complete grossing. The setting is held in the browser's site-settings store; no server contract for site settings exists in docs/architecture/ yet.

    # Histology worklists, embedding, microtomy and staining stations

    Home › Batch Management

    This part covers the bench screens of the histology workflow. They are day-to-day workbench screens, not maintenance screens, so each uses the reference layout: what it shows, what it needs configured first, and which settings change its behaviour. There is no separate configuration screen for the stations themselves. A station's behaviour is set on screens in other chapters: the Scan Stations and Printer Profiles screens (which printer a station uses), the Label Designer (what the printed label shows), Field Requirements (which fields must be filled, by page: batchManagement, embedding, microtomy, slideDistribution), and the Voice tab (foot pedal). A staining station has no screen of its own: staining runs are batches (see Batch Management), and the stain list is the Diagnostic Catalog.

    # Batch Management

    Home › Batch Management

    Status: Built

    1. Navigation: Home > Batch Management (not in Configuration). Opens with screen:batch-management:open. 2. Maintenance item: Not applicable. This is a workbench hub.

    3. Business purpose and scope. Batch Management tracks groups of cassettes and slides through the processing nodes (Decal / Special Processing, Processing, Embedding, Microtomy / Sectioning, Staining, Checkout, External Referral, Cytology Processing, Cytology Staining, Cytology Imaging) by container barcode. It gives chain-of-custody scanning, reconciliation, and a set of queue and report pages reached from tiles. A batch is a container (a staining rack, tissue processor basket, archive storage tray, decal vessel or ad-hoc batch) with a master barcode and a manifest of the items scanned into it.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. The screen reads the scan station set for this computer (to pre-fill the target workstation and to scope the Disposal Queue and Pending Load to the station's facility), the reagent lots and stains for staining and cytology batches, and the facilities with the Reference Lab role for referral batches. With none of these the page still opens, but the matching fields of New Container stay empty.

    # Pathologist sign-out, review, quality and operations settings

    Home › Configuration › System

    This part covers every setting that shapes sign-out and the quality, turnaround and operations screens around it. The screens are grouped as: sign-out and review rules; intraoperative and display; turnaround; quality assurance and cytology QC; and other (contribution, feedback, research feed). The day-to-day pages (Home, Quality Assurance, Lockbox Drop-Off, Margin Exception Review, Cytology QC Queue) are reference pages and are at the end of the part.

    Almost every screen below follows one pattern: an organisation default that each performing lab can inherit or override on the Facility Configuration edit window (Facility Dictionary, Tier 1). The performing lab is the lab that signs the case out, found from the ordering facility. All of them are high-risk configuration: only Admin and Lab Director (and the ForMedrixAI super-administrator) hold the permission to change them by default, and a person without it sees the screen read-only.

    # Peer Review Before Sign-Out

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance › Peer Review Gate

    Status: Built

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Administration & Compliance 2. Maintenance item: Peer Review Gate

    3. Business purpose and scope. A first-time malignancy (judged from the patient's earlier cases) is always recommended for an independent peer review. This screen decides where sign-out also waits for that review. It is off by default. The most specific setting wins: department, then performing lab, then the organisation. When the gate is on, a pathologist can still sign out ahead of the review for urgent care, giving a reason; the review is then owed within 24 hours.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. The rows come from the performing labs (Facility Dictionary) and from the subspecialties (Subspecialties, shown as "Department"). Without them only the organisation switch is available.

    # Release Buffer

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance › Release Buffer

    Status: Partial

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Administration & Compliance 2. Maintenance item: Release Buffer (title on screen: Post-Sign-Out Release Buffer)

    3. Business purpose and scope. A temporary hold between sign-out and genuine external release. While the report is held at Pending Release, the signing pathologist can recall and correct it without a formal amendment. These are the organisation-wide defaults. A performing lab can inherit them or set its own enabled, duration and STAT-bypass values on the Facility Configuration edit window; the watermark and print restriction are organisation-wide only.

    What the code does today (verified in the source). The sign-out time that feeds turnaround reports is still recorded at sign-out. A separate "released at" time is recorded when the hold ends. The hold is ended by a timer that runs in any open PathScribe screen (and a background sweep on any open screen). A server-side scheduler that would release a case nobody has open is planned with the API server and is not built, so the release can be late when no screen is open.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. None for the defaults. Lab overrides: Facility Dictionary.

    Setup sequence · Tier 3, step 12

    Configure first
    Facility Dictionary
    This unlocks
    None.

    5. Screen.

    6. Field reference.

    Field Name Data Type / Format Required/Optional Description & Business Logic System Default
    Enable Post-Sign-Out Release Buffer Switch Optional A signed report is held at Pending Release for the buffer duration unless a bypass applies. On
    Buffer Duration Whole number of minutes, 1 to 30 Required A value outside the range is clamped. 10
    Bypass Buffer for STAT Cases Switch Optional STAT cases release immediately. On
    Watermark Banner Text Text Optional Drawn diagonally across any on-screen view of a Pending Release report and sent to the PDF renderer. PathScribe sends the text; it cannot verify the separate renderer draws it. PENDING FINAL RELEASE - DO NOT DISTRIBUTE
    Release Hold Print Policy Choice: Allow, Warn and confirm, Supervisor override, Block Optional What happens when someone prints a report that is still in its release delay (Batch 654; it replaces the old "Restrict In-House Hardcopy Printing" switch). Allow prints at once. Warn and confirm warns that the copy is a watermarked draft and asks the person to confirm. Supervisor override lets only a person holding print:release-hold:override print, and they must give a reason; everyone else is refused. Block allows no printing until the report is released. Any copy that is printed still carries the pending-release watermark. An old setting of on became Warn and confirm; off became Allow. The setting is organisation-wide and is greyed out while the release delay is switched off. Warn and confirm

    7. Permissions. Open the screen: screen:configuration:open. Change: config:release-buffer:manage (high risk; Admin and Lab Director). Print a report during its release hold under Supervisor override: print:release-hold:override ("Print a report during its release hold (supervisor override)"; Lab Director and Admin hold it by default; give it to any other role that should print held reports). Known limits. Partial because of the scheduler point above. The release-sweep server job that would release a report nobody has open is designed (docs/architecture/RELEASE_SWEEP_SERVER_JOB.md: one sweep every minute; a window that is missed releases late and the case is flagged) and is not built. When it is built it will never release a report that is under a surgical sign-out hold; it flags the case for a person instead. A server version of the settings exists (REPORTS_API.md).

    3. Business purpose and scope. At sign-out PathScribe lists a case for a tumor board when a rule matches the signed report, and records why. There are four board names: Breast MDT, GI MDT, Thoracic MDM and Gyn-Onc. Two kinds of rule exist. A margin rule lists the case when a margin is closer than a threshold. A diagnosis and biomarker rule lists the case when every criterion matches. Enterprise values can be overridden or turned off for one facility. A separate batching cut-off locks a board's case list before its meeting.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. Facility overrides use the Facility Dictionary. Criteria are matched by field label and wording in the signed report, so test a rule on a real report template before relying on it.

    # QA Configuration Center

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance › QA Configuration Center

    Status: Built

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Administration & Compliance 2. Maintenance item: QA Configuration Center

    3. Business purpose and scope. Defines the quality-assurance activities a lab runs. An activity is built on one of two archetypes: Review-with-Outcome (a case is reviewed and graded, for example Frozen vs Final Correlation) or Supervision / Assignment (a provider is supervised over a case count or period, for example FPPE). Standard activities are curated by PathScribe for the lab's jurisdiction; they cannot be switched off or turned into custom ones, and only their sampling, CAPA trigger and similar settings can be configured. Custom activities are the lab's own; the faster route is to duplicate a standard or custom activity, because its review fields come ready-made. Nothing opens a CAPA automatically: a trigger only recommends one to the QA lead, who confirms or dismisses it.

    Standard review activities include: Frozen vs Final Correlation, Cytology-Histology Correlation, Abnormal/Critical Finding Confirmation, GYN Cytology Secondary Screening, Surgical Post-Sign-Out Peer Review, Surgical Biopsy-to-Resection Correlation, Pre-Sign-Out Peer Review, Clinical-Pathologic Correlation and Outside Consult Correlation. The list that shows depends on the jurisdiction.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. The CAPA trigger names a deficiency type from Specimen Deficiencies. Expected case mix uses Subspecialties.

    Setup sequence · Tier 3, step 22

    Configure first
    Specimen Deficiencies, Subspecialties
    This unlocks

    # TAT Configuration (tab)

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab TAT Configuration (opens for people who hold config:tat-targets:manage; the tab is wrapped in a section gate). 2. Maintenance item: TAT Configuration (title on screen: TAT Configuration)

    3. Business purpose and scope. Sets the turnaround time targets per type, urgency, facility, specimen and subspecialty. The most specific matching rule wins when a case is measured. A case falls back to a built-in system default when no custom rule matches. Targets drive the on-time and late marks in Search, the quality dashboards and the Intraoperative board (frozen section warning time).

    # Cytology QC Rules

    Home › Configuration › System › Lab Materials & Workflows › Cytology QC Rules

    Status: Built

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Lab Materials & Workflows 2. Maintenance item: Cytology QC Rules (title on screen: Cytology QC Assignment Rules)

    3. Business purpose and scope. The automated rules that sample, assign and route cytology cases for quality-control peer review. A rule says which cases it covers (criteria), how many of them to select (sampling logic), how urgent the review is (priority tier and SLA) and who may review. Rules are evaluated from the highest Evaluation Priority down. Rules cannot be deleted; they are deactivated. The resulting work is the Cytology QC Queue.

    The demonstration data holds named rules for the US (CLIA high-risk targeted Pap rescreen, 100 percent), the UK (NHS / RCPath rapid rescreen, 20 percent), the EU (ISO 15189 pathologist peer review, 2 percent) and a cytotechnologist negative sign-out random re-screen (10 percent).

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. None are enforced. The performing facility criterion is typed as a list of facility ids (it is not a picklist), so take the ids from the Facility Dictionary. The random-selection rates on Cytology QC Random Selection Rates are separate from these rules.

    # Tier 4: The PathScribe Embedded AI Framework

    Tier 4 covers every setting that decides whether, where and how PathScribe uses artificial intelligence (AI), and the checks that keep a pathologist in control of the result. Read this chapter with one fact in mind: the framework is narrower than its outline. PathScribe calls an external language model for report and dictation help, and it ingests results from vendor image-analysis products. It does not contain a computer-vision engine, a tumour detector, a cell counter, a biomarker scorer, a standalone natural language processing (NLP) engine or a model-weight calibration tool. Each of those is labelled Not built below, with the nearest thing that does exist.

    Production runs on Microsoft SQL Server behind an ASP.NET Core API. Most of the screens in this chapter work on the demonstration data in the browser today, and the status line on each screen says how far its server contract goes.

    # How Tier 4 is set up

    Home › Configuration › AI Behavior

    Complete Tiers 1 to 3 first. Tier 4 reads facilities, physicians, specimen types and code systems from them. Then work through the screens in this order. Each screen's part 4 repeats its own prerequisites.

    1. AI Behavior (tab): choose the AI service and model, set the vendor policy, the confidence threshold and the Orchestrator default.
    2. Validation Studies (tab): the entry point for the evidence that a model works for your data.
    3. Validation Studies: Studies: create, approve and activate a study.
    4. Validation Studies: Reports: close a study and print the report that grades it.
    5. AI Instructions: approve the text that the clinical mismatch check sends to the model.
    6. Clinical Mismatch Rules: set when a mismatch alerts, logs or blocks sign-out.
    7. AI history extraction: turn on the advisory read of historical cases.
    8. Smart Capture: the billing-suggestion prototype switch and its production checklist.

    Validation Studies: Dashboard is a day-to-day page and is not part of setup. A model's facility override needs a published report template and a passing study, so finish Chapter 6 for the templates before you rely on a facility override.

    # AI output governance and the regulatory profile

    Home › Configuration › AI Behavior

    Status: Built in the browser on the demonstration data. The server must repeat the sign-out rule below before production (contract in docs/product/REGULATORY_PROFILE.md).

    PathScribe treats AI output as a draft that a pathologist must vouch for. These rules apply on every install; none of them is a setting on a screen.

    • Regulatory profile. A build setting, VITE_REGULATORY_PROFILE, chooses documentation (the default) or clinical_support (kept for later, not validated). In the documentation profile the clinical screens show no AI confidence percentage (a plain "Check source" prompt or "Strong match" / "Possible match" label appears instead), and a clinical mismatch is a plain low-risk flag that is logged and never holds sign-out. The thresholds and Block rules on Clinical Mismatch Rules are kept for clinical_support. The profile is read when the application starts; changing it needs a new build.
    • AI-drafted narrative must be accepted. Sign-out stops while any AI-drafted narrative section has not been accepted, edited, or kept as the earlier text.
    • Unconfirmed AI values stay out of the signed report. Before the sign-out or Finalize window opens, every optional synoptic or grossing field that still holds an unchanged, unverified AI value is cleared. The AI suggestion stays, so the pathologist can cancel and Confirm. Required fields with an unverified AI value stop the sign-out as before. Values filled by auto-insert or by the Orchestrator button start as unverified.
    • What is written to the audit log (counts and names only, never clinical text): AI_NARRATIVE_ACCEPTED, AI_NARRATIVE_ACCEPTED_EDITED, AI_NARRATIVE_REJECTED, AI_CODE_BOUND, AI_VALUES_AUTOFILLED, AI_VALUES_OMITTED_AT_SIGNOUT. Each AI_CODE_BOUND entry also records the code's wording from the terminology dictionary, the model and provider, the model's own confidence, whether the code was found in the dictionary (or the billing code table), which part of the case it was taken from (and the specimen), and whether the pathologist changed it before binding it.
    • Known limits. The omission and the audit entries are written by the browser; the production API must apply and write them itself. Autopsy and cytology reports carry no AI suggestions today. The wording in this section is a description of behaviour, not a statement that PathScribe meets any regulation.

    # AI infrastructure and model architecture

    Home › Configuration › AI Behavior

    Status: Built for the settings screens. Partial for the server: the production calls are written down, and a few are not yet connected (listed under each screen).

    This section explains how an AI call is made and who decides what it uses. The screen that sets all of it, AI Behavior (tab), follows.

    The AI proxy. The browser never holds an AI key. It calls PathScribe's own /api/ai/... routes and the server adds the key from a secret store such as Azure Key Vault. Routes exist for Anthropic, Google Gemini (generate, stream and model list), OpenAI, Azure OpenAI (/api/ai/azure/chat/completions), a custom endpoint, AWS Bedrock (invoke and invoke-stream), and the UMLS and National Library of Medicine terminology lookups. The server must write an audit entry for each call (without the prompt text) and rate-limit callers. The proxy that the development build uses does not exist in production. Rotating an API key is done by ForMedrixAI support in the server's secret store. No screen sets or shows a key.

    Providers. The screen shows vendor names. Internally each is stored under an id named for the protocol it speaks.

    Shown as Stored id Models offered (first is the default when you pick the provider)
    Anthropic (Claude) structured_messages claude-sonnet-4-6 (recommended), claude-opus-4-8 (highest accuracy), claude-haiku-4-5 (fastest)
    OpenAI (GPT-4) chat_completions gpt-4o (recommended), gpt-4-turbo, gpt-4
    Azure OpenAI chat_completions_managed gpt-4o (Azure), gpt-4-turbo (Azure)
    AWS Bedrock model_gateway anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6-v1:0, anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0, amazon.nova-pro-v1:0
    Google (Gemini) structured_content gemini-1.5-flash (recommended), gemini-1.5-pro
    Self-hosted / Custom endpoint custom custom
    Mock, Demo Mode mock mock-v1

    If the stored provider id is not one of these, PathScribe uses structured_messages. A provider setting of mock or an unknown value still sends the call to the Anthropic route through the proxy (a disclosed behaviour of the proxy, not a demo shortcut). Bedrock needs a server route that signs requests and returns a normalised stream; that route is part of the proxy contract.

    Which setting wins. PathScribe resolves the AI configuration in this order: a personal override (a developer view only; no screen sets it for an administrator), then the organisation's lab setting, then the build defaults VITE_AI_PROVIDER, VITE_AI_MODEL, VITE_AI_PROXY_URL, VITE_AI_GATEWAY_REGION (default us-east-1), VITE_AI_HOSTING_REGION and VITE_AI_MAX_TOKENS (default 1000). The organisation setting is stored under the key pathscribe_ai_org_config.

    Which model each task uses.

    Task Model used Notes
    Report and narrative help (Generate Narrative, Suggest Synoptic Fields, macro suggestions, critical-findings scan, template assignment) The organisation's default model, or the performing facility's own model if one is set in the Facility Dictionary, AI & Performance tab A facility may choose only a model that has a reported study graded PASS for that facility (Validation Studies: Reports). The facility's token limit and request format come with the model.
    Dictation refinement The organisation-wide default model of type Voice Dictation No facility layer. A voice model becomes the default only with a PASS-graded study. Set on the Voice tab (Chapter 4).
    AI synoptic and grossing template assignment As report help The confidence threshold for these two is fixed at 60 in code; there is no setting. Grossing assignment falls back to the standard tissue template.

    Vendor policy. One rule per jurisdiction, and optionally one narrower rule per facility, says which AI services and hosting regions may be used for work in that place. A call must pass the jurisdiction rule and the facility rule. With no rule, every service is allowed. Inside a rule, allowed services can be all or a list, and each allowed service can carry a list of allowed regions; no list means any region. A call whose region is not recorded is refused where regions are limited. A refusal never falls over to another service: the feature carries on without AI and shows "AI is not available for this jurisdiction". The mock provider is always allowed. The server must answer a refused call with 403 and the code AI_VENDOR_NOT_ALLOWED, and audit it as AI_CALL_REFUSED.

    AI audit log. Each AI call writes a record of: case, section, provider, model, status (completed, error, cancelled or refused), token count, time taken, hosting region, jurisdiction, facility and feature. The log holds the latest 2000 entries and is kept in the browser until the server records it. No screen shows it.

    Orchestrator mode. Orchestrator mode writes a report narrative in four fixed steps instead of one request. The engine in src/orchestrator/ is the live code. AI Behavior (tab) sets the organisation default, and a facility can override it. Step wording and order are not editable.

    # Specimen tracking and grossing computer-vision assist

    Home › Configuration › System › Lab Materials & Workflows › Smart Capture

    Status: Not built for computer vision. Two nearby things exist and are described here so no one mistakes them for it.

    PathScribe has no computer-vision engine for specimens. Nothing in the product reads a photograph of a specimen, a cassette or a slide to identify it, count blocks, measure a lesion or track it. The nearest things that exist are these.

    • The grossing imaging vendor dictionary. A list of imaging vendors (for example PAX-it!/PAXcam, PathoZoom and MacroPATH, named in the interface comment) and how to reach each: name, how the link is authenticated (none, signed link, OAuth 2 bearer token or mutual TLS), the https base address, and whether the vendor supports telepathology. It is one category (gross_imaging) of Vendor Integrations in Chapter 4, which documents its fields. It holds addresses only and performs no image analysis. The grossing camera control in the case is plain photo capture; it stores the picture inline, which is flagged as not compliant, and moving it onto this vendor category is deferred.
    • Grossing Hardware (Chapter 2) for scales, cameras and barcode devices.
    • Smart Capture, below. Despite the name it calls no AI model and looks at no image. It is a fixed rule set that suggests billing lines.

    # Smart Capture

    Home › Configuration › System › Lab Materials & Workflows › Smart Capture

    Status: Built (prototype). It works on the demonstration data and has a server contract (SIGNATURES_SMART_CAPTURE_API.md), and the case drawer is labelled "Prototype, not compliance-reviewed".

    3. Business purpose and scope. Smart Capture suggests Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) charge lines for a case from the specimen description words, the block count and the stain counts. The rules are fixed and versioned (sim-rules-1.0): SC-LEVEL (88302 to 88309 by specimen level), SC-SPECIAL (88312), SC-IHC-FIRST and SC-IHC-ADDL (88342 and 88341) and SC-DECAL (88311). It is not AI and not computer vision. The flow is suggest, review (accept or reject each line), approve (a pathologist confirms) and export. In the demonstration the export goes to a simulated engine. This screen switches the prototype on or off and records the production checklist that must be complete before an export to a real interface engine is allowed.

    # NLP and auto-structuring engine

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance › AI history extraction

    Status: Partial. Individual language features exist. A standalone NLP or auto-structuring engine does not, and there is no screen for one.

    What exists today, each of which sends text to the model chosen on AI Behavior (tab) and is subject to the vendor policy:

    • History extraction (AI history extraction): reads historical cases and fills structured fields as advisory information.
    • Suggest Synoptic from Narrative: on the report page, fills synoptic fields from the narrative. Each suggestion carries a confidence from 0 to 100 and a quote from the source text. It works in Orchestrator and Assist modes.
    • Generate Narrative from Synoptic: on the report page, writes the narrative from the synoptic data. Orchestrator mode only.
    • Synoptic template assignment: the model proposes which synoptic template a case needs, with a fixed confidence threshold of 60.
    • Critical-findings scan at sign-out: a negation-aware scan of narrative text only.
    • Dictation refinement (Voice tab, Chapter 4) and macro suggestion (Macros tab, Chapter 4).

    Not built: a general free-text-to-structured pipeline beyond the features above, a screen to configure one, and any trained clinical NLP model of PathScribe's own. The earlier Computational Sidecar was retired on 18 October 2026.

    # AI history extraction

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance › AI history extraction

    Status: Partial. The screen and the rules work on the demonstration data and the server contract is written (HISTORY_AI_EXTRACTION_API.md), but nothing has been tried against a real server. The summary hook for Assist mode is not built.

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Administration & Compliance 2. Maintenance item: AI history extraction

    3. Business purpose and scope. When a pathologist opens a historical case, the model can read its Final Diagnosis and Microscopic text and propose values for the fields of a structured template. The results are labelled "AI-extracted, not verified" and are advisory only: reports, printing, the registry, billing, rules and exports never use them (a test in the code guards this). It makes two model calls per case (choose the template, then fill the fields) and drops any field with confidence below 30 (fixed in code). Results are cached by a hash of the source text, and a failed run is tried again the next time the case is opened. The audit event HISTORY_EXTRACTION_RUN carries no patient text.

    # Digital pathology AI image analysis

    Home › Configuration › System › Lab Materials & Workflows › Vendor Integrations

    Status: Partial. Receiving and showing results from vendor products exists. Tumour detection, cell counting and biomarker scoring performed by PathScribe itself are Not built.

    PathScribe does not analyse images. It records what a vendor's product reports. The nearest thing to an AI analysis module is this chain, which is configured in other chapters:

    • Vendor dictionary (category digital pathology AI in Vendor Integrations, Chapter 4): vendor name, product name, modality (free text), an FDA Cleared checkbox (an administrator's point-in-time record, not a check) and an active switch. It is seeded with Paige Prostate, Ibex Prostate Detect, PathAI AISight Dx, Proscia Concentriq AP-Dx, Hologic Genius Digital Diagnostics (cervical cytology) and BD FocalPoint GS (marked not cleared, as it is a premarket approval and not a 510(k) clearance). Slide viewer vendors (launch address templates) and whole-slide-image scan batches sit beside it.
    • Result record: a status (ordered, completed, failed or timed out), findings (a free-text label, a confidence from 0 to 1 and an optional region), biomarker read-outs as free text (name and value), and a slide triage rank with a review recommendation in the style of BD's quintiles.
    • Ingestion: a vendor result arrives as an inbound interface-engine event. In the demonstration, completing a Cytology Imaging batch places an AI screening order automatically with the first active cervical cytology vendor.
    • Cytology worklist badge and concordance prompt: the pathologist's answer is recorded. A disagreement raises an open deficiency and never starts a corrective action by itself.
    • QA AI discordance tab (Chapter 4): a per-vendor discordance report and a stalled-result report. The stalled-result timeout is set there (whole hours 1 to 720, default 24).

    Not built: a PathScribe-owned tumour detector, cell counter or biomarker scorer, and any control that tunes a vendor's analysis. The real vendor integrations are not closed. The contract is DIGITAL_PATHOLOGY_API.md. Related set-up: Cytology Instrumentation (Chapter 3).

    # Smart quality control and diagnostic anomaly detection rules

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance › Clinical Mismatch Rules

    Status: Built for the rule screens. Demonstration for the server side of AI Instructions. There is no single "anomaly detection" module; the checks below are separate and each is documented where it is configured.

    • Clinical mismatch check (Clinical Mismatch Rules and AI Instructions, this chapter): the model compares the clinical indication and history with the diagnosis, and the rules decide what a result does.
    • Abnormal Trigger Rules (Chapter 3): discrete rules with the severities Abnormal, Critical and Malignant. The seeded rules are Margin Status, Perineural Invasion, Lymph Node Status and Lymphovascular Invasion.
    • Critical-findings narrative scan: the model scans the narrative at sign-out, negation-aware, and sends narrative text only. It has no setting of its own.
    • QA discordance trend policy (Chapter 4), the AI discordance tab (Chapter 4) and Cytology QC rules (Chapter 4).

    Not built: a statistical or machine-learning anomaly detector that watches turnaround times, volumes or results across cases.

    # Clinical Mismatch Rules

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance › Clinical Mismatch Rules

    Status: Built. It works on the demonstration data and has a server contract (CONFIG_SERVICES_API.md, /api/clinical/clinical-mismatch-rule/*).

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Administration & Compliance 2. Maintenance item: Clinical Mismatch Rules

    3. Business purpose and scope. At sign-out the model compares what the clinician told the lab with what the pathologist diagnosed, and returns a kind of mismatch and a confidence from 0 to 100. These rules turn that confidence into an outcome. Below the display threshold the result is dropped. From the display threshold up to the action threshold it is low risk: the pathologist sees an alert and the QA log records it. At or above the action threshold the rule's action applies: Block makes it high risk and holds sign-out until a decision is recorded, Warn alerts, and Log records it. Decisions are recorded as RESOLVED, UNRESOLVED or DEFERRED. The full workflow is in docs/product/CLINICAL_MISMATCH_CHECK.md. One rule per kind of mismatch covers all specimen types, and you can add a rule for one specimen type.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. The check calls the AI service set up on the AI Behavior tab, and the per-specimen-type rules pick from the active specimen types. With no AI service, or one the vendor policy refuses, the check does not run. Skip the Specimen Dictionary and the Add a rule for one specimen type list is empty.

    Configure first
    AI Behavior (tab), Specimen Dictionary

    Action Choice: Block, Warn, Log Required What happens at or above Action at. unexpected malignancy Block, cause of death Block, site or organ Block, expected malignancy absent Log, other Log

Change it: config:clinical-mismatch-rules:manage, which requires view and has no default role, so grant it deliberately. Without manage the screen is view-only.     Known limits. The model can be wrong; the thresholds are the lab's control over how much a pathologist is interrupted. A mismatch at sign-out is advisory unless a rule's action is Block. In the default documentation profile this screen shows only a note that the rules are inactive, because every mismatch is a plain low-risk flag; the rules apply again under the clinical_support profile. The flag shows the words it relied on from the clinical side and the pathology side, checked against the case text; both quotes and whether each was found are saved in the QA record (evidenceClinical, evidenceClinicalFound, evidencePathology, evidencePathologyFound) and shown in the secondary-review queue. A flag made before Batch 685 has no quotes, and a lab whose Clinical-Pathologic Correlation activity type was saved earlier must add the four fields in Quality settings to see them labelled in exports; they hold clinical text from the case, so treat an export like the clinical indication.

    # AI governance, human-in-the-loop thresholds and calibration

    Home › Configuration › Validation Studies

    Status: Built for governance and thresholds. Weight calibration: none exists.

    PathScribe's controls keep a person between the model and the record.

    • Approved instructions. The text the clinical mismatch check sends to the model is versioned, and a second person must approve it (AI Instructions).
    • Evidence. A Validation Study measures how often pathologists accept the model's suggestions unchanged, and a PASS grade is what lets a facility pin a model or a voice model become the default (Validation Studies).
    • Thresholds. Every threshold in the product is listed here.
    Threshold Value Where set
    Confidence Threshold (suggestions) 0 to 100, default 75 AI Behavior tab; per-model override in Model Settings
    Auto-insert at or above the threshold Off by default AI Behavior tab, Advanced
    Clinical mismatch display and action thresholds 0 to 100, display default 60 Clinical Mismatch Rules
    Synoptic and grossing template assignment Fixed 60 Code; no setting
    History extraction field cut-off Fixed 30 Code; no setting
    Study target acceptance rate and maximum mean edit ratio 70% and 30% by default Validation Studies: Studies
    Stalled AI screening result Whole hours 1 to 720, default 24 QA AI discordance tab (Chapter 4)

    Weight calibration and internal-only settings. There is no model weight calibration, fine-tuning or recalibration setting anywhere in PathScribe, and no AI setting is limited to ForMedrixAI staff. A search of the code finds only equipment and cytology calibration, which are unrelated. No capability in the catalogue is marked platform-only for AI. Two related facts are worth knowing. The API key is rotated by ForMedrixAI support in the server's secret store, and there is no screen for it. The model catalogue that the ForMedrixAI store offers is owned by the platform, and there is no staff screen for it either. Because no such setting exists, this chapter has no section marked ForMedrixAI internal only.

    # Validation Studies: Reports

    Home › Configuration › Validation Studies › Reports

    Status: Built.

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab Validation Studies > sub-tab Reports 2. Maintenance item: Reports

    3. Business purpose and scope. Produces the printed report that grades a closed study. The grade is PASS when the acceptance rate is at least the target and the mean edit ratio is at most the maximum; CONDITIONAL PASS when the acceptance rate is at least 85% of the target; otherwise FURTHER REVIEW. Generate & Print Report opens a print window, records the output in the audit trail, moves the study to reported and saves the final grade once. The grade is never recalculated afterwards. Only a reported study graded PASS, with the facility among its participants, lets that facility pin the model as its AI override.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. A report needs a closed study. Skip closing it and the study does not appear in the list.

    # Tier 5: Reporting, Synoptic Forms and Scheduler Configuration

    This chapter covers what a released report looks like, which structured (synoptic) forms pathologists fill in, and how a released report is sent, printed and scheduled. It documents 15 screens in four parts. Three things in the outline are not built, and each one is marked where it comes up: a patient portal delivery channel, automated loading of CAP protocol versions, and a nightly job scheduler that an administrator can configure. The nearest working things are named in each section.

    Setup order for this tier. Do Tier 1 to Tier 4 first (in particular facilities, physicians, roles, and site agents). Then work through this tier in this order. Each screen's own "Setup sequence" box repeats its place in the list.

    1. Approved Fonts: choose which fonts the report editors offer.
    2. Document Style: set the lab's default report text style, page size and margins.
    3. Template Review: decide who may approve and publish synoptic templates.
    4. Part Library: build or copy the reusable headers, bodies and footers.
    5. Report Templates: assemble parts into report templates and publish them.
    6. Routing Rules: choose which template a case uses for a facility, physician or protocol.
    7. Review queue: bring synoptic protocols through draft, review and approval.
    8. Active protocols: check and maintain the published synoptic protocols.
    9. Print Destination Routing Rules: decide which printer a released report goes to.
    10. Delivery Configuration Rules: decide how each released report is sent (result message, print, e-fax, file drop).
    11. Delivery Schedules: decide when things go out.

    Screens that are not part of setup and so have no step number: the two tab pages (Report Templates tab and Synoptic Library tab), All protocols and My exports.

    Delivery channels at a glance. Each is stated again, with its limits, in Part 3.

    Channel Status What exists
    Print queue Built Delivery rules send a print job; print routing rules pick the printer; the Print Queue screen manages jobs.
    Result message to the interface engine (electronic) Built The default channel.
    E-fax Built Sent to the interface server, which hands the PDF to an e-mail-to-fax gateway.
    File drop Built Sent to the interface server, which writes the file to a folder or SFTP target set up on that server.
    Secure e-mail Demonstration A person sends a case-linked message from a window; mail goes to the Simulated mail outbox. It is not a delivery rule channel.
    Patient or provider portal Not built No portal channel exists.

    Where the batch and nightly job tools are. Batch printing and the nightly job scheduler are not one screen. Part 4 lists the screens that exist and where each is documented.

    # Report Template Designer and Branding Setup

    Home › Configuration › Report Templates

    A report is built from three kinds of part (header, body, footer). A template places parts into five slots (page 1 header, pages 2 and later header, body, pages 2 and later footer, page 1 footer). Routing rules decide which template a case gets. The lab's default fonts, page size and margins sit underneath all of it.

    How a template is chosen for a case. The router tries these in order and stops at the first match: a preliminary-report gate first; then a facility override (Pass 0); then, for an affiliate facility with no rule of its own, its enterprise parent's override (Pass 0a); then a physician preference (Pass 0b); then a synoptic protocol match, where admin-defined rules are checked before the built-in table (Pass 1); then the subspecialty fallback (Pass 2); then the gold-standard fallback (Pass 3). Within one rule type, a rule for one performing lab beats a Global rule for the same facility or physician.

    Text style layers. The text style of a report comes from three layers; the most specific wins: the lab default (Document Style) is overridden by a template's own Style panel, which is overridden by a component's label formatting in the inspector.

    Branding. The report header takes its logo, laboratory director name and accreditation number from the Department, falling back to the Facility, then the enterprise. Those fields are set on other screens; this chapter does not repeat them: - Department branding: Department Dictionary (Laboratory Director Name, accreditation number, Header Logo URL). - Facility branding and reporting options: Facility Configuration and Facility Dictionary.

    PathScribe stores only the address of a hosted logo image, never the image. A header part with Show institution logo switched on uses it.

    # Part Library

    Home › Configuration › Report Templates › Part Library

    Status: Built

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab Report Templates > sub-tab Part Library 2. Maintenance item: Report parts (header, body, footer)

    3. Business purpose and scope. A part is one reusable block of a report: a header (institution branding, accession number, patient demographics), a body part (diagnosis, gross description, microscopic, synoptic data) or a footer (page numbers, confidentiality notice, patient identity line). Parts are built once here and placed into any number of templates. A part can be Global (offered to every performing lab) or belong to one performing lab. The library ships with built-in parts, shown with a Built-in badge. Built-in parts cannot be edited or archived; duplicate one to change it.

    # CAP Synoptic Reporting Module Setup

    Home › Configuration › Synoptic Library

    The Synoptic Library holds the structured checklists (protocols) pathologists fill in for cancer and other reporting. It is separate from report templates: a protocol defines the questions and their coding, a report template defines how a report looks. The Routing Rules screen links the two.

    What is actually in the library today (read this first). On the demonstration data the registry holds 36 protocols: 32 Published, 3 In Review and 1 Draft. By source, 23 are Custom and 13 are PathScribe. None is a licensed CAP or RCPath checklist. The CAP, RCPath and ICCR names exist only as source labels on the Upload window and as the names of governing bodies. The 19 entries named "Generic Template" (breast, lung, prostate, colon, kidney, Wilms, melanoma and others) are placeholders at version 0.1.0-generic. The rest are two generic synoptic test forms, PathScribe forms such as Mohs and neck dissection, medical liver, placenta and renal-transplant forms, autopsy gross examination, the three gold-standard grossing routes, and five cytology reporting systems (Bethesda thyroid, Milan salivary, Paris urinary, Papanicolaou pancreaticobiliary, lymph node FNA). A hospital that needs a CAP protocol must obtain it under CAP's own licence and bring it in by the routes below.

    How a protocol version gets in, and out.

    Step Status What exists
    Import a PathScribe protocol file (JSON) Built Upload Protocol reads the file, checks it, and saves it as a draft. It then goes through review like any other draft.
    Check a CAP electronic checklist (eCC, SDC XML) or an Excel workbook Partial The file's format is checked and the number of sections and questions shown. It cannot be imported yet, and the content is not verified against CAP or RCPath.
    Build a protocol in the editor Built Build / Customise starts from scratch or from a copy of an existing protocol.
    Load a new version of an existing protocol Built New Version opens the editor with the next version number. Publishing it archives the version it came from.
    Automatic nightly sync of CAP, RCPath or ICCR updates Not built The Governing Bodies screen has an Auto-sync switch per body, and the Upload window and notification texts mention a nightly sync, but no sync job exists in this build and none is in the server job list. The notification contract (TEMPLATE_NOTIFICATIONS_API.md) describes the messages a future sync job would send. Until then, load updates by hand.
    Retire a protocol Built Archive removes it from new reports; reports already written keep their content. Restore as draft brings it back for review and republishing.

    Lifecycle. Draft, In Review, Needs Changes, Approved, Published, Archived. Action names follow the source: for CAP the approval step is Accept and the publish step Release; for RCPath they are Ratify and Publish; for Custom, PathScribe and ICCR they are Approve and Publish. Governance (self-approval, number of reviewers, the 80% SNOMED rule) is set in Template Review.

    # Scheduled Report Engine and Auto-Distribution Rules

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance

    Three settings decide what happens to a report after sign-out: Delivery Configuration Rules pick the channels, Print Destination Routing Rules pick the printer for the print channel, and Delivery Schedules pick the time. A fourth screen, My exports, lists files a person asked for.

    Channel status, one by one.

    Channel Status What exists today
    Fax Built A delivery rule can set a channel to E-fax with a fax number (7 to 15 digits, optional leading +). PathScribe sends the signed PDF and its details to the interface server as a REPORT_DELIVERY message; the server hands it to an e-mail-to-fax gateway. The gateway is set up on the server, not in PathScribe. If the server has no fax channel it answers 503 and the delivery fails with that reason. Contract: REPORT_DELIVERY_API.md; development receiver: functions/report_delivery.py. Maximum PDF size 20 MB.
    Portal Not built There is no portal channel in the delivery rules. The Facility record has a Delivery Method choice (Email, Fax, Portal, HL7) that is stored but nothing reads it when a report is sent.
    Secure e-mail Demonstration Not a delivery rule channel. A person starts a case-linked secure message from a window; it is delivered to the Simulated mail outbox and nothing leaves the building. A real mail channel is not connected.
    Print queue Built The Print channel creates a print job. The printer comes from the print routing rules, else the facility's own default destination. Jobs are managed on the Print Queue screen (see Part 4).
    Electronic (result message) Built The result message to the interface engine. It is the default when no rule matches.
    File drop Built The server writes the PDF to a folder or SFTP target. The rule names the target; the server holds its address and sign-in details.

    # Delivery Configuration Rules

    3. Business purpose and scope. Decides how each released report is sent: through the result message, printed, faxed, dropped to a file target, or held for manual retrieval. A rule matches on provider, ordering facility, patient location (point of care) and report type. The rule matching the most fields wins. When nothing matches, the report goes Electronic Only.     # Delivery Schedules

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance › Delivery Schedules

    Status: Partial

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Administration & Compliance 2. Maintenance item: Delivery Schedules

    3. Business purpose and scope. Sets when things go out, per feed, for the whole enterprise, with an optional override for a performing facility. Registries get a schedule each.     # Tier 6: Interface Engine and External System Integrations

    This chapter covers how PathScribe exchanges messages with other systems: the hospital's electronic health record (EHR), a laboratory information system (LIS), reference laboratories, billing systems, registries and reporting tools. It also covers the screens an administrator uses to watch those exchanges and to deal with the ones that fail.

    Read the status of each part before you plan a project around it. Much of this tier is a contract that is written and a browser side that is built, while the server and the interface engine on the other end are not yet connected. Where something is not built, the section says Not built or Planned and names the nearest thing that does exist.

    The rule of this chapter. PathScribe decides what is sent and when. The interface engine decides how: the HL7 text, the connection, the retries on the wire and the vendor's own wording. PathScribe never translates a vendor's field names or codes, and it does not claim to be a certified connector for any EHR.

    # The setup order for Tier 6

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations

    Tier 6 is mostly optional. A laboratory that runs PathScribe on its own, with no LIS, no registry feed and no reporting tool, can skip all of it. Do the steps below only for the integrations you use, in this order. Each step names the screens that must be configured first (Tiers 1 to 5), and the same information appears in the "Setup sequence" box on each screen.

    1. Specimen Code Map: map each sending facility's own specimen codes to your Specimen Dictionary, so inbound orders resolve. Needs the Facility Dictionary and the Specimen Dictionary.
    2. Interface Dictionary (ForMedrixAI staff only): describe a vendor's own fields. Customers do not do this step; it is listed so the numbering is complete.
    3. Assist LIS Ingestion: for a laboratory whose LIS owns the case and PathScribe assists with AI drafts. Needs AI Behavior and the Synoptic Library.
    4. Reporting feed (Power BI): let a reporting tool read PathScribe data. Needs the performing-lab facilities in the Facility Dictionary.
    5. Migration Field Mappings: map a legacy system's field names, before any historical import.
    6. Historical Data Migration Jobs: import a legacy file and check the job. Needs step 5.

    The monitoring screens (System Logs: interfaces, Interface Engines, Outbound Interface DLQ, Outbound Dispatches and the Outbound Queue) and the test tools (Outbound Interface Message Preview, Simulated mail outbox, Mock Interface Engine and Mock EMR) are not setup steps. Each says Reference, not part of setup and lists what must exist for it to show data.

    # How the interface engine fits

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations

    Status: Partial

    # The term "PathScribe Interface Engine"

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations

    The outline for this guide calls the interface layer the PathScribe Interface Engine (PIE). That name does not appear in the product, its screens or its design documents, and this guide does not invent a product name. What the product has is two things that together do the work the outline describes:

    • The PathScribe side. Services in the application decide what to send and when, build the JSON message, queue it, record the outcome and let an administrator resend, hold or release it. Everything in this chapter that you can click is on this side.
    • The interface engine. The design uses BridgeLink, an open-source fork of Mirth Connect, as the engine. It turns PathScribe's JSON into HL7 (or another format), holds its own message store, sends to the receiving system, and receives replies. BridgeLink is the working name in the design documents (INTERFACE_ENGINE_EDGE.md). Its channel templates are Planned, not built.

    # Where the engine runs

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations

    The engine is one container image used in two places, chosen per hospital (decision D6). ForMedrixAI can host it in the tenant's region, or it can be installed on a virtual machine inside the hospital. The Interface Engines screen shows which of the two each engine is (Hosted or On site). The image, its channel templates and its health endpoints are Planned, with the server team.

    HL7 messages do not travel on the SQL Server message bus (decision D1). The API server hands a message to the engine as a job of kind interface.dispatch, and the engine keeps HL7 in its own message store.

    # What runs today and what is Planned

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations
    Piece Status What it means for you
    Outbound messages, JSON envelope Built (browser side) The browser posts {queueEntryId, transactionType, dispatchedAt, payload} to the address in the build setting VITE_INTERFACE_RECEIVER_ENDPOINT. In a production build the address must be https; a missing or plain-HTTP address is refused before anything is sent. The wait is 15 seconds.
    What counts as sent Built (browser side) Any 2xx answer marks the message sent. There is no HL7 acknowledgement (ACK) yet. A timeout, an unreachable engine and a rejection are three different errors on the screens.
    Demonstration build Demonstration With no engine address set, a simulated engine receives every message and keeps it in a list. See Mock Interface Engine.
    Inbound events from instruments Built (browser side) Four webhooks exist for the Cassette Engine: block exception, cassette dispatch outcome, material location and engraver status. They use a shared secret in the X-API-Key header, with an optional HMAC signature.
    Inbound HL7 messages Not built The ADT and patient-management processors exist and are tested, but nothing receives a live HL7 message and calls them.
    Server endpoints for the engine (POST /api/interface/inbound, POST /api/interface/outbound-acks, POST /api/interface/heartbeat, GET /api/interface/engines) Planned Written as a contract (phase 2e). They add hand-over, acknowledgement-settled outcomes, retry windows, dead letters and engine status.
    Per-tenant engine credentials Planned OAuth2 client credentials or mutual TLS per tenant engine. See FHIR R4 and OAuth2.

    Planned retry windows. The contract says inbound messages wait 10 seconds, 30 seconds, 1 minute, 5 minutes, then 15 minutes, with a dead letter after 24 hours. Outbound messages are resent at 1, 5, 15 and 60 minutes, then hourly, for 24 hours. Registry submissions are kept for 72 hours. An acknowledgement of AA is sent; CA is sent or awaiting the application acknowledgement; AR and CE are retried within the window; AE and CR fail at once. A dead-lettered result holds later messages for the same case. None of this runs yet. Today a failed send waits for an administrator to resend it.

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations

    The Facility Editor (Tier 1, Facility Dictionary) has a LIS Integration tab. It stores an engine address, HL7 version, authentication type (none, basic, OAuth2 or API key), a flag that says whether a credential has been provisioned, whether the LIS owns case statuses, whether PathScribe allows post-final actions, and the routing identifiers for the sending and receiving facility and an outbound channel override. These settings are saved with the facility. No send path reads them today. A message goes to the one deployment-level address above. The credential is never stored: only a Yes/No flag is.
