    # Message types

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations

    There is no screen that switches message types on or off. The types below are fixed by the product. This part lists only what the code supports. Anything not listed is not supported.

    Outbound. PathScribe queues these transaction types. The engine builds the HL7 for all of them except the three marked "PathScribe builds HL7".

    Transaction type What it carries HL7 form
    A08 Patient demographic update Engine builds ADT^A08. Sex is sent as M, F, U or A for indeterminate in PID-8 (the code A is an assumption pending confirmation with the receiving systems). For UK sites the NHS code is M to 1, F to 2, I to 9, U to X.
    A40 Patient merge Engine builds ADT^A40
    A47 Patient identifier change Engine builds ADT^A47
    ORU_R01 Final, amended or corrected pathology result Engine builds ORU^R01. For US electronic pathology (Tier 7), PathScribe builds an ORU^R01 v2.5.1 itself.
    LIS_SYNC Case data and an Assist case's synoptic result, for the LIS Engine builds it
    ORDER_CREATED A new order Engine builds it
    ACCESSION_EVENT An order accessioned, or an accession deficiency Engine builds it
    REGISTRY_REPORT, CANCER_REGISTRY_REPORT Registry submissions (Tier 7) Engine builds it. Acknowledgements come back.
    REPORT_DELIVERY A signed report PDF for e-fax or file drop Engine or delivery service
    PRINT_JOB A report PDF for the engine to print Engine
    REFERRAL_MANIFEST A referral batch's manifest for a reference lab Engine builds it. Results come back.
    MOLECULAR_ORDER A molecular assay order or an instrument order Engine builds it
    WSI_SCAN_MANIFEST The slides loaded in a whole-slide scan batch Engine builds it. Slide scan status comes back.
    BLOCK_ORDER One block's stain orders for an embedding or staining instrument PathScribe builds HL7: ORM^O01
    SLIDE_ORDER, SPECIMEN_LABEL A slide order; a specimen container label Engine builds it
    MATERIAL_SCAN_EVENT A barcode scan of a cassette or slide Engine builds it
    CHARGE_DFT A charge for the billing system PathScribe builds HL7: DFT^P03
    CHARGE_JSON A charge as a JSON billing webhook JSON, no HL7
    FINANCIAL_CLASS Financial-class payload for a billing engine A preview payload until the formats exist
    CRITICAL_ALERT Post-launch critical alert channels Not wired. Nothing produces it today.

    The "ORM" in the outline is therefore the ORM^O01 that PathScribe builds for block orders to an instrument. PathScribe itself builds no ORM for an EHR or a LIS. The engine decides what HL7 an order-created message becomes, and there is no screen to add a message type.

    Inbound. These processors exist in the application. None is connected to a live listener except the instrument webhooks above. You can run a pasted message through them with the Mock Interface Engine in the demonstration build.

    Family Messages Status
    Admit, discharge and transfer (adtParser.ts) A01, A03, A04, A08, A02, A09, A10, A05, A06, A07, A11, A12, A13, A31 Processor built; no listener
    Patient management (patientManagementParser.ts) A40 merge, A24 link, A47 identifier change, A43 move Processor built; no listener. A message that cannot be matched is queued as an interface exception, never guessed.
    Visit changes (processVisitMessage.ts) A45, A50, A34 Processor built; no listener
    LIS order status (the Assist adapter) ORU^R01, ORM^O01, OML^O21 Status only. You can paste one into Assist LIS Ingestion.
    JSON events HPV result, block exception, material location, referral result, molecular run results, whole-slide scan status Processors built; the instrument webhooks are the only live route

    Inbound orders are not parsed from HL7. The order-intake service takes a structured order, not an ORM message, so a live HL7 order from an EHR is not accepted today. The Specimen Code Map resolves an order's codes once an order reaches the service.

    Vendor adapters. Adapters for Cerebro and Vantage are deliberately stubs that do nothing.

    # Specimen Code Map

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations › Order Types & Inbound Rules

    Status: Built

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Integrations 2. Maintenance item: Order Types & Inbound Rules (the menu name). The title on the screen is Specimen Code Map.

    3. Business purpose and scope. A sending system uses its own codes for specimens, and the same code can mean different things at different sending systems. This screen maps each sending facility's code to one Specimen Dictionary entry. Every incoming order is checked against this table. When no entry matches, PathScribe does not block the order. It creates an entry marked Auto-learned: pending review, creates a pending Specimen Dictionary entry so the order can flow, and queues an interface exception of type unmapped_order_code for a person to resolve. You review the auto-learned entries here, or add a real entry ahead of time so a known code never has to be learned.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. The Facility list is the Facility Dictionary and the Resolves to list is the Specimen Dictionary, so both are set up first. Skip them and the lists are empty, and a mapping cannot be saved because facility, external code and specimen type are all required.

    # Assist LIS Ingestion

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations › Assist LIS Ingestion

    Status: Partial

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Integrations 2. Maintenance item: Assist LIS Ingestion

    3. Business purpose and scope. In Assist mode the external LIS owns the case. Its updates reach PathScribe three ways, by polling, by an HL7 v2 message or by a JSON webhook, and all three go through one staging queue. When the LIS reports Gross Complete, the AI picks the synoptic templates and drafts the fields it can from the gross text. When the LIS reports Microscopic/Diagnosis Complete, it drafts the rest from the diagnosis. This screen holds the settings, a test box for pasted messages, the staging queue and the run log.

    What is built and what is not. Built: the settings, the status mapping, the test box, the staging queue with its retries, the run log and the AI drafting rules. Simulated in the demonstration: the schedule (the app polls at the saved interval while it is open and polling is on, and the screen shows a Simulated schedule note with the last and next run) and the LIS that Poll now asks. Not built: a live listener for HL7 or webhook messages, and a field for the address of the LIS to poll. The screen has no such field.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. The AI step uses the AI Behavior switches and the synoptic templates. If AI turned off in AI Behavior applies, an update changes the case text only and no draft is made. Only a case in Assist mode is processed; a case that is not Assist mode is skipped with the result Not an Assist case.

    Load example Button Not applicable Fills the box with a sample for the chosen format. Not applicable

    Send to staging queue Button Not applicable Shows "Staged: n, Handled now: n" or the reason. Not applicable

    What the adapters read. An HL7 message must be an ORU^R01, ORM^O01 or OML^O21; any other type is refused. One update is made per OBR segment. The accession is OBR-3, else OBR-2, else ORC-3. The status is ORC-5, else OBR-25. The time is OBR-22, else MSH-7, and a time with no offset is read as UTC, so ask the LIS to send an offset. The text comes from OBX-5 by the LOINC code in OBX-3: 22634-0 gross, 22635-7 microscopic and 22637-3 final diagnosis. A JSON body is one object or a list, with accession, status and updatedAt (ISO 8601) required, and grossText, microscopicText, diagnosisText, placerOrderNumber and fillerOrderNumber optional. The order numbers are echoed on the synoptic result.

    Staging queue.

    Retry failed Button Not applicable Retries every failed entry that has had fewer than 5 attempts. Disabled when none failed. Not applicable
    Received, Source, Accession, LIS status, State, Result, Attempts Read-only columns Not applicable Source is Poll, HL7 v2 message or JSON webhook. State is Waiting, Failed or Handled. Result is the outcome or the error. The accession is tagged as patient data for redaction. The list shows the newest 25 rows. An entry stops being retried after 5 attempts. The newest 200 handled events are kept. Not applicable

A result is one of: AI draft prepared; No change since the last draft; Case not in PathScribe; Already signed out; Failed (will retry); Status not mapped; Not an Assist case; Text updated, AI turned off in AI Behavior; Text updated, draft already completed. Details give new drafts, fields suggested and template changes to review. Not applicable

    Known limits. The poll source and the schedule are simulated in the demonstration build, and no listener receives an HL7 or webhook message from a real LIS. The HL7 adapter reads the status from ORC-5, then OBR-25, and the source describes this as a per-site setting, but the screen has no control for it. A signed-out case is never changed. A late or amended gross after the full draft only updates the text.

    # [FORMEDRIXAI INTERNAL ONLY] Interface Dictionary

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations › Interface Dictionary

    🔒 ForMedrixAI Internal Restricted Setting Scope: Internal Service & Deployment Personnel Only. Explanation: A vendor profile decides which fields of a vendor's own HL7, JSON or FHIR message are copied onto a case as extension fields. A profile that is wrong, or changed without a test, would put the wrong value on a case or drop a required one, and the case record is a medical record. Only ForMedrixAI staff build and publish profiles, so each one is tested against a real sample and versioned. The three capabilities that guard it are platform-only, held by the Superadmin role and not assignable by a hospital. The section is not visible to anyone without them.

    Status: Partial

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Integrations 2. Maintenance item: Interface Dictionary

    3. Business purpose and scope. The Interface Dictionary holds vendor profiles. A profile says, for one vendor or device and one message type, where each of the vendor's fields is in the message and which extension field (ext.name) on the case it becomes, with an optional conversion, a default, a code translation and a required flag. A profile goes through a fixed life: draft, test, publish, and later roll back or switch off. The same mapping engine is meant to read live messages, so a profile can add vendor fields without a code release.

    Built and not built. Built: creating profiles, editing mappings, the test with a sample message, publish, roll back, switch off and the scope guard. Simulated: the Apply to a case panel, which applies a pasted message to a case so the Vendor fields panel can be seen. A banner says "Nothing is received from a vendor in this build." No vendor profiles are seeded, so the list starts empty. A profile can only fill an extension field. Anything else needs a code release (see the scope table below).

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. None in this guide. A vendor's sample message is needed to test.

    # FHIR R4 endpoint and OAuth2 client credentials

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations

    Status: Not built

    PathScribe has no FHIR R4 endpoint. It does not publish a FHIR server, does not accept a FHIR resource from another system, and has no screen to configure a FHIR base address, a client id, a client secret or a token address. There is no OAuth2 client credentials setup screen either. Do not plan a go-live that depends on either.

    What exists nearest to it, so you know what a question might be about:

    What What it is Status
    Case service for a FHIR source (FHIRCaseService.ts) Scaffolding for reading cases from a FHIR server. The base address is a placeholder and the function that gets an access token throws. It is not wired to any screen or setting. Not built
    FHIR as a message format in the Interface Dictionary A vendor profile can be written for a FHIR resource such as Observation, and the test reads a pasted sample. Nothing receives a FHIR message from a vendor. Partial, ForMedrixAI only
    Authentication type in the Facility Editor The LIS Integration tab lets you choose OAuth2 as an authentication type for a facility's engine connection. It is a stored choice. No code reads it. Stored only
    OAuth2 client credentials, or mutual TLS, for each tenant's engine The contract for how the engine proves itself to the PathScribe API (INTERFACE_ENGINE_EDGE.md). Planned
    Staff sign-in by OpenID Connect (OIDC) Single sign-on for people, not for system-to-system messages. Covered in Tier 1. Built (browser side)
    Tokens for the Reporting feed (Power BI) Bearer tokens that PathScribe issues, shows once and keeps only as a fingerprint. They are not OAuth2. Partial

    The Mock EMR page contains the note "Production uses FHIR R4 API to sync with LIS". Nothing in the code backs that sentence. Treat it as a design intention.

    # EHR integration: Epic, Cerner, MEDITECH and AthenaHealth

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations

    Status: Not built

    PathScribe has no connector for any EHR, certified or not. It is not listed in any vendor's marketplace and has not passed any vendor's validation by this guide's evidence. Whatever an EHR sends or receives goes through the interface engine, which the hospital's interface team configures, and PathScribe sees only the messages in Message types. Do not describe PathScribe to a customer as "Epic certified", "Cerner certified" or the like.

    EHR What exists in PathScribe What does not exist
    Epic An identifier-format preset named Epic Beaker (accession number and a 2D slide barcode pattern). Set on the Identifier Formats tab of the Facility Editor, Tier 1. A connector, an Epic-specific message profile, a certification, a FHIR app registration.
    Cerner An identifier-format preset named Cerner PathNet. The same.
    MEDITECH An identifier-format preset named MEDITECH. The same.
    AthenaHealth Nothing. The name does not appear in the code, the screens or the design documents. Everything.

    The same preset list also holds Generic, CoPath, Sunquest and Custom. A preset only decides which accession and barcode patterns the scan box recognises. It does not exchange a message with anything.

    What an EHR integration looks like today. An EHR can reach PathScribe only through the engine, as the outbound messages in Message types (results, patient updates, order events, accession events) and as inbound processors that are not yet connected to a live listener. The Interface Dictionary has no seeded vendor profile for any EHR. The Specimen Code Map maps an EHR's specimen codes once an order reaches the order-intake service. The EHR keeps authority over patient identity: an A40, A24, A47 or A43 message that cannot be matched is queued as an interface exception for a person, never guessed. See System Logs: interfaces.

    # Reference laboratory interfaces

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations

    Status: Partial

    A reference laboratory is a facility you send specimens to for outsourced testing, for example molecular or send-out immunohistochemistry. PathScribe supports the send-out with a manifest and the receive-back with a result message. The outbound side is built; the inbound side has a processor but no endpoint.

    There is no screen called "reference lab interface". The setup is split across screens you already have:

    1. Make the lab a facility. In the Facility Dictionary, add the laboratory and give it the role Reference Lab (Outbound Referral Destination). That role makes it selectable as the destination of a referral batch. Only an active facility with the role is offered.
    2. Link it to the tests it performs. In the Diagnostic Catalog, a Molecular test lists the reference labs approved to perform it and which one is the default. The default must be one of the approved labs. The link is kept only for the Molecular category, and an add-on order for that test fills in the default and offers only the approved labs.
    3. Send. Referral batches are made in Batch Management with the processing node External Referral and a destination facility. When the batch completes reconciliation, PathScribe queues a REFERRAL_MANIFEST message and creates the tracking record automatically. A failure here never blocks the batch's own completion. The manifest carries the batch id, the master barcode, the destination facility, the test requested, the priority (STAT or Routine), the items (display id, material type, case accession and specimen label) and any send-out molecular orders. PathScribe decides what and when; the engine decides the transport.
    4. Watch the send. The message appears in the Outbound Queue under the feed Referrals, and in the Outbound Interface DLQ under the queue Referral Manifest, where a failed one is resent.
    5. Receive back. A result message (ReferralResultEventPayload) carries the batch id and either a discrete result (text) or a pdf_attachment (a link to a PDF), never both, and optionally the results for each send-out molecular order. The processor checks the shape, finds the batch, records the result and marks the batch result_received, then applies coded results to the molecular orders. The status of a batch moves only forward: dispatched, in transit, delivered, result received. A person can set in transit and delivered by hand; result received is set only when a result arrives.

    What is not built. No endpoint receives a result message, so no result arrives from a reference lab on its own. The processor remembers the message ids it has handled only in memory, so a restart forgets them. It returns one of four answers: applied, already applied, tracking not found, or invalid payload. There is no test sample for a referral result in the Mock Interface Engine. A reference lab's own wording (its test names and result codes) is not translated by PathScribe; the engine owns that.

    # Interface monitoring, error queues and reprocessing

    Home › Quality & Compliance

    Status: Built (browser side)

    Everything an administrator needs to see what failed, and to resend, hold or release it, is on the screens in this part. They work today against the demonstration data and against the services for the API server. What the engine adds when it is connected (a heartbeat, acknowledgement-settled outcomes and automatic retry windows) is Planned. See What runs today and what is Planned.

    # Reprocessing rules at a glance

    Home › Quality & Compliance

    A failed message is never discarded, and nothing is resent without a person pressing a button today. The rules below are what the code enforces.

    Situation Where it appears What you can do Capability
    An inbound patient message could not be matched (A40, A24, A47, A43) System Logs: interfaces, Interface Exceptions Review it, bind the patients by hand or move cases, or dismiss it. The message is never guessed. None dedicated. See the known limits there.
    An inbound order code has no Specimen Dictionary match Interface Exceptions, type unmapped_order_code Map & Link creates the Specimen Code Map entry, or dismiss. config:crosswalk:manage for the entry
    An outbound message failed to send Outbound Interface DLQ, and the Outbound Queue as Failed Retry Dispatch or Dispatch Now sends it to the engine again. interface:outbound:resend
    A message should not go yet Outbound Queue, Waiting or Failed Hold it with a reason, then Release it. A held message is not sent by any other action: retry says "Held on the Outbound Queue screen: release it there first." interface:outbound:hold, interface:outbound:release
    A message failed past its automatic retries Outbound Queue, Dead-lettered Retry, or Retract charge for a billing item. interface:outbound:resend, interface:outbound:retract
    A registry rejected a submission Outbound Queue, Rejected Retry (resubmit) with a reason, or Mark not reportable with a reason. interface:outbound:resend, interface:outbound:mark-not-reportable
    A charge should leave early or be cancelled Outbound Queue, billing items Release now or Retract charge. interface:outbound:override-release, interface:outbound:retract
    A report print, fax or file drop failed after its retries Delivery exceptions, at the top of the Outbound Interface DLQ Resend from its own queue (the Print Queue, or Report Delivery). It leaves the list when it goes through. interface:outbound:resend for report delivery
    A queued charge failed The Outbound DLQ sub-tab of System Logs, Financial (Tier 7) See System Logs: financial. See that screen

    The built-in roles. Admin holds all of the interface:outbound:* capabilities, interface:engine-status:view and jobs:server-job:view. Lab Director holds none of them and does not have the Outbound Queue screen. QA Reviewer opens the audit log screen and the exports only. Superadmin holds every capability except config:ai-prompt:approve, which is withheld for separation of duties (the Lab Director approves AI instructions; ForMedrixAI support never does). There is no built-in Interface Analyst role: a hospital creates one and grants it the capabilities it wants (the seed file says so).

    What a resend does. A resend builds the message again from the record and posts it. If the record it refers to no longer exists, nothing is sent and the screen says "Not sent: the message couldn't be built". A result with no report PDF yet is held, not sent, and goes with the PDF on a later retry. Every action that changes a message is recorded in the audit log, one entry per message, and the audit text never carries a patient name. The wire-level retry (the engine retrying a connection) is the engine's, not PathScribe's.

    # Interface Engines

    3. Business purpose and scope. One list of each hospital's interface engine, saying whether its listeners are up, what is waiting and what failed. It refreshes every minute and has a Refresh button. It is read only: channels are started and stopped on the engine itself, and failed outbound messages are resent from the Outbound Interface DLQ (the Open Outbound button goes there).

The data comes from the engine's heartbeat, which the engine posts every 60 seconds to an endpoint that is Planned (POST /api/interface/heartbeat; the list is GET /api/interface/engines). Until then the demonstration shows four sample engines, one for each status, with a Simulated badge, and says "There is no interface engine in the demo." With no engine registered, the list says "No interface engine has been registered yet."

    3. Business purpose and scope. A dead-letter queue (DLQ) is the list of messages that could not be sent. This screen shows failed and waiting outbound interface messages for one queue at a time and lets you send them again. Dispatch Now and Retry send the message to the interface engine. The Simulate buttons are a testing aid and never send. A failed charge is in the separate financial DLQ (System Logs: financial). The delivery exceptions panel (below) sits at the top.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. Nothing is configured here. A message appears after an outbound send fails. If VITE_INTERFACE_RECEIVER_ENDPOINT is unset the demonstration engine accepts or rejects according to its response mode (see Mock Interface Engine).

    # Outbound Queue

    Home › Quality & Compliance › Outbound Queue

    Status: Built

    1. Navigation: Home > Quality & Compliance > Outbound Queue, at /outbound-queue. 2. Maintenance item: Outbound Queue

    3. Business purpose and scope. Every outbound message in one place: hold, release or retry it, and fix what a registry rejected. It brings together ten feeds (Results, Patient ADT, Accession, LIS sync, Billing, Report delivery, Cytology results, Referrals, Molecular orders, Registry) and shows each message's destination (Interface engine, Billing system, LIS partner, Delivery service or Registry), the transport the engine uses (REST + mTLS, SFTP, Portal upload, PHIN-MS, Direct TCP or HTTPS API, which are shown as part of the destination label only) and its state. PathScribe decides what is released and when; the engine does the transport.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. The queue reads when a message goes, and its reporting deadline, from the Delivery Schedules: the performing facility's own schedule, else the enterprise's, else the feed's default. Without a schedule a message follows the feed's default. Billing items also follow the billing release settings, and registry items the registry settings, both in Tier 7.

Each of the five besides resend needs the screen capability. Admin holds all of them and the screen by default. Lab Director and QA Reviewer do not have the screen. Hold and release are checked once for a bulk selection.

    Known limits. The queue holds the messages the PathScribe side knows about. Whether a message reached its receiver depends on the engine's acknowledgement, which is Planned: today any 2xx answer counts as sent. Acknowledged appears only for feeds that carry an acknowledgement (registry). The transport named in the destination is a label, because the engine owns the transport.

    # Reporting feed (Power BI)

    Home › Configuration › System › Integrations › Reporting feed (Power BI)

    Status: Partial

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Integrations 2. Maintenance item: Reporting feed (Power BI)

    3. Business purpose and scope. Lets Power BI, Excel, Tableau or a script read PathScribe data through a reporting API on the API server. They never connect to the database. You choose what the feed offers (datasets and performing-lab facilities), issue one token for each tool, and keep identifying data out unless a named person has approved it. By default a token is de-identified: names, record numbers, birth dates and free text are removed, dates are reduced to the month, and ages of 90 and over show as 90+.

    What is built and what is not. Built: the settings, the approval record, token creation, replacement and revocation, the field catalogue and the pull test. A token is shown once; PathScribe keeps only a fingerprint and cannot show it again. Not connected: the feed itself. The reading call, GET /api/bi/v1/{dataset} with Authorization: Bearer psbi_..., is a written contract and the server work item PS-787. In the demonstration build the settings and tokens are kept in the browser, and Test a pull only simulates how the server would answer (it returns no rows). A banner says so.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. A token can only be limited to facilities that have the performing-lab role, so those facilities come first. Skip them and the screen says "No performing-lab facilities are set up", and a token cannot be created because at least one facility must be offered.

    # Historical Data Migration Jobs

    3. Business purpose and scope. Status and cross-validation reporting for legacy LIS migration jobs, and the Import legacy file window that starts one. A job reports how many records succeeded, failed or need review, and reconciles the count against the count the source system claimed. Ambiguous patient matches found during import are sent to the existing Patient Match Review queue and are not tracked separately here.

    What is built and what is Simulated. Built: reading a file, applying the mappings, validating, matching to patients, recording the job and its per-record results, and the reconciliation. Simulated: the import runs in the browser, and the draft cases it creates are marked Simulated. A banner says a server-side bulk import replaces it. The file itself is not kept.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. The source system must have active field mappings, so Migration Field Mappings comes first. Skip it and the system list in the window is empty ("No source system has active field mappings yet").

    # Tier 7: Billing, Revenue Cycle Management and Registry Reporting

    This chapter covers how PathScribe decides what to charge, when a charge may leave the system, and which cancer and screening registries a case is reported to. It also covers the payment lookups that the charge payload uses and the System Logs page where you watch financial events.

    Read these three points first, because they set what you can and cannot expect.

    1. What PathScribe does with money. PathScribe resolves each charge once, at finalisation, into a fixed record: CPT or HCPCS code, relative value units (RVU), and modifier. It does not hold prices. Fee schedules: Not built. There is no dollar amount, price or payer rate field anywhere in the billing rules. The charge payload carries no dollar amounts. Reimbursement is worked out by your billing system or the interface engine, not by PathScribe.
    2. What PathScribe does with registries. PathScribe decides whether a case is reportable, checks the mandatory data, and builds a structured JSON payload. It does not itself write NAACCR XML, COSD XML or any registry wire format. The interface engine (ForMedrixAI's engine, shipped with PathScribe) translates and transmits. No registry specification in the product is confirmed against the registry's own published specification unless the section says so.
    3. Most of this chapter is Demonstration today. Production storage is Microsoft SQL Server behind an ASP.NET Core API. The services behind these screens are browser-held demonstration services, and the API contracts in docs/architecture say nothing there was tried against a real server. Each screen carries its own status.

    Setup order for Tier 7

    Do the screens in this order. Each screen's own "Setup sequence" box shows what it requires.

    1. CPT Modifier Dictionary: the modifier list that the Billing Dictionary offers.
    2. RVU Code Map: the CPT and relative value list that every billing rule points to.
    3. Billing Dictionary (Charge Capture): the versioned billing rules.
    4. NCCI Edit Rules: the bundling pairs (you upload them; none ship).
    5. Pending Billing Rule Approvals: a second person approves steps 1 to 4 before anything takes effect.
    6. Charge Release Triggers: the case milestone at which each billing type creates its charge.
    7. Billing Release: hold and batch rules for charges that are ready.
    8. Master Payment Type Dictionary: the payment categories.
    9. Jurisdiction Payment Mapping: local payer schemes mapped to those categories.
    10. Billing Export Preview: check what a real case would send.
    11. Cancer Registry Reporting: the registry per facility and the go-live approval.
    12. UK Cancer Registry (COSD): England destination settings.
    13. US Electronic Pathology: state profiles for the US ePath feed.
    14. Cytology Registry Reporting: cervical screening programme settings.
    15. Registry Batch Files: file-based registry deliveries.

    The System Logs financial tab is a reference page. It is not part of setup.

    Not built in this chapter: fee schedules, AI or natural-language billing suggestions from report text, X12 837P, KVDT and SESAM-Vitale output, NAACCR XML batch files, and MIPS and MACRA quality reporting.

    # Billing engine architecture

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups

    How a charge is modelled. PathScribe splits a charge into a technical component, a professional component, or both together. The product calls these billing types:

    Billing type On-screen label What it covers Modifier set
    TC Technical (TC) Laboratory work: grossing, processing, slides, stains -TC
    26 Professional (26 Prof.) The pathologist's interpretation -26
    Global Combined (Global) Both parts billed together Neither

    PathScribe sets the modifier from the billing type with no exceptions: TC takes -TC, 26 takes -26, Global takes none. Other modifiers are informational only.

    When a charge is created. By default the technical component is created when the specimen is grossed. The professional and global components are created at final sign-out. You can change this for the whole enterprise or for one site on Charge Release Triggers.

    Charges are fixed once created. At finalisation PathScribe resolves the charge once into an immutable charge record that keeps a snapshot of the CPT, HCPCS, RVU and modifier. Later edits to a billing rule do not change a charge already made. A correction after sign-out uses a credit and rebill pair, not an edit.

    Billing rules are versioned. A billing rule is identified by billing code, scope and version. Versions are only ever added. The statuses are DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL, ACTIVE, REJECTED and RETIRED. The person who drafts or submits a version cannot approve it (the Four-Eyes principle, enforced in the services). On approval, the new version takes effect and the version it replaces ends.

    Scope. A rule applies enterprise-wide or to one Site. The word Site is used on these screens, not Facility.

    Split cases. When the technical component is performed at a different laboratory than the professional reading, the case carries a technical component facility and the performing facility. The release decision checks for this (see Billing Release).

    Where charges go. Ready charges go to the Outbound Queue. A charge in PENDING_APPROVAL or HOLD status is skipped by the outbound sweep. The interface engine does the transport, translation and retries. PathScribe only decides what is released and when.

    Optional charge approval. A charge can be held for approval. The approval capability billing:charge:approve is checked per performing laboratory. It is in the capability catalog but no built-in role holds it by default, so grant it through Roles if you use charge approval.

    Fee schedules: Not built. The outline asks for fee schedules. There is no screen, contract or field for a dollar amount, price or payer-specific rate. A billing rule carries only the CPT code, HCPCS code, and RVU values for work, practice expense (PE) and malpractice (MP). The nearest things that exist are the RVU values on the Billing Dictionary and the RVU Code Map. The check called ZERO_FEE_MAPPING_ERROR is worded as a fee check, but it tests for a charge that resolved with zero RVU across work, PE and MP and has no suppression advisory.

    # Auto-coding engine and billing hold rules

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups

    Auto-coding engine: Partial. What is built is rule-based and always confirmed by a person:

    • Suggested codes from structured case data: stain categories, 88312 for a special stain, 88342 and +88341 for immunohistochemistry per specimen, and 88331 or 88332 for a frozen section.
    • A fallback list of default codes. It is not billing-ready.
    • Manual code entry in the code window and the billing review panel.

    Not built: suggestions from the report text by AI or natural-language processing. That work is gated on attorney and compliance input. Base specimen codes (88302, 88305, 88309) are not worked out automatically. The nearest configuration screen is Smart Capture.

    Sign-out billing checks. At sign-out PathScribe runs six checks and records a deficiency for each finding:

    Trigger Code Severity
    A UNSUPPORTED_CPT_LEVEL COMPLIANCE_WARNING
    B NCCI_BUNDLING_VIOLATION (only pairs with modifier indicator 0) CRITICAL_REJECTION_RISK
    C MISSING_DIAGNOSTIC_ICD10 CRITICAL_REJECTION_RISK
    D UNATTACHED_ANCILLARY_ORDER COMPLIANCE_WARNING
    E MODIFIER_MISMATCH CRITICAL_REJECTION_RISK
    F ZERO_FEE_MAPPING_ERROR REVENUE_LEAKAGE

    MISSING_CHARGE, POST_SIGNOUT_CORRECTION and BLOCK_DELETED are raised outside sign-out. These checks never stop the pathologist signing out. A toast says billing items were flagged for QA and the findings go to QA. They do block export: a case cannot be exported while any deficiency is OPEN or UNDER_REVIEW. The statuses are OPEN, UNDER_REVIEW, RESOLVED and OVERRIDDEN_WITH_JUSTIFICATION.

    # Billing Release

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance › Billing Release

    Status: Demonstration

    1. Navigation: Configuration tab System > group Administration & Compliance 2. Maintenance item: Billing Release

    3. Business purpose and scope. The hold rules. Each rule says which charges it matches and what to do with them: release at once, hold for a time, or release in a scheduled batch, with or without manual review. The most specific matching rule wins. PathScribe decides what and when. The interface engine moves the message.

    Specificity points: facility 100, billing type 8, case types 4, ordering site 4, pathologist 2, amendment 1.

    When no rule matches: release at the milestone, manual review on, auto-release on.

    Always applies: an amendment change is parked for review; a charge whose CPT has no mapping is parked (unmappedCpt); a split case with no technical facility is parked (missingTechnicalFacility).

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. A rule can name a facility or ordering site, so set those up first. A scheduled batch is sent on a timetable defined in Delivery Schedules.

    # Cancer registry configuration

    Home › Configuration › System › Lab Materials & Workflows

    What exists. PathScribe has 14 cancer registry definitions and 12 cervical screening registry definitions. Every cancer registry is marked configurable, meaning the specification is not verified against the registry's published specification. Of the screening registries, three are marked verified: the UK cervical screening management system (CSMS), PALGA in the Netherlands and the Australian National Cancer Screening Register (NCSR).

    Cancer registry id Wire format named
    naaccr_us NAACCR XML
    epath_npcr_us HL7 v2 ORU
    cpac_canada NAACCR XML
    cosd_uk COSD XML (GB_EW)
    phs_scotland HL7 v2 ORU
    nicr_northern_ireland HL7 v2 ORU
    ncri_ireland HL7 v2 ORU
    nkr_netherlands PALGA protocol
    inca_france CDA CR-ACP
    adt_gekid_germany oBDS XML
    bcr_belgium HD-S4S JSON
    aihw_australia HL7 v2 ORU
    nz_cancer_registry HL7 v2 ORU
    kccr_korea HL7 v2 ORU

    What each format means today. PathScribe builds one structured JSON payload. The named format is the target the interface engine would translate to. PathScribe does not write NAACCR XML, COSD XML, oBDS, CDA or the other formats. There is no Spain cancer registry or Spain screening registry, although Spain is a jurisdiction in the product. NAACCR XML as a batch file: Not built. MIPS and MACRA: Not built (see Quality and public health reporting).

    Reporting rules built in.

    • The trigger is surgical pathology sign-out only. Cytology never triggers a cancer report. Reporting is fire-and-forget and never holds sign-out.
    • Mandatory data: date of birth, diagnosis date, primary diagnosis and ICD-O code. A registry that keys on a patient identifier also needs that identifier. A report with missing data is held as HOLD_MISSING_MANDATORY_DATA and appears on Registry Exceptions.
    • Reportability: only the documented NAACCR exclusions are built (cervical carcinoma in situ and CIN III, prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia III, and skin basal and squamous cell carcinoma). The list is not exhaustive.
    • Send gate: a validation instance never sends real cases. A production instance holds a report until go-live is approved for that registry.
    • Patient opt-out: the Honours opt-out setting is off by default. When off, an opted-out patient is still reported and the audit log records that.

    # Quality and public health reporting (MIPS/MACRA)

    Home › Configuration › System › Lab Materials & Workflows

    Status: Not built

    PathScribe has no Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS), Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act (MACRA) or Quality Payment Program measure, screen, export or contract. A search of the source and documents found none. Nothing here calculates a quality measure or builds a submission file.

    The nearest things that exist:

    • The Reporting feed sends case data to a business intelligence tool, where you can build your own measures.
    • Exports: users with the right capability can download exports from the application, and the System Logs financial tab exports billing events as CSV.
    • Cancer and cervical screening registry reporting (above) is the public health reporting that is built, in the limits described.

    # Jurisdiction payment mappings, master payment types and the financial log

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups

    PathScribe describes who pays in two layers. A master payment type is a category used everywhere (for example commercial insurance). A jurisdiction payment mapping says that a local scheme (for example DE_GKV) belongs to one category and which outbound format it is meant for. The financial class that goes with a charge is built from both. The outbound formats named on the mapping are labels only: X12 837P, KVDT and SESAM-Vitale are Planned and none is generated.

    # Appendices: Troubleshooting and Audit Log Verification

    This chapter has three parts. The first is a troubleshooting matrix: the problems an administrator meets most often, each with its cause and the screen that fixes it. The second is an index of the error codes PathScribe shows or records. The third documents the System Logs screen and gives a step-by-step guide for verifying what the audit log holds. The glossary of terms is the last chapter of the guide (Glossary).

    The User Guide (Batch 657). The online User Guide for the people who do the work is built from Markdown in docs/user-guide/ by python3 scripts/user-guide/build.py and published with the application under /help; each screen's Help button and F1 open the article for the screen being shown. Configuration and administrator screens keep their Administrator Guide buttons. No setting is needed. Add or change a page by editing its file and rebuilding; the build checks the required sections, links and routes.

    Every message quoted here is the English text from the product. Every code is one that exists in the source; a code that is only a placeholder in a contract, with no use in the product, is not listed.

    # Troubleshooting matrix

    Home › Administrator Guide › Appendices › Troubleshooting matrix

    Status: Built

    How to use the matrix. Find the symptom the user reports, read the likely cause, and follow the fix. Most "it is broken" reports are one of two things: a dictionary that was never set up (an empty list), or a role that does not hold a capability (a greyed-out button or a refused save). When the symptom shows an upper-case code, look it up in the error code index.

    Before anything else. Two checks answer most questions.

    1. Open System Logs and search for the person's name or the capability key. A refused permission check writes a Capability refused entry that names the capability and the person's session role.
    2. Look at the Error Log tab for an open error with a code, source and time near the report.

    # Empty lists and "not set up" messages

    An empty drop-down or a "none configured" message almost always means a dictionary earlier in the setup order was skipped. The Setup order page lists the order.

    Symptom (what the user sees) Likely cause Fix Screen
    In a case's team window: No participation types configured, with the hint "Set up types in System → Participation Types." No participation type exists. Add the types the lab uses, then reopen the window. Participation Types
    A test print or a label window says No printer profiles configured. No printer profile has been added. Add a printer profile for each label printer model. Printer Profiles
    An embedding or microtomy station says No printer configured or The configured printer profile no longer exists. A slide-distribution station says This station isn't set up for slide-label printing. The station has no printer profile, or its profile was deleted. Open the station and choose a printer profile that still exists. Scan Stations, Printer Profiles
    A slide-distribution or scan-batch window says No slide scanners are set up (the text names Configuration, Equipment, kind "Slide scanner"). No equipment record of kind Slide scanner. Add the scanners. Equipment
    A label does not print and the message reads No GS1 GTIN configured. Set one in Print Settings before printing a GS1 cassette label (or slide label). The facility has no GS1 GTIN entered. Enter the GTIN in Print Settings. Print Settings
    Facility Ops dashboard says No display profiles are configured yet. No display profile exists. Add one under Display Profiles. Display Profiles
    The OR dashboard says No terminals configured yet. No OR suite terminal exists. Add the terminals. OR Suite Terminals
    In the routing rule window: No active pools. Enable "Pool / Workgroup" on a Subspecialty first. No subspecialty is in Pool / Workgroup mode. Switch Pool / Workgroup on for at least one subspecialty, then add the rule. Subspecialties, Routing Rules
    In the new container window: No facility is currently configured with the Reference Lab role. No facility has the Reference Lab role. Give a facility that role in its facility settings. Facility Dictionary
    A user trying secure email sees Your lab has no secure messaging gateway set up. The facility has no gateway under its Secure messaging tab. Add a gateway in the facility's settings. Facility Dictionary
    The Client service levels Add list is empty, with the note that every client already has a level or no clients are set up. Every facility already has a service level, or no client facilities exist. Add the facilities first, or edit the existing level. Facility Configuration, Client service levels

    # Saves refused, greyed-out buttons and screens you cannot open

    PathScribe checks capabilities twice. The screen greys out an action the person cannot do. The service behind the action checks again and refuses it. In production the API server repeats the check and has the final word. There is no bypass for any role, Superadmin included.

    Symptom Likely cause Fix Screen
    A button is greyed out. Its tooltip reads Your roles don't include "". None of the person's roles holds that capability. Add the capability to a role the person holds. Capabilities are grouped by area in the Role Dictionary. Roles, Members
    The tooltip reads "" also needs "", which your roles don't include. The capability requires another capability (its requires list in the catalog). Grant both. A role save is refused with "a capability is missing one it needs" until the required one is also granted. Roles
    The tooltip reads "" isn't available here: your facility assignment doesn't cover it. The person holds the capability, but the action touches a facility outside their assigned facilities (or spans all facilities). Change the person's facility assignment. Members
    A Configuration save fails with Not saved: this needs the "" permission. An administrator can grant it in Configuration → Staff → Role Dictionary. The person lacks the config:...:manage capability for that screen (code CONFIG_NOT_PERMITTED). Grant the named permission to the person's role. Roles
    A role save fails: Not saved: no role could manage roles afterwards. The change would leave no assignable role holding config:roles:manage. Give Manage roles to another assignable role first, then save. Roles
    A role or staff save fails with changing the clinical mismatch rules and approving the AI instructions are separate duties. One person (or one role) may not hold both config:clinical-mismatch-rules:manage and config:ai-prompt:approve (code SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES). Split the two capabilities across two roles held by different people. Roles, Members
    A role save fails with this role is managed by ForMedrixAI. The Superadmin role cannot be changed at a hospital. None. Use a different role. Roles
    A user opens a screen and sees You don't have access to this screen; after sign-in the Home page says None of your roles gives you access to a screen yet. The role lacks the screen:<name>:open capability, so Home shows no tile and the route refuses the address. Add the screen capability to the role. Roles
    A person cannot approve their own edit: You edited this text, so you can't approve it. Self-approval is refused for AI instructions (code SELF_APPROVAL). Have a different holder of config:ai-prompt:approve approve it. AI Instructions
    An export button does nothing, or the export screen shows You don't have permission to export this report. Each export has its own capability (for example audit:audit-log:export), and the server checks it again at download. Grant the export capability named on the button's tooltip. Roles, My exports

    # Labels and reports that do not print

    Symptom Likely cause Fix Screen
    A label goes to the browser print window and the message reads The label printer is not connected, so this label went to the browser print window. Check that QZ Tray is running on this computer. The QZ Tray service is not running or not reachable on that computer. Start QZ Tray on the computer and print again. Printer Profiles, Print Settings
    Label did not print: is out of labels / is out of ribbon / the print head is open / could not be reached. The printer reported that state (codes PAPER_OUT, RIBBON_OUT, HEAD_OPEN, PRINTER_UNREACHABLE). Fix the printer, then retry the label. A label is never retried by itself, so it cannot print twice. Print Queue
    ...did not print: rejected the label layout or its barcode failed GS1 validation. This is a PathScribe problem; please report it. The label's content was refused (MALFORMED_ZPL, INVALID_GS1). Retrying cannot help. Report it to ForMedrixAI support with the time and the label's layout. Label Designer
    A report print job is Failed with "Network printing needs the PathScribe site agent." A report was sent to a network printer from a browser, which cannot reach it (NEEDS_SITE_AGENT). Route the lab's printing through a site agent printer. Site agents, Print Destination Routing Rules
    Printing "works" but nothing comes out in the demonstration. The demonstration records prints instead of sending them. Read the simulated print log. Simulated print log

    # Interface messages that are stuck

    Symptom Likely cause Fix Screen
    A message shows in Outbound Interface DLQ with Error Dispatch rejected, Dispatch timeout or Engine unreachable. The interface engine did not return a 2xx (DISPATCH_REJECTED, DISPATCH_TIMEOUT, DISPATCH_UNREACHABLE). The message is kept for retry. Check the engine in the Engines sub-tab. When it is healthy, choose Retry Dispatch (needs interface:outbound:resend). System Logs: interfaces
    Retry answers Held on the Outbound Queue screen: release it there first. The message is on hold in the Outbound Queue. Release it on that screen, then resend. System Logs: interfaces
    Retry answers Held: the report PDF isn't available yet. The report document is not rendered yet. Wait. It is sent with the PDF on a later retry. System Logs: interfaces
    A charge is in the Outbound DLQ (financial) with Missing ICD-10 code or Missing provider NPI. The charge cannot be built without the code or the NPI (MISSING_ICD10, MISSING_PROVIDER_NPI). Enter the value on the row; the row has an input for each. System Logs: financial
    A job in Server jobs cannot be requeued: Resend this job from Interfaces. Interface and print jobs are resent from their own screens (WRONG_SCREEN). Use the interface or print queue, with interface:outbound:resend or print:job:retry. System Logs: interfaces
    A requeue answers This job is no longer failed; it may already have been requeued. Someone already requeued it (NOT_DEAD_LETTERED). Refresh. No action. System Logs
    Pending interface exceptions (a count badge on the Interface Log tab). Inbound messages that could not be bound to a patient or case wait for a person. Open the Interface Exceptions sub-tab and review each. System Logs: interfaces

    # Sign-in fails

    Symptom Likely cause Fix Screen
    Incorrect email or password, then One more failed attempt will lock sign-in for this email for 15 minutes. Password sign-in locks an email after 5 failed attempts in a row, for 15 minutes. The count is per email typed, whether or not the email belongs to an account. Wait 15 minutes, or set a new password for the person: setting a password clears the lock. The audit log holds Sign-in failed, Sign-in locked and Sign-in refused. Members
    Ask your administrator to reset your password from the Staff screen. The person forgot the password. There is no self-service reset in the sign-in form. Set a temporary password on the person's record. The person must choose their own at next sign-in. Members
    Single sign-on: You signed in, but there is no active PathScribe account for you. No staff record matches (not_provisioned). Add the person as a member. The first single sign-on links by email. Members
    Single sign-on: Your PathScribe account is inactive. The staff record is inactive. Reactivate it. Members
    Single sign-on: More than one PathScribe account matches this sign-in. Two staff records share the email (ambiguous). Remove the duplicate. Members
    Single sign-on: This PathScribe account is already linked to a different sign-in account. A reassigned mailbox: the record is linked to another identity at the same provider (already_linked). Unlink the old account on the person's record, then sign in again. Members
    Single sign-on: Your PathScribe account doesn't include access to this application. The person's roles carry neither case access nor configuration access (no_app_access). Give the person a role with access. Roles
    Single sign-on: Your organisation requires a second factor, and the sign-in service did not report one. The identity provider did not report a second factor (mfa_required). Complete the second factor at the identity provider. Session Security
    Sign-in isn't set up for this installation. Contact your system administrator. The build has no sign-in configured. Correct config.json (see the start-up codes below). Start-up configuration codes
    A full-page PathScribe can't start: its configuration needs fixing with a list of codes. config.json has a setting the product refuses. PathScribe will not start with the wrong settings. Correct config.json on the web server and reload. Each code is in the index. Start-up configuration codes
    Second-factor codes: That code was already used. Wait for the next one. or Too many attempts. Second-factor codes are locked until . The code was replayed, or too many wrong codes were entered. Wait for the next code, or until the lock time. Session Security
    This account is already signed in on another tab or window on this browser. PathScribe allows one live session per account per browser. Continue to sign the other session out (its unsaved work is kept and offered for review). Session Security

    # An interface message or screen looks stuck

    Symptom Likely cause Fix Screen
    A screen says The PathScribe server can't be reached. Try again in a moment. The browser could not reach the API server, or it answered with a server error (UNAVAILABLE), or did not answer within 30 seconds (TIMED_OUT). Check the network path and the API server's health. The screen retries where it says so (for example the engines panel every minute). System Logs
    Your session has ended. Sign in again. The server returned 401 (SIGNED_OUT). Sign in again. Session Security
    This was already done. Refresh and look again. or a save that reports a conflict. Someone else changed the same record (CONFLICT). Refresh the screen and apply the change again. System Logs
    An export stays Preparing, or ends The export took too long and was stopped. A build is stopped after 30 minutes (TIMED_OUT). Narrow the filters and export again. My exports
    You already have 3 exports being prepared. One user may have 3 open exports (TOO_MANY_OPEN). Wait for one to finish, or cancel one. My exports

    # System error code index

    Home › Administrator Guide › Appendices › System error code index

    Status: Built

    What this index covers. The upper-case codes in the source that an administrator can see on a screen, read in the Error Log or find in a contract. Each row gives the screen it appears on, what it means and what to do. The contract named in the second column is in docs/architecture/; where no contract lists a code, the row names the service file instead.

    How codes reach a screen. The API client gives every failed call a short fixed code and never uses the server's message text, because that text could name a patient. A server code is used when it is upper-case letters, digits and underscores, from 2 to 40 characters, starting with a letter. Otherwise the code comes from the HTTP status.

    Status Code
    401 SIGNED_OUT
    403 NOT_PERMITTED
    404 NOT_FOUND
    409 CONFLICT
    400, 422 INVALID
    429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS
    anything else UNAVAILABLE

    Lower-case reasons also exist (for example the sign-in reasons not_provisioned and inactive, and the server's capability_refused, support_access_disabled and support_access_not_approved). They are not upper-case codes, so they are in the matrix above and in the Support Access screen, not in this index.

    # Codes any server-backed screen can show

    Error Code Where it appears Meaning What to do
    SIGNED_OUT Any screen that calls the API server. Contract: HTTP_SERVICES_PATTERN.md section 4; src/services/apiServer/apiHttpClient.ts. The server answered 401: the sign-in has ended or the token was not accepted. Sign in again. If it returns straight after signing in, tell ForMedrixAI support.
    NOT_PERMITTED Any server-backed screen. Contract: HTTP_SERVICES_PATTERN.md; AUTHORIZATION_API.md. The server answered 403: the capability is missing, or is outside the person's facilities. See the matrix rows on greyed-out buttons. Search System Logs for Capability refused.
    NOT_FOUND Any server-backed screen. Contract: HTTP_SERVICES_PATTERN.md. The record no longer exists, for example deleted or retired by someone else. Refresh and open it again.
    CONFLICT Any screen with a versioned save. Contract: HTTP_SERVICES_PATTERN.md (versioned saves). The server answered 409: the record changed since it was read. For a case, the server also returns the version it holds. Refresh and apply the change again.
    INVALID Any server-backed save. Contract: HTTP_SERVICES_PATTERN.md. The server answered 400 or 422: it refused the values. Check the entries on the form and save again.
    TOO_MANY_REQUESTS Any server-backed screen. Contract: HTTP_SERVICES_PATTERN.md; STAFF_ADMIN_API.md. The server answered 429: a rate limit was reached. Wait a moment and try again. Repeated cases go to ForMedrixAI support.
    TIMED_OUT Any server-backed screen; the exports list. Contract: HTTP_SERVICES_PATTERN.md; ASYNC_EXPORT_API.md section 4. The call had no answer within 30 seconds (the client's default). For an export build, the build was stopped after 30 minutes. Retry. For an export, narrow the filters.
    UNAVAILABLE Any server-backed screen, for example the workstation list, the site agents list, the engines panel and Server jobs. Contract: HTTP_SERVICES_PATTERN.md. The server could not be reached, answered with any other status, or sent a reply that was not a JSON object. Check the network and the API server. Retry.
    NOT_SUPPORTED A demonstration-only action on a server deployment. Contract: HTTP_SERVICES_PATTERN.md; src/services/apiServer/httpServiceExtras.ts. The method exists only for the demonstration (seeding demo data). The server version makes no call. Nothing. Expected on a server deployment.

    # Permission and approval refusals

    Error Code Where it appears Meaning What to do
    CONFIG_NOT_PERMITTED Every Configuration save. Contract: AUTHORIZATION_API.md; src/services/authorization/guardConfigWrites.ts. The person's roles lack the capability for that screen, so nothing was saved. The Configuration page shows the capability name. Grant the capability on Roles.
    EXPORT_NOT_PERMITTED Case search export and case report export. Contract: CASE_SEARCH_API.md; AUTHORIZATION_API.md (exports). The export capability (search:case-results:export or search:case-report:export) is missing. No rows are returned. Grant the capability.
    SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES Role save and staff save. Contract: AUTHORIZATION_API.md (separation of duties). One role or one person would hold both config:clinical-mismatch-rules:manage and config:ai-prompt:approve. Hold the two capabilities in separate roles with different people.
    SELF_APPROVAL AI instructions. Contract: AUTHORIZATION_API.md; AI Instructions. The person edited the pending text, so cannot approve it. Have another holder of config:ai-prompt:approve approve it.
    AI_VENDOR_NOT_ALLOWED Any AI feature. Contract: AI_PROXY.md; src/services/aiIntegration/aiCallPolicy.ts. The AI vendor policy refuses the service or region for the jurisdiction. The call is not made and is audited as AI_CALL_REFUSED. The feature carries on without AI and says "AI is not available for this jurisdiction." Change the rule or the hosting region on the AI Behavior tab, if the lab's policy allows it.

    # Exports

    Error Code Where it appears Meaning What to do
    INVALID_PARAMETERS My exports. Contract: ASYNC_EXPORT_API.md section 3. The server could not use the filters. Change the filters and export again.
    TOO_MANY_ROWS My exports. Contract: ASYNC_EXPORT_API.md. More than 1,000,000 rows matched. Narrow the filters.
    TOO_MANY_OPEN My exports. Contract: ASYNC_EXPORT_API.md. The person already has 3 exports queued or running. Wait, or cancel one.
    BUILD_FAILED My exports. Source: src/services/exports/asyncExportContract.ts. The server could not make the file. A build gets 2 attempts. Try again. If it fails again, tell ForMedrixAI support.
    CANCELLED My exports. Source: src/i18n/locales/en.json (exports.problem). The export was cancelled. Export again if it is still needed.
    EXPIRED My exports; the site agent. Contract: ASYNC_EXPORT_API.md; SITE_AGENT_API.md section 6. For an export: the file was deleted after its keeping period (7 days by default, 1 to 30 set by the lab). For a site agent job: it was not started in time and was returned. Export again. For a job, see the print rows below.

    # Start-up configuration

    These appear on the full-page PathScribe can't start: its configuration needs fixing screen. PathScribe will not start until they are corrected. The settings and the rules are in RUNTIME_CONFIG.md section 3. The code is src/services/runtimeConfig/runtimeSettings.ts.

    Error Code Where it appears Meaning What to do
    UNREADABLE Start-up screen. config.json is not valid JSON. Correct the file.
    NOT_AN_OBJECT Start-up screen. config.json must be a list of settings and values (a JSON object). Correct the file.
    UNKNOWN_SETTING Start-up screen. The name is not one of the settings PathScribe knows, or is a build-only name. Check the spelling against RUNTIME_CONFIG.md.
    NOT_TEXT Start-up screen. A value must be text, a number, or true or false. Correct the value.
    TOO_LONG Start-up screen. A value is longer than 2,000 characters. Shorten it.
    INVALID_URL Start-up screen. The value must be a web address, or a path on this site starting with /, with no user name or password in it. Correct the address.
    NOT_HTTPS Start-up screen. An address must use https. Plain http is allowed only to this computer in a development build. Use an https address.
    NOT_THIS_SITE Start-up screen. A proxy path leads to another site (for example //host). Use a path on this site, or an https address.
    API_SERVER_REQUIRED Start-up screen. A server build needs the address of the PathScribe server and none is set. Set the API address.
    SSO_REQUIRED Start-up screen. A server build signs in through the identity provider only, so VITE_AUTH_MODE must be sso. Set it and the provider's settings.
    API_SERVER_IN_DEMO_BUILD Start-up screen. A demonstration build never talks to a real server. Install a server build.
    NOT_IN_DEMO_BUILD Start-up screen. A demonstration build cannot use a hub, renderer, interface receiver or server-job setting, and is never production. Install a server build.
    ADDRESS_NOT_FROM_SERVER Start-up screen, marked "from the PathScribe server's /api/config". The server may not set an address, because the site's security policy is made from config.json. Put the address in config.json.
    NOT_FROM_SERVER Start-up screen, marked "from the PathScribe server's /api/config". Only config.json or the build may set this setting (sign-in, the instance role, which jobs the server runs). Move the setting to config.json.

    # Printing, labels and the site agent

    The first six codes have their own message text. The contract for the agent's codes is SITE_AGENT_API.md section 6; the list is AGENT_ERROR_CODES in src/services/siteAgent/siteAgentContract.ts. Report prints are retried on the lab's delivery schedule (1, 5 and 15 minutes by default, up to 10 retries). Labels are never retried by themselves.

    Error Code Where it appears Meaning What to do
    PRINTER_UNREACHABLE Label toast; Print Queue. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. No connection to the printer. Retried for reports. Check the printer's power and network, then retry.
    PAPER_OUT Label toast; Print Queue. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. The label printer is out of labels. Load labels and retry.
    RIBBON_OUT Label toast; Print Queue. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. The label printer is out of ribbon. Load a ribbon and retry.
    HEAD_OPEN Label toast; Print Queue. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. The print head is open. Close it and retry.
    MALFORMED_ZPL Label toast. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. The printer rejected the label layout. Not retried. Report to ForMedrixAI support.
    INVALID_GS1 Label toast. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. The label's barcode failed GS1 validation. Not retried. Report to ForMedrixAI support. Check the GTIN in Print Settings.
    NEEDS_SITE_AGENT Print Queue. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md; src/services/printing/printJobFailureReason.ts. A browser cannot send to a network printer. The job fails at once and goes to the exception queue. Use a site agent printer. See Site agents.
    PRINTER_OFFLINE Print Queue. Source: src/services/printing/attemptPrintDelivery.ts. QZ Tray is not connected on the print computer. Retried. Start QZ Tray.
    PRINT_REJECTED Print Queue. Source: attemptPrintDelivery.ts, redispatchPrintJob.ts. A job cannot be printed, for example no printer is configured for QZ Tray delivery, or the report document could not be made. Fix the printer settings, then retry.
    PRINTER_REJECTED Print Queue. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. The printer refused the job. Not retried. Check the printer's own error display.
    DOCUMENT_UNAVAILABLE Print Queue. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. The agent's download link failed or expired. Retried. None at first. If it persists, tell ForMedrixAI support.
    DOCUMENT_INTEGRITY Print Queue. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. The file's SHA-256 did not match, so it was never printed. Not retried. Tell ForMedrixAI support.
    UNKNOWN_DESTINATION Print Queue; file drop. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. The agent has no printer or share with that id (its configuration is out of date). Update the agent's printer list on Site agents.
    SHARE_UNREACHABLE File drop delivery. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. The share could not be reached. Retried. Check the share.
    SHARE_ACCESS_DENIED File drop delivery. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. The agent may not write to the share. Not retried. Fix the share's permissions.
    SHARE_FULL File drop delivery. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. The share is full. Retried. Free space.
    IN_DOUBT Print Queue. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. The agent stopped after it began sending and before it knew the result. It is never resent by itself. Check the printer. Reprint if the page is not there.
    AGENT_ERROR Print Queue. Contract: SITE_AGENT_API.md. Any other agent failure. Retried. Check the agent on Site agents.

    # Outbound messages, charges, registries and server jobs

    Error Code Where it appears Meaning What to do
    DISPATCH_REJECTED System Logs: interfaces (shown as "Dispatch rejected"). Contract: INTERFACE_TRANSACTIONS.md. The engine did not return a 2xx. The message is kept for retry. Check the engine, then Retry Dispatch.
    DISPATCH_TIMEOUT System Logs: interfaces (shown as "Dispatch timeout"). Contract: OUTBOUND_QUEUE_API.md; INTERFACE_TRANSACTIONS.md. The engine did not answer in time. As above.
    DISPATCH_UNREACHABLE System Logs: interfaces (shown as "Engine unreachable"). Contract: INTERFACE_TRANSACTIONS.md. The engine could not be reached. As above.
    MISSING_ICD10 System Logs: financial. Contract: DIAGNOSIS_CODING.md; src/services/billing/validateChargeMetadata.ts. A charge has no ICD-10 code. Enter the code on the row.
    MISSING_PROVIDER_NPI System Logs: financial. Source: validateChargeMetadata.ts. A charge has no provider NPI. Enter the NPI on the row.
    REGISTRY_NOT_READY Outbound Queue; Registry Exceptions. Contract: BATCH_REGISTRY_FEED_API.md; REGISTRY_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_API.md. A registry submission is held: a required field or setting is missing. Complete the missing item named on the entry.
    REGISTRY_LIVE_NOT_APPROVED Outbound Queue; Registry Exceptions. Contract: REGISTRY_GO_LIVE_API.md. A real case was signed out but the registry connection is not approved live. The entry shows "Held: attestation required". Complete go-live approval on the registry settings screen.
    NOT_DEAD_LETTERED Server jobs. Contract: MESSAGE_BUS_API.md. The job is no longer failed (409). Refresh.
    WRONG_SCREEN Server jobs. Source: src/services/serverJobs/serverJobsContract.ts. Interface and print jobs are not requeued here. Resend from the interface or print queue.

    # System Logs reference

    Home › Administrator Guide › Appendices › System Logs reference

    Status: Built

    System Logs is where the record of what people, the system and the AI did is read. This part documents the screen. The next part (Audit log verification guide) says how to use it to answer an auditor's questions.

    # System Logs

    Home › System Logs

    Status: Built. The audit log is held in the browser in the demonstration; with an API server it is held by the server (see Known limits).

    1. Navigation: Home tile System Logs (address /audit). 2. Maintenance item: System Logs (a reference screen; nothing is set up here).

    3. Business purpose and scope. One screen for the compliance record of the lab: AI actions, user changes, system events, errors, quality-assurance activity, interface and print activity, financial dispatch failures, critical alerts, outside consult links and the background jobs of the API server. It is read-only apart from three actions: marking an error Resolved, resending a failed interface message or print job, and revoking a consult link. Each tab is a different record kept by a different service. The Audit Log and Error Log tabs are documented here. The Interface Log tab is documented in System Logs: interfaces and the Financial tab in System Logs: financial.

    4. Prerequisites and dependencies. The screen shows only what has happened, so there is nothing to configure first except who may open it. A person who lacks screen:audit-log:open sees no Home tile and, if they type the address, the message "You don't have access to this screen".

    Setup sequence · Reference, not part of setup

    Configure first
    Roles, Members
    This unlocks
    None.

    5. Screen.

    The page header reads System Logs with the subtitle "Complete record of AI actions, user changes, system events, errors, and quality assurance activity". A tab strip follows, then a Find a support reference box, then the active tab. A count badge on Error Log shows open errors, on Interface Log the pending interface exceptions and on Quality Assurance the open quality items. A person whose role is Pathologist sees the notice "Showing your case activity only — validation study events are not visible to pathologists".

    6. Field reference. The screen has filters, columns and buttons rather than form fields. Row names start with the tab.
