    7. Permissions. - Open the screen: screen:audit-log:open. Admin, Lab Director and QA Reviewer hold it by default. The Pathologist role does not, by default. - Export: one capability per log, each high risk, each requiring screen:audit-log:open: audit:audit-log:export, audit:error-log:export, audit:interface-log:export, audit:qa-log:export and audit:billing-log:export. Roles that open the screen are seeded with all five. Every export is itself audited. - Resolve an error: audit:error:resolve (high risk). - Consult links tab: audit:consult-links:view. Server jobs: jobs:server-job:view, and requeue with jobs:server-job:requeue. - Scoping on screen: Pathologists see every entry that names a case, plus their own entries with no case. Validation-study events (validation_study_created, validation_study_activated, validation_study_closed, validation_study_deleted, validation_report_generated and the three validation_routing_rule_* events) are hidden from everyone except Admin, Pathologist-Admin and Superadmin. - Viewing the log is not itself audited. Exports, resolving an error and a support-reference lookup are.

    Known limits. - No tamper-evidence on the main audit log. The main audit log is append-only by design (no update or delete call exists in the service, and the server contract gives the application's database login no such permission), but its entries are not hash-chained and nothing on screen verifies them. The only hash-chained record is the Support Access audit. See the verification guide. - Retention is a setting, not enforced. The log's keeping period is set on Data Retention. No purge job reads it yet (PS-345), so nothing is deleted by it today. - Audit detail is English by design. It is a compliance artifact, not interface text. The column headings, filters and buttons are translated; the detail text and the exported file are not. - Demonstration. Without an API server the audit log is stored in the browser and starts with seeded sample entries. The time and the acting user come from the browser. With an API server the server sets the time and the actor from the sign-in token. - No facility or station column on screen or in the CSV, though both are recorded (see above).

    # Audit log verification guide

    Home › Administrator Guide › Appendices › Audit log verification guide

    Status: Partial. The recording, searching and export are built. Tamper-evidence for the main audit log and automatic purging by retention are not built.

    Who this is for. An administrator or a ForMedrixAI services engineer who has to show an auditor or inspector what changed, who changed it and when. It uses only what exists today.

    # What is recorded

    Each audit entry holds: an id; a time (stored in UTC); a type (AI, User or System); an event name; a detail sentence in English; the acting user's display name; a case accession number when there is one; an AI confidence where it applies; a facility id where the code supplies it; and the scan station where the action was done. The station id is added automatically to every entry the audit service writes.

    What lands in the log:

    • Every check of a high-risk capability, allowed or refused. The event is Capability allowed or Capability refused. The detail names the capability key, the roles that granted it or the reason it was refused, the person's session role and the facility. The capability catalog marks which capabilities are high risk. A configuration screen's save is one of these checks.
    • Role and staff changes. Role capabilities changed lists what was granted and removed for a role. Staff access changed records a change to a person's roles, facilities, pediatric access, orchestration access or cross-tenant QA access, each from and to. Staff credentials changed records credential edits.
    • Sign-in events. Signed in, Sign-in failed (attempt n of 5), Sign-in locked, Sign-in refused, SSO account linked, SSO account unlinked and SSO sign-in refused. The log never records what was typed.
    • Named change events for some settings. For example AI_VENDOR_POLICY_CHANGED, CLINICAL_MISMATCH_RULE_CHANGED, AI_PROMPT_EDITED, AI_PROMPT_APPROVED, FEEDBACK_SETTINGS_CHANGED, RECALL_SETTINGS_CHANGED, QA_TREND_POLICY_CHANGED, CODE_SYSTEM_POLICY_CHANGED, PEER_REVIEW_GATE_CHANGED, Template review settings changed, Organ map colours changed, Signing-authority country profile changed and the four Signing-authority facility override events (added, changed, removed, justification updated). The facility override events carry each changed flag from and to, and the administrator's justification or "Justification: none given".
    • Spoken commands. Voice command executed and Voice command refused. The detail names the action id and the screen, for example Voice command executed: action TABLE_DELETE on screen WORKLIST; confirmed by repeating the phrase; a refusal gives the reason (not available on this screen, the phrase was not repeated to confirm, or not repeated in time). The person is the acting user. The log never records what was said, and no entry names a case.
    • Prints and exports. DOCUMENT_PRINTED, DOCUMENT_REPRINTED, DOCUMENT_RENDERED, DOCUMENT_EXPORTED, DOCUMENT_FAXED: who, the accession, the destination, the status and, for an export, the row count.
    • Case events, such as synoptic generation, field updates, finalization, protocol selection, drift detection and correction, billing corrections and patient management (mpi.*).
    • Automatic actions under a system actor.

    Two limits matter when you read the record.

    1. A capability entry shows that a person used a capability and whether it was allowed. For most settings it does not show the old and new values. Only the events named above, and a few others, carry the change itself.
    2. A change made while a Superadmin session is acting in another organisation is also written to that organisation's Support Access record.

    The detail text is English by design. Audit records are compliance artifacts, not interface text, so the detail stays literal English in every language of the product and in the export. Search with the English event name or the capability key.

    # How to find a change to a setting

    1. Open System Logs, tab Audit Log.
    2. Set Date range. The default is Last 7 Days; choose Custom Range for an older change. Entries outside the range are hidden, not missing.
    3. In Search, type the capability key for the screen you are checking. Every Configuration screen's change capability is named in its Permissions part in this guide (for example config:retention-policy:manage for Data Retention). The search matches the detail text, so it finds the Capability allowed entries.
    4. Read the User and Timestamp columns for who and when. The detail names the role that granted the capability.
    5. If the screen has a named change event (see the list above), search for that event name too. It holds the change itself, not only the permission check.
    6. To exclude noise, use the Type pills (User shows the human actions).
    7. To see only refusals, search Capability refused.

    An entry that says Capability allowed shows that the person was permitted to make the change, and that the change was attempted. It does not by itself prove which value was saved. For a setting without its own change event, compare against the screen's current value and, if the lab keeps one, a configuration export (see Export below).

    # How to check who changed a permission

    1. On the Audit Log tab, search Role capabilities changed. Each entry reads Role "<name>": granted <keys>; removed <keys>. The User column is the person who saved the role.
    2. To see who was given or lost a role, search Staff access changed. The detail lists each change from and to (roles, facilities, pediatric access, orchestration access, cross-tenant QA access).
    3. To see credential edits, search Staff credentials changed.
    4. To see whether a person actually used a permission, search the capability key and read the Capability allowed and Capability refused entries.
    5. To list who can do something today, use Roles and Members; the log shows history, those screens show the present state.
    6. For a role the hospital cannot change: a change to the Superadmin role is refused at a hospital, so no entry will show one. Superadmin is held by ForMedrixAI support staff and is granted outside the hospital's staff directory.

    A role save is also refused, before anything is written, if it would leave no role able to manage roles, would break a separation-of-duties pair, or would grant a capability without its required one. A refused save writes no Role capabilities changed entry.

    # How record integrity and retention work

    Append-only. The audit service has no call to update or delete an entry; it can only write new ones and read them. The server contract (STAFF_ADMIN_API.md section 1; AUTHORIZATION_API.md) requires the audit table to be append-only: no update or delete call exists and the application's database login has no such permission. A resolved error is the one change allowed to a record, and it is recorded as who and when on the error entry, not as an overwrite of the message.

    Who sets the time and the actor. With the API server, the server sets the time and the acting user from the bearer token. The browser sends only the event, so a user cannot choose the name that appears. In the demonstration, the browser does.

    Unique ids. Every entry gets a unique id. The server's table is expected to enforce uniqueness as well.

    Tamper-evidence: the main audit log has none. The main audit log is not hash-chained or signed. Nothing on the System Logs screen proves that an entry has not been altered by someone with direct database access, and there is no "verify" button for it. Integrity rests on the append-only rule above and on database permissions. The only record that is hash-chained is the Support Access audit (see below). If your auditor requires cryptographic tamper-evidence for the main log, say so to ForMedrixAI: it is not built.

    Retention. The keeping period for the audit log is a setting on Data Retention: the field Audit Logs, in days, from 90 to 3650, 365 by default. The screen says a change "takes effect at next purge cycle". No purge job reads this setting yet (PS-345), so today nothing is deleted by it. Treat the number as a recorded policy, not an enforced one. A record of each export (who, what, when, row count and file hash) is kept with the audit log's retention.

    Exports are working copies. The exported CSV is a copy of what was on screen. The record of the export is the audit entry.

    # How to export

    1. On the tab you need, set the filters first. The export covers the rows the filters leave, not the whole log.
    2. Choose Export CSV. The button is greyed out, with a tooltip naming the capability, unless the person holds the export capability for that tab (see Permissions above).
    3. The service checks the capability before building the file. A refusal builds nothing.
    4. With an API server the export is built by the server (see My exports): the file is a working copy kept for 7 days by default (1 to 30), a person may have 3 open exports, and more than 1,000,000 rows is refused. In the demonstration the browser builds and downloads the file at once.
    5. A file name has the form pathscribe-audit-log-<date>.csv. The first lines are a header naming the report, who requested it, the filters used and the row count. Then the columns: ID, Timestamp, Type, Event, Detail, Actioned By, Accession No., AI Confidence. Cells that begin with =, +, - or @ are neutralised so a spreadsheet will not run them as a formula.
    6. Every export writes a DOCUMENT_EXPORTED entry with the person, the file name, the format and the row count. Search DOCUMENT_EXPORTED to see who has exported the log.
    7. The CSV does not carry the facility or station ids. If an inspector needs them, say so to ForMedrixAI services: the server holds them.
    8. The other tabs export the same way, each with its own capability and its own columns: Error Log (ID, Timestamp, Severity, Code, Message, Source, Accession No., Resolved), Quality Assurance (ID, Group, Date, Case, Specimen, Detail, Status, User), Interface Log and the Financial billing log.

    # How the Support Access audit fits

    ForMedrixAI support reaching your data is recorded in its own stream, separate from the main audit log, and it belongs to your organisation. It is documented on Support Access.

    • What it records. Policy changes; requests, approvals, rejections, expiries, early ends and revocations; refused opens; case opens and edits; every list, search or report that disclosed your cases (with the case ids); the names, never the values, of search criteria; and exports of this audit. A support agent's own exports and configuration changes are recorded here too (as supportExport and supportConfigChange), as well as in the main audit log.
    • Entries are never removed. Each entry holds a sequence number, the time, the actor, the ticket, the action, the case ids and an English, patient-free detail.
    • It is hash-chained. Each entry carries a SHA-256 over its fields and the previous entry's hash, starting from 64 zeros. A changed, removed or re-ordered entry breaks the chain. The screen says Record intact (N entries) or Record altered at entry N, and the JSON export carries the chain check.
    • To verify it. Open Support Access, read the audit panel's chain line, and export JSON for an independent check. You need config:support-audit:view.
    • Export formats. CSV, JSON and PDF, with the columns Timestamp, Support agent name, Originating IP, Originating country, Ticket ID, Action taken, Case IDs, Detail.
    • Limits. Originating IP and country can only be recorded truthfully by the server from the request, so the demonstration leaves them empty. Tenant-isolated storage in its own append-only table is server work (PS-358).

    This is the one record in the product with built-in tamper-evidence. It covers support access only, not the main audit log.

    # A short verification routine

    For a routine review of a sampled period, work through these steps.

    1. Set the Audit Log date range to the period. Record the count in the footer ("Showing N of M events").
    2. Search Role capabilities changed, Staff access changed and Capability refused and read each entry.
    3. Search Sign-in locked and Sign-in refused for sign-in problems.
    4. Search DOCUMENT_EXPORTED to see who took data out.
    5. Open the Error Log tab, filter Open Only, and check that nothing important is unresolved.
    6. Open Support Access and confirm the chain line reads intact; read the entries for the period.
    7. Export the Audit Log CSV for the period and keep the file with your review notes. The export is itself recorded.

    # Step-by-step procedures: report templates, synoptic templates, JSON files and scheduled reports

    This chapter is a set of numbered procedures. The screen chapters (Chapter 6 for templates, the Synoptic Library and delivery) say what each field means; this chapter says what to click, in what order, what you should see, and how to undo it. Each procedure names the screen it uses, so you can jump to the field reference. Labels, billing and registries are in Chapter 11.

    Read these points first.

    1. Status. Every screen used here is Built, except Delivery Schedules, which is Partial, and saved-report schedules, which are Demonstration (nothing is delivered). Today most data services are browser-held demonstration services; the production API is connected service by service. A step that works in the demonstration may not yet be backed by the production server.
    2. There are two different kinds of template. A report template (Configuration tab Report Templates) lays out the printed report: header, body and footer parts. A synoptic template, also called a protocol (Configuration tab Synoptic Library), is the structured checklist of questions a pathologist answers for a cancer or cytology case. They are built on different screens, saved in different formats and routed by different rules. Only the synoptic template has a JSON file (see Part C); a report template has none.
    3. Draft first, and a second person to publish. A synoptic template is never published straight from the editor. It goes Draft, then In Review, then Approved, then Published. By default the person who wrote it cannot approve or publish it (see Review rules).
    4. Permissions. Each procedure lists the capability it needs. If a button is greyed out, you do not hold the capability. Who holds it by default is in the Permissions line of the screen's own section in Chapter 6.
    5. Copy names. A copy made by Duplicate is named <name> (Copy) in English. The wording follows the language of the person who made it, and the name is stored, so it does not change if someone later switches language.

    # Part A: Report templates, parts and routing

    Home › Configuration › Report Templates

    A report template is built from parts. The order of work is always the same: make or copy the parts, publish them, assemble them into a template, publish the template, then tell routing which cases use it. Only published parts can be placed in a template, and only a published template can be chosen by routing.

    Permissions: opening the tab needs screen:configuration:open. Create, edit, duplicate, delete and archive need config:report-template:manage. Publish needs config:report-template:publish. Both are high risk and audited. Admin and Lab Director hold both; Template Author holds manage; Template Approver holds publish. Reference: Part Library, Report Templates, Routing Rules.

    # A1. Copy an existing part (Duplicate)

    Home › Configuration › Report Templates › Part Library

    Use this to change a built-in part, because a built-in part (the card shows a Built-in badge) cannot be edited or archived.

    1. Open the Configuration tab Report Templates, then the sub-tab Part Library.
    2. Find the part. Type part of its name in Search, or narrow with the type buttons (All, Headers, Bodies, Footers) and the lab filter.
    3. On the part's card, select Duplicate. The button reads "Duplicating…" for a moment.
    4. The part builder opens on the copy, named <original name> (Copy), in Draft. Change what you need (see A2, steps 5 to 9).
    5. Select Publish when it is ready.

    To undo: archive the copy (see A3). The original is never changed.

    # A2. Create a new part

    Home › Configuration › Report Templates › Part Library › Part builder
    1. Open Report Templates > Part Library.
    2. Select New Part. The page asks "What kind of part are you creating?". The three choices are Header Part (institution branding, accession number, patient demographics, at the top of pages), Body Part (the clinical content: diagnosis, gross description, microscopic, synoptic data) and Footer Part (page numbers, confidentiality notice, patient identity line). Choose one. The kind cannot be changed afterwards, because it decides which template slot the part can go in.
    3. The part builder opens with a name such as New Body Part. Click the name and type a clear one, for example Surgical body: diagnosis and microscopic.
    4. Select Settings to open the details. Optionally fill in Specialty (blank means General), Description, Standard (None, CAP, RCPath or Custom; this is a label only and does not load or check any protocol) and Performing Lab. Leave Performing Lab on "Global (every performing lab)" unless the part is only for one laboratory.
    5. Drag components from the Components palette (groups: Structure, Content Blocks, Layout, Conditional) onto the canvas.
    6. Click a component on the canvas. Its settings appear in the inspector on the right: label, width, binding key, required, hide when empty, visibility conditions and so on. The full list is in Inspector. A field that shows case data needs its Binding key.
    7. Drag components up or down to reorder them. Use Grid on / Grid off if the grid gets in your way; it only changes the display.
    8. Watch the save indicator at the top: it reads Unsaved, Saving, Saved or Error. The part saves as you edit.
    9. Select Publish. The button then reads Published. If the part marks a field as the final diagnosis and a template that already uses it would end up with more than one, publishing is refused with a message naming the template. Unmark the extra field and publish again.

    You should see the part on its card in the library under Headers, Bodies or Footers, with a Published badge. Use the back arrow (←) to return to the library.

    # A3. Edit, archive or restore a part

    Home › Configuration › Report Templates › Part Library
    1. In the Part Library, find the part and select Edit (not offered on built-in parts).
    2. Change it as in A2, steps 3 to 8.
    3. To take a part out of use, select Archive on its card, then Yes to confirm (No cancels). Archived parts are hidden from the list and from the template editor's part picker.

    Templates that already contain the part are not rewritten when you archive it. Whether the part still appears in a template that was published earlier is not verified here; check with a preview before you rely on it.

    # A4. Create a report template

    Home › Configuration › Report Templates › Report Templates
    1. Open Report Templates > the sub-tab Report Templates. The page is titled "Report Templates".
    2. Choose how to start. - From Standard (also Use Standard Template when the list is empty). Copies the standard surgical pathology layout as a new draft named My Surgical Pathology Report and opens the editor. This is the quickest start. - New Template (also Start Blank). Opens the editor on an empty draft.
    3. In the editor, click the template name at the top and type the real name. It saves when you click out of the box.
    4. In the Part Library panel on the left, set the Performing lab filter. "All Labs (Global + every lab)" shows every published part; Global or one lab narrows the list. Use Search parts to find one by name. If the panel says "No published parts found", publish the parts first (A2).
    5. Click the + in a zone of the page layout to choose where the next part goes. The zones are Page 1 Header, Pages 2+ Header, Body, Pages 2+ Footer and Page 1 Footer. The panel header changes to "Click a part to add" and the target.
    6. Click a part in the panel. It is placed in the zone you chose. Repeat for each zone. A header or footer zone holds one part; the Body zone holds a list. Pages 2+ can read "same as Page 1".
    7. Drag body parts to reorder them. Use the dot (●) on a slot to switch it off or on without removing it. Use the remove button to take a part out. Body parts continue across all pages.
    8. Select Style to set the template's default font family, size (points), bold, underline and text transform for headers, body or footers. Leave a value blank to follow the laboratory default from Document Style. A single component can still override it.
    9. If the template should use AI-assisted writing in Orchestration mode, select a component and set its AI generation fields in the inspector (see Chapter 5).
    10. Select Preview to see the template filled with mock case data, with the page count. Margins and page size here apply to the preview only.
    11. Check that no message under "Assembly issues" remains. Mark at most one field as the final diagnosis if the template is a Final template: with more than one, Publish is refused ("A Final template may have only one; unmark the others before publishing").
    12. Select Publish. The button then reads Published. The indicator reads "Saved" when the last change has been stored.

    You should now see the template in the list with a Published badge, an AI badge if AI generation is on, and the number of active slots.

    # A5. Copy a report template (Duplicate)

    Home › Configuration › Report Templates › Report Templates
    1. Open Report Templates > Report Templates. Use Search templates… or the status buttons (All, Published, Draft, Archived) to find the template.
    2. Point at the row. Its buttons appear on hover: Edit, Duplicate and Delete (a draft) or Archive (anything that was ever published).
    3. Select Duplicate. A copy named <name> (Copy) is created as a draft and the editor opens on it.
    4. Change the copy as in A4, steps 3 to 11, then select Publish.

    The standard template shows a STANDARD badge and has no Edit button; copy it to change it.

    # A6. Edit, delete or archive a report template

    Home › Configuration › Report Templates › Report Templates
    1. To change a template, select Edit on its row and work as in A4. The editor offers Edit on every row except the standard template. To change a template that is already in use, the safest route is to Duplicate it, edit the copy, publish the copy, point routing at the copy (A7), then archive the old one.
    2. To remove a draft that was never published, select Delete, then Yes at the "Delete?" prompt. This removes it for good.
    3. To retire a template that was ever published, select Archive, then Yes at "Archive?". It is not deleted, so the structure of reports already generated from it stays available.

    Whether editing a published template in place changes reports that are already open is not verified here. Do not edit a template in place during clinical hours; use the copy route in step 1.

    # A7. Route cases to a template (Routing Rules)

    Home › Configuration › Report Templates › Routing Rules

    Routing decides which published report template a case uses. The built-in chain is protocol, then subspecialty, then the gold standard. Rules you add override it. Permission: config:template-routing:manage (Admin and Lab Director). Reference: Routing Rules.

    1. Open Report Templates > the sub-tab Routing Rules ("Template Routing Rules").
    2. Choose the section that fits. - Facility Overrides: a given facility always uses a given template. Select Add Facility Rule. - Physician Preferences: a given physician always uses a given template. Select Add Physician Rule. - Protocol Mappings: a given synoptic protocol uses a given template. Select Add Protocol Mapping. Use this when you have published a new or changed synoptic protocol and want it to use a template without waiting for a software release.
    3. In the window, pick the facility, physician or protocol. A protocol that is not yet published shows its state in brackets, and archived protocols are not offered.
    4. Pick the Performing Lab: "Global (every performing lab)" or one lab. A lab-specific rule is checked before a Global rule for that lab's own cases.
    5. Pick the Report Template. Only published templates are listed.
    6. Optionally type a Note ("Why does this override exist?"). Select Add Rule.
    7. To test, scroll to Test Template Routing. Choose a Performing Facility, Ordering Physician, Subspecialty and Synoptic Template ID (each can stay "Any" or "None"), then select Test Routing. The result names the template and the pass that chose it, and the Resolution priority panel highlights that pass. An "Ambiguous" result lists the templates that qualify; add a more specific rule to settle it.
    8. To switch a rule off without losing it, use Disable rule on its row (it then reads Enable rule and shows Disabled). To remove it, select the delete button and confirm at "Delete?". To change it, use the edit button and select Save Changes.

    To undo a rule: disable it. Cases then fall through to the next pass.

    # Part B: Synoptic templates (protocols)

    Home › Configuration › Synoptic Library

    A synoptic template is a set of sections, each holding questions (the editor calls them fields). Each question has a type, answer options, optional SNOMED CT and ICD codes, and optional rules about when it shows. A template is saved as a draft, submitted for review, approved and then published.

    # B1. Who may do what, and the review rules

    Home › Configuration › Synoptic Library › Review Queue
    Step Capability Default holders
    Draft, import, build, save, submit config:protocol:draft Template Author, Admin
    Approve, or return for changes config:protocol:approve Template Approver, Lab Director, Admin
    Publish config:protocol:publish Template Approver, Lab Director, Admin
    Archive, restore config:protocol:retire Template Approver, Lab Director, Admin

    Rules enforced when someone approves or publishes (from templatePublishingRules.ts):

    • Independent review. Anyone who authored or edited the template (every saver is recorded) cannot approve or publish it, unless the site setting Allow Template Self-Approval is on. It is off by default.
    • Approvals needed. The site setting for required reviewers (1 to 3, default 1) says how many different people must approve before the template can be published. Set both in Template Review.
    • Coding coverage. A diagnostic template needs at least 80% field-level SNOMED coverage to publish. A procedural template such as a grossing checklist is exempt.
    • If the check fails, the screen names the reason: the person is not an approver, is the author, the approvals are too few, or coverage is below 80%.

    On a one-person system nobody can approve a template they wrote. Turn on self-approval in Template Review for a test system, or plan a second person before you start.

    # B2. Create a synoptic template from scratch

    Home › Configuration › Synoptic Library › Template editor

    Permission: config:protocol:draft. Without it the editor opens read-only with the message "Read only: you can view this template, but drafting and submitting it needs the Template Author role."

    1. Open the Configuration tab Synoptic Library. Choose Active Protocols, Review Queue or All Protocols; each has the Build / Customise button.
    2. Select Build / Customise. The window is titled "Build / Customise" with the line "Start blank or base it on an existing template".
    3. Select Start from Scratch ("Blank template — define your own sections, fields, and coding"). The editor opens with the breadcrumb "Protocols › New Template".
    4. Under Template Metadata, fill in: - Template Name (required). It must be unique among protocols that are not archived; otherwise the editor says A template named "<name>" already exists. - Anatomical Category (pick one of the pills, for example Breast, Colon, Lung, Prostate, Skin). The editor needs a category before the template counts as ready. - Source / Governing Body: CAP, RCPath, ICCR, RCPA or Custom. It decides the names of the review actions (for example CAP: Accept and Release; RCPath: Ratify). - Reporting standard (optional; for a cytology system such as a Bethesda edition) and Staging edition (optional, for example AJCC 8th). - Version. It starts at 1.0.0. The up buttons bump MAJOR, MINOR or PATCH.
    5. In the first section, type a Section title in the box. Select + Add Section for each further section.
    6. In a section, select + Add Field to add a question. For each question:
    7. Type the Field label (for example Tumor site).
    8. Choose the Field Type: Dropdown, Radio, Checkbox, Numeric, Free Text or Long Text. (Part grid and Mohs stage map questions are built into some PathScribe protocols and cannot be picked as a new type.)
    9. Tick Required if it must always be answered. A required question shows a Required badge.
    10. For Dropdown, Radio or Checkbox, select + Add Answer Option for each answer and type its label. Select the ⌥ button on an option to add its SNOMED CT and ICD codes.
    11. Optionally add Field-level Coding (a SNOMED CT code and an ICD code for the question itself), a Hint / Helper Text, and, for Numeric, a Unit (for example cm).
    12. Use the up and down arrows to reorder sections and questions. Use Collapse and Expand to tidy a long form. Use the delete buttons to remove a question or section.
    13. To show a question or section only in some cases, open its condition and choose Show it: "when the answer is" or "unless the answer is". Pick the trigger question (only Dropdown, Radio and Checkbox questions can be triggers), then the answer. + Or also when… adds an alternative. A question that carries the badge IF has a condition.
    14. Select 👁 Preview to try the form as a pathologist would, with conditions live. Select Reset to clear your trial answers.
    15. Check the Readiness panel on the right. It ticks Template name, Category set, At least 1 section and At least 1 field. The Coding Coverage panel shows the SNOMED CT and ICD percentages; a diagnostic template needs SNOMED at 80% or more to publish.
    16. Select 💾 Save Draft. The page shows "● Unsaved changes" until you do. The address changes to the saved template, so a page refresh does not create a second copy.
    17. When it is ready for review, select 📤 Submit for Review, then Submit for Review → in the window ("This will move … to the Review Queue and notify admins and clinical leads. You won't be able to edit it until it's returned for changes.").

    If you leave the page with unsaved changes the window "Unsaved Changes" offers Save Draft & Leave, Discard Changes and Keep Editing.

    To undo: before submitting, archive the draft (see B8). After submitting, a reviewer must return it (B6).

    # B3. Copy a synoptic template (Duplicate or Build / Customise)

    Home › Configuration › Synoptic Library › All Protocols

    Use a copy to start a variant of a protocol (for example a local version of a CAP checklist). The copy is a new protocol and the original is not changed.

    Route 1, from the list:

    1. Open Synoptic Library > All Protocols (or Active Protocols).
    2. Find the protocol with Search protocols… or the status filter.
    3. Open the row (on Active Protocols, click it to expand) and select Duplicate.
    4. The editor opens on a copy, named <name> (Copy). The version is bumped by one PATCH. The copy keeps whether the original is diagnostic, its type and its group.

    Route 2, from the Build window:

    1. Select Build / Customise.
    2. Under "or base it on", search for the template by name, source or category (Search by name, source, or category…). Each result shows its version and field count.
    3. Select the template, then Customise This Template →. The editor opens on a copy.

    Then continue as in B2, steps 4 to 12. Give the copy its own Template Name first, because two protocols that are not archived cannot share a name.

    # B4. Edit an existing synoptic template

    Home › Configuration › Synoptic Library › Template editor
    1. Open Synoptic Library > All Protocols and find the protocol.
    2. A Draft or Needs Changes protocol shows Open Editor. An In Review or Approved protocol shows Open Reviewer (the editor is locked until it is returned). A Published protocol shows View Protocol only; to change it, make a New Version (B5).
    3. Select Open Editor. Change sections, questions, options, codes and conditions as in B2 steps 5 to 10.
    4. If a reviewer returned it, a Changes Requested banner shows the reviewer's note. Fix what it asks for.
    5. Select 💾 Save Draft, then 📤 Submit for Review.

    Things the editor can set on a question beyond the basics (all stored in the template and in the JSON file):

    • Narrative phrase on an answer, and Narrative sentence and Clinical tier on a question. Write the sentence with a {value} placeholder, for example The specimen is {value}.. The editor warns "This sentence has no {value}" if you leave it out. Tier 1 carries the diagnostic category.
    • Reports as (Nothing specific, pT, pN, pM, FIGO stage, Block identifier). What the question reports in the structured result sent to the LIS and registries.
    • Count rules on a Numeric question: whole number, "Can't exceed" another count, "Can't be below the sum of" other counts, or a total from a grid. A value that breaks a count rule stops the save and the sign-out.
    • Filled from in-house molecular test on a choice question, with what a positive and a negative result mean.
    • Deprecated codes and Terminology warnings buttons appear at the top when the codes in use have alerts. Review them before submitting.

    # B5. Publish a new version of a published template

    Home › Configuration › Synoptic Library › Active Protocols
    1. Open Synoptic Library > Active Protocols. Click the protocol's row to expand it.
    2. Select New Version. The editor opens on a copy with the same name, the MINOR number bumped (for example 1.0.0 becomes 1.1.0), and a link to the published protocol it replaces. The breadcrumb reads "New version — v".
    3. Make the changes. Use a MAJOR bump for a change that alters what is reported, if your lab policy says so; the bump buttons are in Template Metadata.
    4. Save Draft and Submit for Review, then review and publish as in B6.
    5. When the new version is published, the old one is archived. Reports already written with the old one keep their content.

    # B6. Review, approve and publish

    Home › Configuration › Synoptic Library › Review Queue

    This is done by a different person from the author (see B1).

    1. Open Synoptic Library > Review Queue. A banner states "Templates require ≥80% SNOMED coverage and clinical sign-off before publishing." Count tiles show In Review, Needs Changes and Approved.
    2. Open the card ("Open Reviewer"). Read the questions, the options and the coding coverage.
    3. To send it back, select Needs Changes and type the reason (required). The author sees it in the Changes Requested banner and the card shows "Open Editor to Address Changes".
    4. To approve, select Approve (CAP: Accept; RCPath: Ratify) and optionally add notes. If the site needs more than one approval, the protocol stays In Review until enough different people have approved.
    5. When it shows Approved, the card reads "Open Reviewer to Publish". Select Publish (CAP: Release). If a rule fails, the message names it; coverage under 80% must be fixed in the editor first.
    6. After publishing, the protocol appears under Active Protocols, available to all pathologists at once.

    To undo a publish: archive it (B8) and restore a previous version.

    # B7. Export a synoptic template to a file

    Home › Configuration › Synoptic Library › Active Protocols
    1. Open Active Protocols or All Protocols, and open the protocol's row.
    2. Select Export JSON. The browser downloads a file named from the protocol and version, for example cap-colon-resection-v1.0.0.json.
    3. The export is recorded in the audit log. The button has no separate permission; anyone who can open the screen can export.

    The file is the starting point for the JSON procedures in Part C.

    # B8. Archive and restore a synoptic template

    Home › Configuration › Synoptic Library › All Protocols

    Permission: config:protocol:retire.

    1. Open the protocol's row and select Archive.
    2. Read the window "Archive protocol?". For a published protocol it says it will no longer be offered for new reports and that reports already written with it keep their content.
    3. Confirm. The protocol disappears from the All filter; choose the Archived filter to see it.
    4. To bring it back, open All Protocols, choose Archived, and select Restore as draft. It returns as a draft and must go through review again before it can be used.

    # Part C: Building a synoptic template from a JSON file

    Home › Configuration › Synoptic Library › Upload Protocol

    A PathScribe synoptic template can be written as a JSON file and imported as a draft. The import checks only the file's format. It does not check the clinical content against the CAP or RCPath published protocol, because PathScribe does not hold those bodies' licensed files; every result says "Unverified against CAP or RCPath: only the file's format was checked, not its content against the published protocol." The imported draft still goes through review.

    What can be imported. Only a PathScribe JSON protocol. A CAP eCC (SDC) XML form or an Excel workbook (.xlsx) is read and reported, but "can be checked here but not imported yet". Report templates have no import file.

    Limits. JSON, XML or XLSX; at most 10 MB; not empty.

    # C1. The easiest way: export, edit, import

    1. Export an existing protocol as in B7.
    2. Open the .json file in a text editor that checks JSON (any code editor; a word processor will damage the quotation marks). Edit the values.
    3. Change the name inside template to a name that no non-archived protocol uses. An import is refused if the name exists.
    4. Save the file and import it (C4).

    PathScribe gives the imported draft a new id and ignores the id, supersedesId and copiedFromId in the file, so an import can never overwrite an existing protocol.

    # C2. The file layout

    Two layouts are accepted.

    1. The export wrapper (what Export JSON writes). format must be exactly pathscribe-synoptic-protocol. formatVersion is a number; the current version is 1, and a file with a higher number is refused ("exported by a newer version of PathScribe"). The template is inside template. The protocol block (id, name, source, version, category, status, isDiagnostic, supersedesId) describes the protocol as it was when exported and is not used on import.
    2. A bare template: just the object that would sit in template, with sections at the top.

    The template object:

    Property Type Required Meaning
    id text Yes in the model Replaced on import.
    name text Yes (checked) Shown in the library. Must be unique among non-archived protocols.
    source text Yes in the model CAP, RCPath, ICCR, RCPA or Custom. On import the Governing Body you choose in the window decides this (CAP, RCPath and ICCR are kept; RCPA and Other become Custom).
    version text such as 1.0.0 Yes in the model Major.minor.patch.
    category text Yes in the model The anatomical category, for example COLON.
    sections list Yes (checked, at least one) The sections.
    ajccEdition text No Staging edition, for example AJCC 8th.
    standard text No Reporting system, for example a Bethesda edition.

    A section:

    Property Type Required Meaning
    id text Yes in the model Unique inside the template. Conditions point at ids, so give every section and field one.
    title text Yes (checked) The section heading.
    fields list Yes The questions. A section with none gives a warning.
    collapsed true or false Yes in the model Whether it starts collapsed. Use false.
    visibleWhen condition No Show the section only when a condition holds.

    A question (field):

    Property Type Required Meaning
    id text Yes in the model Unique inside the template.
    label text Yes (checked) The question as the pathologist sees it.
    type text Yes (checked) One of dropdown, radio, checkboxes, numeric, text, longtext, partGrid, spatialStageCanvas. Anything else is refused.
    required true or false Yes in the model Always answered.
    snomed, icd text Yes in the model Codes for the question itself; use "" when none.
    options list Yes in the model The answers of a dropdown, radio or checkboxes question; [] for the others.
    hint text No Helper text.
    unit text No For a numeric question.
    wholeNumber true or false No A count: a whole number, 0 or more.
    notMoreThan field id No A numeric question this one cannot exceed.
    visibleWhen condition No Show only when a condition holds.
    requiredIf condition No Required only when a condition holds.
    narrativeSentenceTemplate text with {value} No The narrative sentence.
    clinicalTier text No tier_1_diagnostic_category or tier_2_descriptive.

    An option: id, label, snomed, icd (each text, "" when none) and optionally narrativePhrase.

    A condition: { "fieldId": "<id of the triggering question>", "answerId": "<id of the option>" }. For several answers use "answerIds": ["a","b"], and "answerId": "" with "notAnswerIds": [...] for "unless". or holds a list of further conditions.

    Only the properties marked "checked" are verified on import. A missing id, collapsed, options or required is not reported by the import check, and a file like that may import and then behave badly in the editor. Always include them. Whether a question without an id can be edited cleanly is not verified.

    # C3. A minimal file

    This is the smallest file that passes the check: one section, one question.

    {
  "id": "tmpl-example-min",
  "name": "Example: minimal checklist",
  "source": "Custom",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "category": "OTHER",
  "sections": [
    {
      "id": "s1",
      "title": "Specimen",
      "collapsed": false,
      "fields": [
        {
          "id": "f1",
          "label": "Specimen adequacy",
          "type": "radio",
          "required": true,
          "snomed": "",
          "icd": "",
          "options": [
            { "id": "o1", "label": "Satisfactory", "snomed": "", "icd": "" },
            { "id": "o2", "label": "Unsatisfactory", "snomed": "", "icd": "" }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

    # C4. A fuller file

    This example shows the export wrapper, two sections, every common question type, answer-level codes, a count rule, a visibility condition and narrative text. The SNOMED CT and ICD codes are placeholders for illustration. Replace them with codes your clinical lead has checked; PathScribe does not validate them on import.

    {
  "format": "pathscribe-synoptic-protocol",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "exportedAt": "2026-10-26T12:00:00.000Z",
  "protocol": {
    "id": "tmpl-example-full",
    "name": "Example: colon resection (illustration only)",
    "source": "Custom",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "category": "COLON",
    "status": "draft"
  },
  "template": {
    "id": "tmpl-example-full",
    "name": "Example: colon resection (illustration only)",
    "source": "Custom",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "category": "COLON",
    "ajccEdition": "AJCC 8th",
    "sections": [
      {
        "id": "s-specimen",
        "title": "Specimen",
        "collapsed": false,
        "fields": [
          {
            "id": "f-procedure",
            "label": "Procedure",
            "type": "dropdown",
            "required": true,
            "snomed": "",
            "icd": "",
            "hint": "As stated on the requisition.",
            "options": [
              { "id": "o-right", "label": "Right hemicolectomy", "snomed": "", "icd": "" },
              { "id": "o-left", "label": "Left hemicolectomy", "snomed": "", "icd": "" },
              { "id": "o-other", "label": "Other", "snomed": "", "icd": "" }
            ]
          },
          {
            "id": "f-other-text",
            "label": "Other procedure (specify)",
            "type": "text",
            "required": false,
            "snomed": "",
            "icd": "",
            "options": [],
            "visibleWhen": { "fieldId": "f-procedure", "answerId": "o-other" }
          },
          {
            "id": "f-length",
            "label": "Specimen length",
            "type": "numeric",
            "unit": "cm",
            "required": false,
            "snomed": "",
            "icd": "",
            "options": []
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "id": "s-tumour",
        "title": "Tumour",
        "collapsed": false,
        "fields": [
          {
            "id": "f-histology",
            "label": "Histologic type",
            "type": "dropdown",
            "required": true,
            "snomed": "363346000",
            "icd": "C18.9",
            "clinicalTier": "tier_1_diagnostic_category",
            "narrativeSentenceTemplate": "The tumour is {value}.",
            "options": [
              { "id": "o-adeno", "label": "Adenocarcinoma", "snomed": "413448000", "icd": "C18.9", "narrativePhrase": "an adenocarcinoma" },
              { "id": "o-muc", "label": "Mucinous adenocarcinoma", "snomed": "", "icd": "", "narrativePhrase": "a mucinous adenocarcinoma" },
              { "id": "o-na", "label": "Not specified", "snomed": "", "icd": "" }
            ]
          },
          {
            "id": "f-nodes-examined",
            "label": "Lymph nodes examined",
            "type": "numeric",
            "wholeNumber": true,
            "required": true,
            "snomed": "",
            "icd": "",
            "options": []
          },
          {
            "id": "f-nodes-positive",
            "label": "Lymph nodes positive",
            "type": "numeric",
            "wholeNumber": true,
            "notMoreThan": "f-nodes-examined",
            "required": true,
            "snomed": "",
            "icd": "",
            "options": []
          },
          {
            "id": "f-margins",
            "label": "Margins involved",
            "type": "checkboxes",
            "required": false,
            "snomed": "",

              { "id": "o-prox", "label": "Proximal", "snomed": "", "icd": "" },
              { "id": "o-dist", "label": "Distal", "snomed": "", "icd": "" },

}

    Check that the example behaves as intended: the question "Other procedure (specify)" shows only when "Other" is chosen; "Lymph nodes positive" cannot exceed "Lymph nodes examined" and both must be whole numbers; the narrative sentence puts the chosen phrase where {value} is.

    # C5. Import a JSON file

    Home › Configuration › Synoptic Library › Upload Protocol

    Permission: config:protocol:draft.

    1. Open Synoptic Library > Active Protocols, Review Queue or All Protocols, and select Upload Protocol.
    2. In the window "Upload Protocol", choose the Governing Body: CAP, RCPath, ICCR, RCPA or Other. It becomes the draft's source (RCPA and Other are stored as Custom).
    3. Drop the file on the drop zone, or click it to browse. A line "Checking the file…" shows, then the result.
    4. Read the result. "Format checked: no problems found" and "PathScribe protocol with N sections and M questions. It can be imported as a draft." means you can go on. "Format checked: problems found" lists each problem (see C6); fix the file, then choose it again.
    5. Select Import as draft →. The window says "<name>" was saved as a draft. Open it in Protocols to edit it, then submit it for review.
    6. Open All Protocols, find the draft (filter Draft), select Open Editor, check it with 👁 Preview, make any changes, Save Draft, then Submit for Review.

    Importing never publishes anything. An imported protocol must go through review and approval like any other.

    # C6. Errors and warnings from the check

    Home › Configuration › Synoptic Library › Upload Protocol
    Message in the window Cause What to do
    The file is empty. Zero bytes. Choose the right file.
    The file is larger than 10 MB. Over the size limit. A protocol export is well under 1 MB; a larger file is probably the wrong file.
    This file type is not supported. Use JSON, XML or XLSX. Another extension. Save as .json.
    The file is not valid JSON. A missing comma or quote, a trailing comma, or smart quotes from a word processor. Paste it into a JSON checker or open it in a code editor, fix the marked line.
    This JSON is not a PathScribe protocol (a protocol has a list of sections). There is no sections list, or the file is a list instead of an object. Use the layouts in C2.
    This file was exported by a newer version of PathScribe (format N). formatVersion is above 1. Export again from this PathScribe, or lower the number only if you know the layout is unchanged.
    The protocol has no name. name is blank. Add a name.
    The protocol has no sections. sections is empty. Add at least one section.
    Section N has no title. A section's title is blank. Add the title.
    Section N has no questions. (a warning) fields is empty. Add questions or remove the section; the file can still import.
    Section N, question M has no label. A question's label is blank. Add the label.
    Section N, question M has an unknown question type. type is not one of the eight allowed values (lower case, exact). Use dropdown, radio, checkboxes, numeric, text, longtext, partGrid or spatialStageCanvas.
    The file is not well-formed XML. / No questions were found in the file. XML file problems. An XML form can be checked but not imported.
    The file is not an Excel workbook. / The sheets were not read… XLSX file problems. A workbook can be checked but not imported.
    A protocol with this name already exists. Rename it in the file, or archive the existing one, and choose the file again. Name clash with a non-archived protocol. Change name.
    The draft could not be saved. Drafting protocols needs the Template Author role. Missing config:protocol:draft. Ask an administrator to grant the capability (Staff, Roles).

    Section and question numbers count from 1 in the order they appear in the file.

    # C7. What the import does not check

    Be aware of these gaps when you write a file by hand. They are not reported by the import and are caught, if at all, only later in the editor or at sign-out.

    • Whether id values exist and are unique.
    • Whether a visibleWhen or requiredIf condition points at a question and an answer that exist.
    • Whether a dropdown, radio or checkbox question has any options.
    • Whether SNOMED CT and ICD codes are real, current, or match the label.
    • Whether the content matches the CAP or RCPath protocol it claims to follow.
    • Whether version, category and source use the expected values.

    After every import, open the draft in the editor and use 👁 Preview and the Readiness and Coding Coverage panels before you submit it.

    # Part D: Scheduling reports and report delivery

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance

    "Scheduling reports" means three different things in PathScribe. Choose the one you need.

    You want to Use Status
    Decide where each released patient report goes (result message, print, fax, file drop) Delivery Configuration Rules (D1) Built
    Decide when feeds go out (report delivery, billing, registries and so on) Delivery Schedules (D3) Partial
    Run a saved search report every day, week or month for named recipients Saved-report schedules (D4) Demonstration: nothing is delivered

    Billing and registry schedules are covered with the Registry feed in D3 and in Chapter 11.

    # D1. Choose where released reports go (Delivery Configuration Rules)

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance › Delivery Configuration Rules

    Permission to change: config:delivery-rules:manage (Admin and Lab Director). Reference: Delivery Configuration Rules.

    1. Open the Configuration tab System, group Administration & Compliance, then Delivery Configuration Rules.
    2. Select Add Rule.
    3. Choose the cases the rule covers. Every criterion is optional: Provider, Ordering Facility, Patient Location (Point of Care) and Report Type (Preliminary, Final, Corrected, Addendum). The more criteria that match, the stronger the rule. A rule with none set matches every case but only as the lowest priority, and the window warns you.
    4. For each channel, choose Off, Primary, Secondary or Fallback. The channels are Electronic (result message to the interface engine), Print, E-fax and File drop. Primary and secondary go at once. A fallback goes only when a primary print, fax or file drop has nowhere to go or still fails after its retries.
    5. If E-fax is on, type the Fax number (7 to 15 digits, optional leading +), or leave it blank to fax the ordering physician, or the ordering facility if there is no physician number.
    6. If File drop is on, type the File-drop target, the name of the target as set up on the interface server. The folder or SFTP address and sign-in details are kept on the server, not in PathScribe.
    7. Optionally type a Note. Save the rule.
    8. Test it. In Test Delivery Resolution, choose a Provider, Ordering Facility, Patient Location and Report Type, then select Resolve. The result shows the matched rule, the action (Electronic Only, Print Only, Dual Delivery, Suppress) and the channel plan.
    9. To set automatic retries, type the minutes to wait before each try in Automatic retries: wait before each (minutes), for example 1, 5, 15. Each wait is from 1 to 1,440 minutes and you may list up to 10. Select Save retries. After the last try the delivery goes to the delivery exceptions, Admin and Lab Director are sent a message, and the rule's fallback channels are used. Leave it blank for no retries.

    The window refuses: a fallback with no primary ("A fallback needs a primary channel to fall back from"), a fax number that is not 7 to 15 digits, and a file drop with no target. When no rule matches, the report goes Electronic Only.

    To undo: edit the rule or delete it. Reports already sent are not recalled.

    # D2. Choose the printer for the print channel

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance › Print Destination Routing Rules

    A delivery rule with the Print channel creates a print job. The printer comes from Print Destination Routing Rules, otherwise the facility's own default destination. Set these rules before turning Print on in a delivery rule. The Add rule window and the Test Print Destination Resolution panel work like those in D1.

    # D3. Set when feeds go out (Delivery Schedules)

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance › Delivery Schedules

    Permission to change: config:delivery-schedules:manage (Admin and Lab Director). The schedule is stored and evaluated, and the outbound queue shows each item's scheduled time and reporting-deadline flag, but the production server must apply the same rules before handing an item on. A browser or development build does not hold a send until its time. Reference: Delivery Schedules.

    1. Open the Configuration tab System, group Administration & Compliance, then Delivery Schedules.
    2. In Schedules for, choose "Whole enterprise" or one performing facility.
    3. Find the feed's card. The feeds are Report delivery, Billing delivery, Results feed, Admissions feed (ADT), Accession feed, LIS sync and one card for each Registry. A card reads "No schedule set: sent immediately", "Follows the enterprise schedule" or "Set for this facility".
    4. Select Edit (for a facility, Set for this facility first).
    5. Under How it goes out, choose one: - Send immediately. - Only during set hours. Add rows of Days, From and Until (24-hour). Each must end after it starts on the same day. - In a batch at set times. Choose How often (Every day, Weekly or Monthly). For weekly, tick the Batch days. For monthly, type the Days of the month (1 to 28). Type the Batch times, for example 06:00, 22:00. Optionally type a Cutoff time: items signed out after it on a run day wait for the next run. - Hold until final sign-out. - At sign-out after a review hold. Type the Review hold in minutes (1 to 10,080). Match it to your quality review and amendment window.
    6. Optionally type Days with no sending as dates, for example 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01. This applies to set hours and batch schedules.
    7. Choose the Time zone as an IANA name, for example America/New_York. All times are read in this zone.
    8. Optionally type a Reporting deadline in days from sign-out (1 to 3,650). The queue flags cases within 3 days of it or past it. Registries often need this.
    9. Decide whether An amendment puts the item back in the queue. It is on by default for registries.
    10. Select Save schedule. It is refused if a required value is missing or invalid, or if you lack the capability.
    11. Test it with Try a schedule: choose the Feed, optionally a performing facility, the Registry for the Registry feed, and the Date and time; say whether the case is finally signed out and when. Select Check. It answers "It goes out" or "It waits", with the reason and the next opportunity.

    For a facility to go back to the enterprise schedule, select Follow the enterprise on its card.

    Registry destinations, required fields, go-live approval and transport belong to each registry's own setup, not to this schedule. A registry with no schedule holds each item 240 minutes after sign-out, and an amendment re-queues it.

    # D4. Schedule a saved report (Search > Report > Schedules)

    Home › Search › Report › Schedules

    Permission: search:report-schedule:manage. This is a user feature: the person who owns the saved report schedules it. An administrator sets it up for a person by granting that capability and teaching these steps.

    Nothing is delivered yet. A schedule is stored, and Run now (Simulated) builds the report and records its counts, but nothing is emailed or filed. Do not rely on a schedule to reach anyone.

    1. Open Search, run a search and select Report. Group the cases, choose the columns, then save the report with a name. A schedule runs a saved report; with none saved the panel says "Save a report first".
    2. Select Schedules.
    3. Under New schedule, choose the saved report from "Choose a saved report…".
    4. Choose how often: daily, weekly or monthly. For weekly, set the Day of the week. For monthly, set the Day of the month (1 to 28). Set the time of day.
    5. Optionally tick "Cover the most recent days each run, instead of the saved dates", then set Days to cover (1 to 366). Leave it unticked to use the dates saved with the report.
    6. Tick the people under "Recipients": the label shows how many you chose out of the most allowed (20). PathScribe compares each person's access with the report ("Checking what each recipient can see…"). If someone cannot see every case, you are asked to narrow the report for them or skip them; PathScribe does not choose for you.
    7. Select the create button. Each schedule is listed with its pattern, "Covers the last … days", the number of recipients and the next run. A person may hold up to 25 schedules.
    8. Use Run now (Simulated) to test, Pause (then Resume) to stop temporarily, and Delete to remove.

    A schedule shows "Not run yet" before its first run and "Last run failed: …" with the reason when a run fails. "The schedule could not be saved." means the form was refused for a reason not named; check each box and try again.

    # What is not covered, and what to check

    Home › Configuration
    • No import for report templates or parts. Only synoptic templates have a file format.
    • No review step for report templates. They go Draft, Published, Archived, with no second approver (unlike synoptic templates).
    • Not verified here: how editing a published report template in place affects reports that are open; whether a part archived after a template uses it still prints; how a question with no id behaves in the editor; the exact shape of the production server's response for any save.
    • Scheduled report delivery. Saved-report schedules do not deliver. Delivery Schedules are partly applied by the browser build.
    • Content is never verified against CAP or RCPath. A reviewer must compare the protocol to the governing body's current published version.
    • Translations. This chapter is written in English. The French, German, Dutch, Korean and Spanish editions do not yet contain it.

    # Step-by-step procedures: labels, billing and charge capture

    This chapter is a set of numbered procedures. The screen chapters (Chapter 2 for labels and printers, Chapter 8 for billing and registries) say what each field means; this chapter says what to click, in what order, what you should see, and how to undo it. Each procedure names the screen it uses, so you can jump to the field reference when you need it.

    Read these four points first.

    1. Status. Every screen used here is Built or Demonstration as its own chapter says. Today most data services are browser-held demonstration services; the production API is connected service by service. A step that works in the demonstration may not yet be backed by the production server.
    2. Two people for billing tables. Billing rules, the RVU Code Map, the CPT Modifier Dictionary and NCCI Edit Rules never take effect on their own. Whoever saves a change submits it, and a different person with approval rights approves it on Pending Billing Rule Approvals. On a one-person system nobody can approve, so plan for a second approver before you start (see Approve or reject a change).
    3. Things that do not exist. There is no fee schedule or price field anywhere in the billing rules, no way to copy a label layout from one label type to another, and no MIPS or MACRA reporting. Each is marked Not built where it comes up, with the nearest thing that does exist.
    4. Permissions. Each procedure lists the capability it needs. If a button is greyed out, you do not hold the capability. Who holds it by default is in the Permissions part of the screen's own section.

    # Part A: Labels

    Home › Configuration › System › Workstation & Hardware › Label Designer

    PathScribe has nine label types: Requisition, Specimen (Container), Block (Cassette), Slide, Decant Container, Molecular Specimen, Molecular Plate, Molecular Rack and Molecular Deck Location. A layout is where each field sits on one label type, in millimetres, on a label of fixed size. The size cannot be changed.

    How a layout is used, so you know what you are changing:

    • A layout is kept per label type. There is one Enterprise Default for each type. Only Requisition, Specimen and Decant Container also allow a facility override. Block, Slide and the four Molecular types show Enterprise Standard: Locked and can be edited only at the enterprise default, because every site must print the same physical format for cassette, slide and instrument hardware.
    • When a label prints, PathScribe uses the facility override if one exists and is allowed, otherwise the Enterprise Default, otherwise the built-in layout. A saved layout with no fields placed counts as no layout, so the built-in layout is used.
    • The print paths for all nine label types read the saved layout this way. Printing a label for a real case shows the layout you saved, not only the preview.
    • The designer previews with sample values (for example patient name Maria Garcia, accession DVMC26-0001). It is not a live case.

    Permission: opening the screen needs screen:configuration:open. Save, reset and restore need config:label-layouts:manage (high risk, audited). Reference: Label Designer.

    # Open the Label Designer and choose what to edit

    Home › Configuration › System › Workstation & Hardware › Label Designer
    1. Select Configuration from Home, then the System tab.
    2. In the group Workstation & Hardware, select Label Designer.
    3. In Label Type, choose the label. The canvas resizes to that label's fixed size, and the caption under it shows the size, for example "50.8mm × 25.4mm — live preview using sample data".
    4. Look at the Scope control next to it. - For Requisition, Specimen and Decant it offers Enterprise Default and one "(facility name) (override)" entry per active facility. - For every other type it shows Enterprise Standard: Locked instead of a choice, and you edit the enterprise default.
    5. Choose the scope you want to edit.

    Expected result: the canvas shows the saved layout for that type and scope, or is empty if none has been saved.

    Be careful: changing Label Type, or Scope, replaces what is on the canvas with the saved layout for the new choice, with no warning. Changing Label Type also puts Scope back to Enterprise Default. Save before you switch.

    # Create a layout from nothing

    Home › Configuration › System › Workstation & Hardware › Label Designer

    Use this when a label type has no saved layout yet (the canvas is empty and Available Fields lists every field).

    1. Open the Label Designer and choose the label type and scope.
    2. Under Available Fields, drag a field onto the canvas where you want it. Fields you have already placed disappear from the list, so a field cannot be placed twice. When none are left the list says "All fields placed."
    3. Drag a placed field to move it. It keeps the point where you grabbed it, and it stops at the label's edge.
    4. Click a placed field to select it. Eight handles appear on it (hover text "Drag to resize"). Drag a handle to resize. Handles show only on the selected field.
    5. For an exact position, use the Inspector panel on the right: X (mm), Y (mm), Width (mm), Height (mm) and Font Size (mm). Type a number and move out of the box. Values are kept inside the label.
    6. The barcode field draws a real sample barcode at the label type's symbology. If the sample cannot be drawn the field shows "barcode render failed" instead; the layout can still be saved.
    7. If any field goes past the label edge it is outlined, and a warning reads "N field(s) go past the edge of the label and would print off it." Select Fit to label to bring every field inside.
    8. Select Save Layout.

    Expected result: a message under the buttons. "Enterprise default saved." when you edited the enterprise default, "Facility override saved." when you edited a facility override. If a field is past the edge the message is "Not saved: a field goes past the edge of the label. Use “Fit to label”, or move or resize it." and nothing is saved.

    To undo: use Version history to restore an earlier version, or Reset to Default to remove the layout.

    # Edit an existing layout

    Home › Configuration › System › Workstation & Hardware › Label Designer
    1. Open the Label Designer and choose the label type and scope you want to change. The saved layout loads.
    2. To change a field, click it on the canvas, then move it, resize it, or use the Inspector.
    3. To remove a field, select it and choose Remove Field. It returns to Available Fields.
    4. To add a field, drag it from Available Fields.
    5. Select Save Layout. Every save is kept as a new version, with who saved it and when.

    Expected result: "Enterprise default saved." or "Facility override saved." The next label printed for that type and facility uses the new layout.

    To undo: restore the previous version.

    # Make a facility override from the enterprise default (copy)

    Home › Configuration › System › Workstation & Hardware › Label Designer

    This is the one way to copy a layout. It works only for Requisition, Specimen and Decant Container labels.

    1. Open the Label Designer and choose one of those three label types.
    2. In Scope, choose the facility, shown as "(facility name) (override)".
    3. If that facility has no override yet, the canvas opens with the enterprise default's layout. This is the starting copy.
    4. Change whatever the facility needs. Leave the rest alone.
    5. Select Save Layout. The message is "Facility override saved."

    Expected result: the facility now has its own layout, separate from the enterprise default. A later change to the enterprise default does not change it, and a facility with no override keeps following the enterprise default.

    To go back to following the enterprise default: choose that facility's scope and select Reset to Default (see below).

    What cannot be copied. There is no copy between two facilities, no copy between two label types, and no export or import of a layout as a file. A layout belongs to one label type, and each type offers its own list of fields. To build a second facility's layout, start from the enterprise default as above, or place the fields again by hand. Not built: a facility-to-facility or type-to-type copy.

    # Show a field only when another field has a value

    Home › Configuration › System › Workstation & Hardware › Label Designer

    Use this to hide a line when its data is missing, for example the referring provider on a label.

    1. Open the layout and click the field you want to make conditional.
    2. In the Inspector, find Show this field. It shows Always. Open it and choose the other field to test. The barcode and the field itself are not offered.
    3. A second choice appears. Choose one of: - when that field has a value - when that field is empty - when that field equals, then type the Value to match (matching ignores upper and lower case).
    4. To see how the label prints when the tested field is empty, tick Preview with that field empty. This changes the preview only.
    5. Select Save Layout.

    To undo: set Show this field back to Always.

    # Version history, restore, and reset

    Home › Configuration › System › Workstation & Hardware › Label Designer

    See and restore a version.

    1. Choose the label type and scope.
    2. Select Version history. The list is headed "Saved versions of this layout". Each row reads "Version N, saved (when) by (who)". A layout never saved shows "This layout has not been saved yet."
    3. Select Restore this version on the row you want.

    Expected result: "Version restored and saved as the newest version." The restore is itself a new version, so the old versions stay. The designer keeps the 20 most recent versions of each layout.

    Reset to Default. Select Reset to Default to remove the saved layout for the chosen type and scope. The canvas clears and the message is "Layout reset to default." Printing then uses the next level: for a facility override, the enterprise default; for an enterprise default, the built-in layout. Reset needs config:label-layouts:manage.

    # Export printer code and test the label

    Home › Configuration › System › Workstation & Hardware › Label Designer

    Use this to check that a layout fits and scans before you trust it, without printing on a real label.

    1. Open the layout (saved or not). The export uses what is on the canvas, so you do not have to save first.
    2. Select Export ZPL, Export EPL or Export DPL. A box appears headed Exported ZPL. It carries this heading for all three languages; read the note above the text to see which language it holds.
    3. Select the text and copy it.
    4. For ZPL, open the viewer named on the screen (labelary.com/viewer.html), set 203 dpi (8 dpmm) and the label size shown, and paste. Check that every field is on the label and the barcode scans.
    5. Or send the code to your own printer yourself.

    Things to know:

    • ZPL is the language PathScribe sends to printers (through QZ Tray). EPL and DPL are export text only. PathScribe never sends them to a printer; the screen says the text is a starting point and barcode commands differ a little between printer models.
    • The barcode in the export is a sample value, not a real case's barcode. The export confirms fit and general scannability, not the exact encoding of a real label (for example a real GS1 GTIN for cassettes and slides).

    # Send labels to the right printer

    Home › Configuration › System › Workstation & Hardware › Print Settings

    A layout decides what is on the label. Printer settings decide where it prints. Set up the printer once, then test.

    1. Register the printer on Printer Profiles: select + Add Printer Profile, enter the Printer ID, Model, Bridge Type, DPI and the other fields, and save. Only the QZ Tray bridge sends labels directly today. Any other bridge falls back to the browser print dialog.
    2. Open Print Settings (Configuration > System > Workstation & Hardware > Print Settings).
    3. To change one facility only: in the facility selector, choose the facility, then select + Create Facility Override. This copies the system default so the facility can differ. Until you do, the facility shows the default and is read-only.
    4. Under the printer profile pickers, choose the profile for Container Label Printer Profile, Molecular Label Printer Profile and Requisition Label Printer Profile. Each control saves as you change it. With no profile chosen the label goes to the browser print dialog ("Use browser print dialog").
    5. For cassette and slide labels, set the label face (width, height, barcode module size, text height) and the GS1 GTIN. Without a GTIN each real GS1 print is refused with an error. The fit check under each shows a warning when the barcode or text will not fit.
    6. Select Send Test Print, choose a profile, and hold the printed label against a real cassette, container or slide before use.

    Expected result: a test label prints through the chosen profile. If a field is cut off, adjust the layout in the Label Designer or the face size in Print Settings and test again.

    Permission: Print Settings changes need config:print-settings:manage; printer profiles need config:printers:manage.

    # Reprint labels for many cases

    Home › Batch Management › Label reprint
    1. Open Batch Management from Home and select the Label reprint tile ("Reprint labels for many cases at once").
    2. Enter at least one of Accessioned from, Accessioned to, Accession number from, Accession number to. With all four empty, no cases are found ("No cases match. Enter a date range or an accession number range.").
    3. Select Find cases. The list shows each case, oldest first, with a Reprint tick box and its specimens ("N cases found; N selected").
    4. Under Labels, tick Cassettes, Specimen containers and/or Requisition.
    5. If you ticked Cassettes, choose the Cassette printer. Without one the screen says "Choose the cassette printer first."
    6. Select Reprint labels. Labels print one at a time, about a quarter of a second apart, with a "Printing N of M…" counter.
    7. When it ends, read the summary: "Printed N; failed N; blocked by the on-demand guardrail N." Select Retry N failed labels to try the failures again.

    Every label is audited. The permission is label:batch:reprint (Histotechnologist and Admin hold it by default). Without it the screen says "You don’t have permission to reprint labels in a batch." Reference: Batch Management.

    # Part B: Billing and charge capture

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups

    The order matters, because later screens read earlier ones. Work in this order the first time:

    1. RVU Code Map and CPT Modifier Dictionary: the lists the billing rules pick from.
    2. Billing Dictionary: the billing rules.
    3. NCCI Edit Rules: bundling pairs.
    4. Pending Billing Rule Approvals: a second person approves steps 1 to 3.
    5. Charge Release Triggers and Billing Release: when a charge is created and when it is released.
    6. Master Payment Type Dictionary and Jurisdiction Payment Mapping: who pays.
    7. Billing Export Preview: check what a real case would send.

    All of these live under Configuration > System and need screen:configuration:open; Billing Release is in the group Administration & Compliance, the others in Financial & Revenue Lookups.

    What PathScribe does with a charge. At final sign-out it resolves each charge once into a fixed record: CPT or HCPCS code, relative value units (RVU) and modifier. Later edits to a rule do not change a charge already made. Fee schedules: Not built. There is no price, dollar amount or payer rate field. Your billing system or the interface engine works out reimbursement. The nearest things are the RVU values on a rule and in the RVU Code Map.
