    Auto-coding is not set up on a screen. The suggested codes (special stains, immunohistochemistry, frozen sections) come from rules built into the product, and a person always confirms them. The only screen that touches the nearest setting is Smart Capture. Base specimen codes (88302, 88305, 88309) are not worked out automatically. See Auto-coding and billing hold rules.

    # Add a code to the RVU Code Map

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups › RVU Code Map

    Capability: config:billing-rvu:manage. Approval needs config:billing-tables:approve.

    1. Open RVU Code Map. The Active version table lists the codes; Search narrows it.
    2. Select + Add Code. The window is headed "Add Code".
    3. Enter Code (for example 88305) and Billing Code (placeholder "Often same as Code"). Both are required.
    4. Choose Level (Specimen, Block, Stain or Decant) and Component Type (TC, 26 or Global). The Component Type decides when the charge is created: TC at specimen grossing complete, 26 and Global at case sign-out.
    5. Optionally enter Description, HCPCS Code and the Work RVU, RVU — Practice Expense and RVU — Malpractice values. Leave Work RVU blank if you have not verified it; the row then shows Unverified. A Work RVU must be a positive number.
    6. Select Submit for Approval.

    Expected result: a message "(code) submitted for approval — see Pending Billing Rule Approvals." A code that already exists in the active version is refused ("Code (code) already exists in the active version."). The change does not apply until a second person approves it.

    To undo: before approval, the second person rejects it. After approval, edit the code and submit again.

    # Edit or bulk-load the RVU Code Map

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups › RVU Code Map

    Edit one code.

    1. In the Active version table, select Edit on the row. The window is headed "Edit — (code)". Code and Billing Code are locked.
    2. Change the other fields and select Submit for Approval.

    Load many codes from a file.

    1. Select Download Template, fill it in a spreadsheet and save it as .csv. Columns are Code (or HCPCS), Description and WorkRVU.
    2. Select Upload Spreadsheet and choose the file. A file that is not .csv is refused with a message telling you to save it as CSV. A file with no usable rows says "No real rows found in this file - check it has Code and WorkRVU columns."
    3. The window Review before saving shows the codes found. Only payable codes load; the screen tells you how many non-payable or modifier rows it skipped.
    4. Enter a Version label and an Effective date.
    5. Select Submit for Approval (N codes).

    Expected result: "(label) submitted for approval". The whole file becomes one pending version. Uploaded rows get their level guessed from the description (specimen if unclear) and billing type Global; check them after approval. Older versions stay under the older-versions toggle with their status (Approved (superseded), Pending approval, Rejected).

    # Edit or upload the CPT Modifier Dictionary

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups › CPT Modifier Dictionary

    Capability: config:billing-modifiers:manage. The dictionary is a reference list only. PathScribe sets the modifier from the billing type (TC takes -TC, 26 takes -26, Global none). It does not check or add any other modifier.

    Change one description.

    1. Select Edit on a modifier row. The window is headed "Edit — (code)".
    2. Change the Description and select Submit for Approval.

    Replace the list from a file.

    1. Select Download Template, fill in Code and Description, save as .csv.
    2. Select Upload Spreadsheet and choose the file. The window "Import Modifier Dictionary — (file name)" shows the rows read.
    3. Enter a Version Label and Effective From (a valid date is required).
    4. Tick I confirm my organization holds a real, current AMA license covering these modifier descriptions. The upload does not go ahead without it, and says "Confirm you hold a real, current AMA license for these modifier descriptions before importing."
    5. Select Submit for Approval.

    Expected result: a pending version waits for a second person. The shipped descriptions are placeholders (marked synthetic); the American Medical Association text is licensed, so only load your own text if you hold the licence.

    # Create a billing rule

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups › Billing Dictionary

    Capability: config:billing-rules:manage. Prerequisite: the CPT code exists in the RVU Code Map. The CPT picker reads that map, and an empty map gives an empty picker.

    1. Open Billing Dictionary. The table lists each billing code's current rule for the scope in Viewing. Viewing starts on Enterprise-Wide; choose a site to see or add that site's rules.
    2. Select + Add Billing Code. The window is headed "New Billing Code", with two tabs: Billing & RVU and Coding Rules.
    3. On Billing & RVU, enter Billing Code (for example IHC-FIRST), choose Scope (Enterprise or a site), and optionally Country.
    4. Choose the CPT Code by searching the RVU Code Map entries. Optionally search an HCPCS Code.
    5. Choose Level (Specimen, Block, Stain or Decant) and Component Type (TC, 26 or Global). Enter Description. Enter the RVU — Work, RVU — Practice Expense and RVU — Malpractice values, or leave RVU — Work blank if unverified ("Never fabricated — leave blank if unverified.").
    6. Enter Effective From. Optionally add Notes.
    7. On the Coding Rules tab, add any reminders: Modifiers Commonly Associated, Quantity Rule, Bundling Rule, Documentation Requirements, Suppression Advisory. These are stored for audit and the billing system only. PathScribe never validates, enforces or suppresses a charge because of them.
    8. Select Create Billing Code.

    Expected result: the rule is saved as version 1 with status DRAFT. A DRAFT is not used. Continue with Submit a rule for approval.

    # Submit a rule for approval

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups › Billing Dictionary
    1. On the rule's row, select History. The window is headed "Version History — (code) ((scope))" and lists every version with its status.
    2. On the DRAFT row, select Submit for Approval.

    Expected result: the status becomes PENDING_APPROVAL, and the audit log records "Billing rule submitted for approval". The rule now waits on Pending Billing Rule Approvals. The statuses a version can have are DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL, ACTIVE, REJECTED and RETIRED.

    # Change a rule: a new version

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups › Billing Dictionary

    Versions are only ever added; you never overwrite one.

    1. Make sure Viewing is the scope you want to change (Enterprise-Wide or a site).
    2. On the rule's row select New Version. The window is headed "New Version — (code) ((scope), v(N))" and is filled from the latest version. (A row marked Inherited has no rule of its own at that site; it shows no New Version button. Use Duplicate to give the site its own.)
    3. Change the fields. Change Reason is required when the scope already has versions.
    4. Select Create New Version. It saves as DRAFT.
    5. Submit it for approval.

    Expected result: when a second person approves it, the new version becomes ACTIVE and the version it replaces ends. Charges already created keep the values they were made with.

    # Copy a rule, or give one site its own rule

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups › Billing Dictionary

    Duplicate copies a rule into a new billing code, a different site, or both. It is how you start from an existing rule.

    1. On the rule's row select Duplicate. (You can also select History, then Duplicate on a version row to copy an older version.) The window is headed "Duplicate — (code) ((scope), v(N))" and is filled from the rule.
    2. Change Billing Code, Scope, or both. To give a site its own version of an enterprise rule, keep the code and choose the site as Scope. When the code or scope changes, the window explains "This will create a real, new, independent version 1 for this billing code + scope combination".
    3. Change any other fields, enter Effective From and Change Reason if asked.
    4. Select Save Duplicate. It saves as DRAFT.
    5. Submit it for approval.

    Expected result: at that site, the site rule replaces the enterprise rule (Scope on the row shows Site Override instead of Inherited).

    # Retire a rule

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups › Billing Dictionary
    1. On the rule's row select History.
    2. On the ACTIVE version, select Retire. There is no confirmation window.

    Expected result: the status changes to RETIRED. Retire is offered only on an ACTIVE version. If a site override is retired, that site goes back to the enterprise rule (shown as Inherited). To bring a retired rule back, create a new version or duplicate it and approve it.

    # Approve or reject a change

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups › Pending Billing Rule Approvals

    Capability: config:billing-tables:approve. The person who drafted or submitted a change cannot approve it (Four-Eyes Principle). That includes you if you submitted it: the button is locked and the hint reads "You drafted or submitted this change — a different reviewer is required (Four-Eyes Principle)."

    1. A different approver opens Pending Billing Rule Approvals. Two tables can show. Pending Billing Rule Approvals lists billing rule versions (billing code, CPT, RVU (Work), effective date, scope, drafted by, submitted by, change reason). Pending Dictionary Updates lists whole-table updates: modifier dictionary versions, NCCI imports, RVU Code Map versions and bulk code imports.
    2. Check the row. For a table update, the label tells you which upload it is.
    3. Select Approve to activate it, or Reject. Reject opens a box: enter a reason (required, "A real rejection reason is required.") and select Confirm Reject.

    Expected result: an approved item takes effect; a bulk code import applies the whole job. A rejected item ends, and its reason shows on the older-versions list of the screen it came from. Both decisions are audited.

    If nobody else can approve (a one-person system), the change stays pending. Grant config:billing-tables:approve to a second person in Roles.

    # Upload or edit NCCI bundling pairs

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups › NCCI Edit Rules (Bundling)

    Capability: config:billing-ncci:manage. No real National Correct Coding Initiative data ships. The seed is one synthetic pair, and the screen warns while it is active. The holder of the licensed CMS file loads it.

    1. Select Download Template, fill the columns Column 1, Column 2, Modifier Indicator (0, 1 or 9), Effective Date and Deletion Date, and save as .csv.
    2. Select Upload Spreadsheet and choose the file. Rows with a problem are skipped and listed ("N rows skipped:" with the row and reason: a missing code, an indicator other than 0, 1 or 9, or a missing effective date).
    3. Enter the Quarter Version (for example 2026Q3).
    4. Select Submit for Approval (N pairs).
    5. To change one pair, select Edit on its row, change the Modifier Indicator or Deletion Date, and select Submit for Approval. An edit sends the whole table again as a new pending import.

    Expected result: a pending import waits for approval. Only pairs with indicator 0 raise a deficiency at sign-out; 1 and 9 do not.

    # Set when each charge is created

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups › Charge Release Triggers (TC/26/Global)

    Capability: config:billing-triggers:manage. Defaults: TC (Technical Component) at Specimen grossed; 26 (Professional Component) and Global (Combined) at Case signed out.

    1. Open Charge Release Triggers. The selector shows "Viewing: Enterprise-Wide". To change one site only, choose "Viewing: (site name)". A site that already has an override is marked "(has override)".
    2. For each billing type, open the Releases At list and choose Specimen grossed or Case signed out. Each change saves at once, with "✓ Saved (scope)". There is no Save button.
    3. To undo, select Reset all to real default (enterprise) or Reset (site) to Enterprise-Wide (a site). The button is greyed out when there is no override.

    Expected result: only charges created from then on follow the new setting. Charges already made are not changed. Each change and reset is audited ("Charge release trigger changed", "Charge release triggers reset to default").

    # Add, edit or remove a billing release (hold) rule

    Home › Configuration › System › Administration & Compliance › Billing Release

    Capability: config:billing-release:manage. A release rule says what happens to a charge once it exists: release at once, hold it a set time, or release it in a scheduled batch. The most specific matching rule wins. When no rule matches, the charge is released at its milestone. PathScribe decides what and when; the interface engine moves the message.

    1. Open Billing Release. Rules for starts on Whole enterprise; choose a facility to see its own rules. A facility with none shows "This facility has no rules of its own and follows the enterprise rules."
    2. Select Add a rule. The window is headed "Billing release rule: (scope)".
    3. Under Applies to, choose Billing type (Any billing type, Technical component (TC), Professional component (-26), Global). Optionally enter Case types (specimen categories) separated by commas (empty means every case), choose an Ordering site, enter the Primary pathologist (ID), and choose Amendment reports (Original or amended, Original reports only, Amended reports only).
    4. Under Release, choose Release mode: - Release after a hold: enter Hold (minutes). A technical charge is counted from grossing, the others from final sign-out. 0 means at once. The limit is 30 days (43,200 minutes). - Release in a batch: choose How often (daily or weekly), the Batch days for weekly, the Batch times (24-hour, comma separated; a charge goes in the first batch after its milestone) and the Time zone. The window shows the same schedule as a cron line.
    5. Tick or clear Release automatically when due (clear it to keep charges until a person releases them from the Outbound Queue) and Park for review when the code is unmapped or the technical facility is missing.
    6. If the window shows a problem in red, fix it. Save rule stays greyed out until there are none. Possible problems: "Choose a billing type from the list.", "Choose a release mode.", "The hold must be a whole number of minutes, 0 or more, up to 30 days.", "A batch rule needs a batch schedule.", "Choose which reports the rule applies to.", "Case types can't be empty entries."
    7. Select Save rule. The screen shows "Saved." (or "Not saved." if it was refused).

    To change a rule select Edit; to delete one select Remove (no confirmation window). A charge from an amended report, a charge whose CPT is unmapped, and a split case with no technical facility are always parked for review, whatever the rules say.

    Test a rule before you rely on it. Under Try a charge, enter the Billing type of the charge, Case type, Performing facility, Charge generated (UTC), and tick whichever apply (From an amended report, A delta charge of the amendment, The CPT code is mapped, The technical-component facility is missing, The case is finally signed out, with Final sign-out (UTC)). Set Check at (UTC) and select Check. The result is Released, Waits, Waits for a person or Parked for review, with the rule that matched.

    # Add or change a payment type

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups › Master Payment Type Dictionary

    Capability: config:payment-types:manage. A payment type is a category of payer (self pay, commercial insurance, national health service). Eleven are seeded.

    1. Open Master Payment Type Dictionary.
    2. To add one, select + Add Payment Type. Enter Category ID (stored in capitals, spaces become underscores, for example SELF_PAY) and Display Name. Both are required, and a duplicate ID is refused (the Create button stays greyed out).
    3. Tick Requires Subscriber ID if staff must enter a policy number, and if so optionally enter its label (for example "NHS Number" or "Claim #"). Choose Requires Guarantor (Required, Optional or Not Required). Tick Supports Split Billing if technical and professional parts may go to different payers. Add Notes if you wish.
    4. Select Create.
    5. To edit, select Edit on a row, change the fields and select Save Changes. The Category ID is locked ("locked — referenced by Jurisdiction Mappings") because mappings point to it.
    6. To retire one, select Deactivate; to bring it back select Reactivate. Show inactive lists inactive rows too.

    Notes: there is no Duplicate button here. Deactivating a type is not checked against the mappings that use it, so check Jurisdiction Payment Mapping first.

    # Add or change a jurisdiction payment mapping

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups › Jurisdiction Payment Mapping

    Capability: config:payment-mappings:manage. A mapping ties a local payer scheme to one payment type. The Primary Jurisdiction selector on the accessioning Outside Patient Data tab reads these.

    1. Open Jurisdiction Payment Mapping. Use the country filter and Show inactive to find rows.
    2. Select + Add Mapping. Enter Country Code (for example US, UK, DE, CA_ON), Local Scheme Code (for example DE_GKV), Local Display Terminology (the local-language name), choose the Master Payment Type (only active types are offered), and enter Primary Outbound Format. All five are required. Add Notes if you wish.
    3. Select Create. Codes are stored in capitals.
    4. To change one, select Edit, change the fields and select Save Changes. To hide one from accessioning select Deactivate; to bring it back, Reactivate.

    Notes: nothing checks for a repeated country and scheme code. The Primary Outbound Format (for example X12 837P) is a label only. No file is generated; X12 837P, KVDT and SESAM-Vitale output are Planned.

    # Check what a case would send, and read the financial log

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups › Billing Export Preview

    Preview the charge payload. Capability config:interface-preview:view.

    1. Open Billing Export Preview and enter a case id or accession. The case must be finalised and have charges.
    2. Read the JSON payload. This is what PathScribe sends: the charge lines (CPT or HCPCS, RVU, modifier) and the financial class from the payment type and mapping. It carries no dollar amounts. The HL7 DFT^P03 preview beneath it is an illustration only; PathScribe does not build or send HL7.
    3. If the case has an open billing deficiency, the export is blocked until the deficiency is resolved. Send to billing engine goes to a simulated engine in the demonstration ("Simulated" badge).

    Find a billing event in the log. Capability screen:audit-log:open.

    1. Open System Logs and select the Financial tab, sub-tab Billing Logs.
    2. Filter by Case Number, Patient ID (MRN/MPI), Type (Charge, Credit, Deficiency, Code Review, Dispatch, Amendment, Audit), Status and the date ranges. Select Search. At most 50 cases show; "Case limit reached" appears when more match.
    3. To export the result select Export CSV (needs audit:billing-log:export).

    Fix a charge that failed to send. On the Outbound DLQ sub-tab, find the case in the Failed table. If the error is MISSING_ICD10 or MISSING_PROVIDER_NPI, use Fix & Retry (Save & Re-queue attaches the code or NPI to the case and re-queues it, and is audited). Use Retry Dispatch to try again, or Capture as CAPA to raise a deficiency. Simulate Timeout and Simulate Rejected are test buttons only. Real dispatch is not built.

    # Choose and approve a cancer registry

    Home › Configuration › System › Lab Materials & Workflows › Cancer Registry Reporting

    Capability: config:cancer-registry:manage. PathScribe builds one structured JSON payload for the chosen registry. It does not write NAACCR XML, COSD XML or any other registry file format; the interface engine translates and sends. Every cancer registry's specification is marked as not verified against the registry's own, so a person must confirm it. There is no Spain registry.

    Choose the registry.

    1. Open Cancer Registry Reporting.
    2. Set Enterprise Default registry. With none chosen, no cancer report is made.
    3. Optionally tick Honours opt-out. It is off by default; when off, a patient who opted out is still reported and the audit log records it.
    4. Select Save.
    5. For one facility that reports elsewhere, select + Add Override, choose the Facility and Registry, and Save. Remove takes the override away.

    Take a registry live.

    1. In the Registry (go-live) panel, choose the registry. Enter the Agreement reference for the data-sharing agreement and select Record agreement.
    2. On a validation instance, select Run test suite (needs registry:test-suite:run), then Export validation record. On a production instance, import that record file under Validation record file.
    3. Tick Specification confirmed (required for registries whose specification is not verified) and, if you have it, enter the Registry test sign-off reference.
    4. Check the Go-live pre-checks list. Then select Request go-live.
    5. An approver (registry:live-register:approve) chooses I am approving as, selects Approve with my credentials, and re-enters their credentials. The number of approvals needed (1 to 3) and whether the requester may approve are settings on a production instance.
    6. To cancel a request select Withdraw request. To stop reporting select Stop live reporting.

    Expected result: a production instance sends real results only to a registry with a current approval; results for others are held. Each request, approval and stop appears in the Go-live history. The same panel appears on Cytology Registry Reporting. Reference: Cancer Registry Reporting.

    # Not built: fee schedules and quality reporting

    Home › Configuration › System › Financial & Revenue Lookups
    • Fee schedules: Not built. There is no screen, field or contract for a price or payer rate. Keep prices in your billing system.
    • MIPS and MACRA quality reporting: Not built. See Quality and public health reporting. The nearest things are the reporting feed to a business intelligence tool and the CSV exports.
    • Auto-coding from the report text by AI: Not built. The rule-based code suggestions are described in Auto-coding and billing hold rules.
    • X12 837P, KVDT and SESAM-Vitale output: Not built. The payload is JSON for the interface engine.

    # Common problems

    Home › Configuration › System
    What you see Likely cause What to do
    A label type shows Enterprise Standard: Locked and no facility choice Block, Slide and the four Molecular types allow only an enterprise default Edit the enterprise default. A facility cannot override these types.
    "Not saved: a field goes past the edge of the label." A field is outside the label Select Fit to label, or move or resize the field, then save.
    The canvas changed and my edits are gone Changing Label Type or Scope reloads the saved layout without warning Save before you switch. Use Version history to recover a saved version.
    A saved layout does not appear on the printed label The layout has no fields (it counts as none), or a facility override is hiding the enterprise one Check the scope you saved to. For a facility, an override takes the place of the default.
    The text after Export EPL is headed "Exported ZPL" The heading does not change Read the note above the text; it says which language the text is in.
    Labels open the browser print dialog instead of printing The printer profile is not on the QZ Tray bridge, or no profile is chosen Set the profile on Printer Profiles and choose it in Print Settings.
    "Choose the cassette printer first." Cassettes were ticked on Label reprint with no printer Choose the Cassette printer.
    The CPT search in a billing rule is empty The RVU Code Map has no active codes Add codes and have them approved.
    A change never takes effect It is waiting for a second person, or it was rejected Open Pending Billing Rule Approvals; a different person approves.
    Approve is locked You drafted or submitted the change Ask a different approver.
    Retire is not offered Only an ACTIVE version can be retired Check the version's status in History.
    No New Version button on a row The row is Inherited from the enterprise Use Duplicate to give the site its own rule.
    "Code (code) already exists in the active version." The code is already in the RVU Code Map Edit it instead.
    The modifier upload does nothing The licence box is not ticked, or the effective date is blank Tick the licence confirmation and enter a valid date.
    A deficiency blocks the billing export An open billing deficiency exists on the case Resolve it, then export again.
    Charges release too early or too late A trigger or a release rule differs from what you expect Check Charge Release Triggers, then test with Try a charge.
    A payment type cannot be picked for a mapping The type is inactive Reactivate it on the Master Payment Type Dictionary.

    # Glossary

    Each term below is linked the first time it is used in a section of the guide. A standard or vendor named here is defined as a term; whether PathScribe supports it is stated in the chapter for the feature, never in the glossary.

    • ACK: In HL7, the acknowledgement message a receiving system returns to say it accepted, or refused, a message.
    • accession: The act of receiving a specimen and giving it a permanent case number; also that number (the accession number). It ties a case to the physical tissue and its chain of custody.
    • accession number: The permanent identifier of a case, built from the facility's case mask. It is treated as a patient identifier on screen: it is shown inside patient-data tags so that screenshots can be redacted.
    • action group: A named bundle of Action Registry commands that a workstation group can allow or load by default.
    • Action Registry: The list of voice and keyboard commands PathScribe knows. The commands are not access control; capabilities are.
    • ADT: Admit, Discharge, Transfer. The family of HL7 messages that carry patient registration and movement, such as A01 (admit), A08 (update patient) and A40 (merge patients).
    • AI vendor policy: A per-jurisdiction rule that says which AI services and hosting regions may be used. A call the rule refuses is not sent, and the feature carries on without AI.
    • AMA: American Medical Association, the publisher and owner of the CPT code set.
    • AP-LIS: Anatomic pathology laboratory information system, the system that runs surgical pathology and cytology cases from accessioning to sign-out.
    • API: Application programming interface. The PathScribe API server is the ASP.NET Core service the browser calls for all production data.
    • APLIS mapping: The value a container type is sent as in the specimen field of an HL7 message, so another system can recognise the container.
    • append-only: A record that can be added to but never edited or deleted by the application. The audit log is append-only by design.
    • ASP.NET Core: The Microsoft web framework PathScribe's API server is built on.
    • assist mode: A way of running PathScribe beside an existing LIS, where the LIS keeps ownership of the case and PathScribe reads its updates and drafts reports for pathologist review.
    • audit log: The record of what people, the system and the AI did, read on the System Logs screen. Its detail text is English and contains no patient names or clinical values.
    • BAA: Business Associate Agreement. A contract the HIPAA rules require between a US healthcare organisation and a vendor that handles its protected health information.
    • Bethesda: The reporting system for cervical cytology results and specimen adequacy, used in the United States and widely elsewhere.
    • BI feed: The reporting feed that supplies datasets to a business-intelligence tool such as Power BI. It can be de-identified or identified, and identified use needs an approval on record.
    • block: A piece of tissue embedded in wax inside a cassette, from which slides are cut.
    • break-glass: A restricted action that overrides a normal safeguard and always needs a reason and a written justification. The patient rebind on System Logs is an example.
    • BSN: Burgerservicenummer, the national citizen service number of the Netherlands, used as a patient identifier.
    • cancer registry: A body that collects cancer diagnoses for a country or region, such as NAACCR registries in North America or the COSD collection in England.
    • CAP: The College of American Pathologists. It accredits laboratories and publishes the cancer protocols (checklists) that PathScribe's synoptic reports follow.
    • CAP eCC: CAP electronic Cancer Checklists, the structured form of the CAP cancer protocols, distributed as SDC XML.
    • CAPA: Corrective and preventive action. A tracked response to a quality problem, with an owner and a reason for opening or dismissing it.
    • capability: One permission, named in the form domain:object:verb, such as config:roles:manage. Roles are granted capabilities, and every protected action checks one.
    • capability catalog: The complete list of capabilities, with each one's risk level and any capability it requires.
    • case: One patient episode in the laboratory, identified by an accession number and made up of one or more specimens and one report.
    • case mask: The pattern an accession number follows: a prefix, a pattern such as the year and a sequence number, and a counter that is never reset by a change of pattern.
    • cassette: The plastic holder in which a tissue block is embedded and labelled for cutting.
    • charge capture: Recording the billable work done on a case so it can be sent for billing.
    • CHI number: Community Health Index, the patient identifier used in Scotland.
    • CLIA: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments, the US federal regulations for laboratory testing. CLIA sets, among other things, limits on cytology workload.
    • client service level: The agreed time in which a client's cases should be reported, held per client facility.
    • CMS: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, the US agency that sets Medicare billing rules, including NCCI edits.
    • config.json: The file on the web server that gives a deployment its settings, such as the API server address. A wrong value stops PathScribe from starting.
    • consult link: A view-only link issued to an outside consultant for one case. It can be revoked at once and expires on its own.
    • COSD: Cancer Outcomes and Services Dataset, the English national dataset for cancer registration.
    • countersign: A second signature on a report from another qualified person, for example a pathologist on a cytotechnologist's work.
    • CPT: Current Procedural Terminology, the AMA's code set for medical and laboratory procedures, used for billing in the United States.
    • CRM: Circumferential resection margin, the distance from a tumour to the cut edge of a resection, recorded on colorectal reports.
    • critical result: A finding the laboratory must communicate quickly to the clinician, with the communication recorded.
    • crosswalk: A table that translates a code from one system into another, such as an outside order code into a PathScribe specimen type.
    • CSV: Comma-separated values, a plain-text spreadsheet format. PathScribe's exports are CSV files.
    • cytotechnologist: A laboratory professional who screens cytology slides and refers abnormal ones to a pathologist.
    • dead letter: A message or job that failed every automatic retry and now waits for a person to resend or discard it.
    • delegation: Handing a case to another pathologist for a peer review, second opinion, subspecialty referral or tumor board discussion.
    • demonstration build: A build of PathScribe that holds its data in the browser and carries demonstration accounts. It never connects to a real API server.
    • department: The coarse class of a specimen at intake, such as surgical tissue or fluid cytology. It steers the grossing template, the case mask and any retention override.
    • DFT: Detailed Financial Transaction, the HL7 message that carries charges to a billing system.
    • discordance: A difference between two reads of the same material, such as a preliminary and a final diagnosis, or a first and a second pathologist.
    • display profile: A saved layout of dashboard tiles that a wall display shows.
    • DLQ: Dead-letter queue, the list of messages that failed every retry. System Logs has one for outbound interface messages and one for charges.
    • DOB: Date of birth.
    • DOS: Date of service, the date a billed service was performed.
    • DPA: Data processing agreement, the contract required under GDPR between a data controller and a processor.
    • embedding: The step where processed tissue is set in wax in a cassette to make a block.
    • EMR: Electronic medical record, the hospital system that holds the patient's chart and sends orders.
    • enterprise: The top level of a customer's organisation in PathScribe. Settings made here apply to every jurisdiction and facility below unless they are overridden.
    • ePath: Electronic pathology reporting, the sending of pathology reports to a cancer registry in a standard electronic form.
    • error code: A short upper-case code, such as NOT_PERMITTED, that tells a screen or an administrator why a call failed. The server's message text is never used, because it could name a patient.
    • EU: European Union.
    • facility: One laboratory or site within an enterprise. A performing-lab facility does the testing; a client facility only sends specimens.
    • FAD: Final anatomical diagnosis, the final diagnosis of an autopsy report, the counterpart of the PAD.
    • FHIR: Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources, an HL7 standard for exchanging health data through web interfaces.
    • field requirements: The settings that decide which fields a page must have filled in before a step can be completed.
    • flag: A marker placed on a case or specimen, for example to order an extra stain or to hold a case.
    • FNA: Fine-needle aspiration, a biopsy that draws cells through a thin needle.
    • FOV: Field of view, a region on a cytology slide that an AI tool or a screener examines.
    • four-eyes principle: A rule that one person prepares a change and a different person approves it. The billing code import uses it.
    • FPPE: Focused professional practice evaluation, a structured review of a clinician's work, used for new privileges or a concern.
    • frozen section: A tissue sample frozen and cut while the patient is in surgery so a pathologist can give a quick answer.
    • GDPR: The EU General Data Protection Regulation. The UK has its own version, UK GDPR.
    • governing body: The authority whose rules a jurisdiction follows, such as CAP or a national college, which sets minimum retention periods and requirements.
    • GS1: The standards organisation behind the barcode formats and the GTIN numbering used on cassette and slide labels.
    • GTIN: Global Trade Item Number, the number a GS1 barcode carries. Print Settings holds the facility's GTIN.
    • GYN: Gynaecologic, as in GYN cytology, the screening of cervical samples.
    • grossing: The examination and cutting of a surgical specimen by a pathologist or pathologists' assistant, describing it and choosing the pieces to process.
    • HCPCS: Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System, the US code set that adds codes to CPT for supplies and services.
    • HIPAA: The US Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, which sets rules for protecting patient health information.
    • histotechnologist: A laboratory professional who embeds tissue and cuts and stains slides.
    • HL7: Health Level Seven, the family of standards for exchanging healthcare information between systems.
    • HL7 v2: The widely used HL7 message format made of lines of pipe-separated fields, each message starting with an MSH segment.
    • hosting region: The geographic region where a cloud AI service processes data. The AI vendor policy can allow or refuse regions.
    • HPV: Human papillomavirus. A high-risk HPV (hrHPV) result is used with cervical cytology.
    • hub: The SignalR service that pushes live updates from the API server to open screens.
    • ICD-10: The International Classification of Diseases, tenth revision, a diagnosis code set.
    • ICD-11: The eleventh revision of the International Classification of Diseases.
    • ICD-O: International Classification of Diseases for Oncology, which codes tumour site and type (morphology). The third edition is ICD-O-3, with codes such as 8500/3.
    • identity provider: The service that signs people in for single sign-on, such as a hospital's Microsoft Entra directory.
    • IHC: Immunohistochemistry, a stain that uses antibodies to show specific proteins in tissue.
    • inking: Marking the surface of a specimen with colored ink so margins can be recognised on the slide.
    • intraoperative: During surgery. Intraoperative consultations, such as frozen sections, are handled in the intraoperative queue.
    • IPP: Internet Printing Protocol, a network print protocol. In French text IPP is also the patient identifier used in place of MRN.
    • IPPS: Internet Printing Protocol over TLS. A printer on IPPS confirms that a job was printed, which is why a site's report printers should use it where they can.
    • ISO 15189: The international standard for the quality and competence of medical laboratories.
    • jurisdiction: A country or national health system whose rules PathScribe applies, such as the United States, England and Wales or Germany. It sets code systems, signing rules, retention floors and formats.
    • JSON: JavaScript Object Notation, a plain-text data format used by the API, by config.json and by webhooks.
    • LBC: Liquid-based cytology, a way of preparing cervical and other cytology samples in liquid.
    • LIS: Laboratory information system, the software that runs a laboratory's orders, specimens and results.
    • LOINC: Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes, a code set for laboratory tests and observations.
    • lockbox: A drop-off point where specimens are received outside working hours. Each drop gets a receipt, and a barcode with no order gets a placeholder, never an accession number.
    • LPR: Line Printer Remote, an older network print protocol (also written LPR/LPD). It cannot confirm that a page was printed.
    • MACRA: The US Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act, which created the Quality Payment Program that includes MIPS.
    • macro: A saved piece of text or a set of settings, such as a report phrase or a stain order, that can be inserted in one step.
    • MDT: Multidisciplinary team meeting, also called a tumor board, where specialists discuss a patient's care.
    • MFA: Multi-factor authentication, signing in with a second proof such as a code from an authenticator app, as well as a password.
    • microtomy: Cutting thin sections from a block with a microtome to make slides.
    • MIPS: The Merit-based Incentive Payment System, a US Medicare program that adjusts payment by reported quality measures.
    • Milan System: The reporting system for salivary gland fine-needle aspiration cytology.
    • modifier: A short code added to a CPT code to say how a service was done, for example that only the technical component was provided.
    • Mohs: Mohs micrographic surgery, where skin cancer is removed in thin layers and each layer is checked under the microscope before the next is taken.
    • MPI: Master patient index, the record that links the different identifiers one patient has.
    • MRN: Medical record number, the identifier a facility gives a patient.
    • MSH: The first segment of an HL7 v2 message. It names the sender, receiver, message type and version.
    • NAACCR: The North American Association of Central Cancer Registries, which sets data standards for cancer registry reporting in North America.
    • NATA: The National Association of Testing Authorities, which accredits laboratories in Australia.
    • NCCI: National Correct Coding Initiative, a set of US Medicare edits that say which code pairs cannot be billed together.
    • NCRAS: The National Cancer Registration and Analysis Service, the English cancer registry body that receives COSD submissions.
    • NHI: National Health Index, the patient identifier used in New Zealand.
    • NHS number: The ten-digit patient identifier used in the NHS in England and Wales. The last digit is a check digit.
    • NLM: The US National Library of Medicine, source of public terminology look-ups such as UMLS.
    • non-GYN: Cytology other than cervical screening, such as fluids, urine and fine-needle aspirates.
    • NPI: National Provider Identifier, the ten-digit identifier of a US healthcare provider, needed on a charge.
    • OIDC: OpenID Connect, the sign-in standard PathScribe uses for single sign-on.
    • OML: The HL7 laboratory order message type (OML^O21).
    • OPCS-4: The UK classification of surgical operations and procedures.
    • ORM: The HL7 general order message type (ORM^O01).
    • ORU: The HL7 unsolicited observation result message type. ORU^R01 carries a result.
    • outbound queue: The list of messages and charges PathScribe has built and not yet sent, held, sent or failed.
    • OR terminal: A screen in an operating room suite used to see and act on intraoperative cases.
    • PAD: Preliminary anatomical diagnosis, the first diagnosis of an autopsy report. A body can be released once a PAD is signed and no ancillary hold is active.
    • Paris System: The reporting system for urinary tract cytology.
    • participation type: A role a person plays on a case, such as primary pathologist or screener, with its own signing authority.
    • part library: The reusable parts, such as a block of questions, from which report templates are assembled.
    • PDF: Portable Document Format, the form in which a signed report is stored and printed.
    • peer review: An independent read of a case by a second pathologist, which can be required before sign-out for a first malignancy.
    • performing lab: The facility that does the testing and issues the report, as opposed to a client that only sends specimens.
    • PHI: Protected health information, any data that identifies a patient together with health information. Patient identifiers on screen are tagged so screenshots can be redacted.
    • PHIN-MS: The Public Health Information Network Messaging System, a US transport for sending public health reports.
    • placeholder: A record made for a lockbox barcode that has no order yet. It holds the receipt and is linked to an order later; it never gets an accession number.
    • PPS number: The Personal Public Service number used as a patient identifier in Ireland.
    • print queue: The list of report and label print jobs with their status, from queued to printed or failed.
    • printer profile: The saved settings for one model of printer, including its connection method (bridge).
    • production gate: A switch that stays closed until a lab approves sending real data to a real interface engine.
    • protocol: A structured set of questions for reporting one kind of case, such as a CAP cancer protocol, from which a synoptic report is built.
    • QA: Quality assurance, the review of work to find and correct problems.
    • QC: Quality control, the checks that confirm a process works as intended, such as a second review of screened slides.
    • QZ Tray: A small program on a computer that lets a web page print to a local printer, such as a label printer, without a print dialog.
    • RBAC: Role-based access control. People are given roles, roles hold capabilities, and a capability decides whether an action is allowed.
    • reagent lot: A tracked batch of a stain, solution or reagent, with its dates and its use.
    • reference lab: A laboratory to which testing is sent out. A facility is given the Reference Lab role.
    • registry: A body that collects reports of a disease or a screening result for a country or program, such as a cancer or cervical screening registry.
    • retention: How long a kind of data or material is kept. Retention periods are set by jurisdiction, with an optional override.
    • retention hold: A hold that stops disposal of a case's material after finalisation, for example for litigation.
    • role: A named set of capabilities given to staff, such as Admin or Pathologist. A person can hold several roles.
    • ROSE: Rapid on-site evaluation, where a specimen's adequacy is judged at the time it is taken.
    • RVU: Relative value unit, the measure of the work and cost of a service used in Medicare payment and in productivity reports.
    • SAML: Security Assertion Markup Language, an older single sign-on standard. PathScribe's single sign-on uses OIDC.
    • scan station: A named bench computer setup, with its printers and display, that a person selects so labels and scans go to the right place.
    • SCIM: System for Cross-domain Identity Management, a standard by which an identity provider creates and deactivates staff accounts automatically.
    • SDC: Structured Data Capture, the XML form standard used to distribute CAP electronic cancer checklists.
    • separation of duties: A rule that two powers must not rest with one person, such as changing the clinical mismatch rules and approving the AI instructions.
    • server build: A build of PathScribe for a real deployment, with no demonstration accounts, that signs in through the identity provider and talks to the API server.
    • SFTP: SSH File Transfer Protocol, a secure way of copying files to another system.
    • SHA-256: A cryptographic hash that turns a file or record into a fixed fingerprint, used to detect a change.
    • SignalR: The Microsoft technology PathScribe uses to push live updates from the server to open screens.
    • signing authority: The kinds of report a person may sign out, set by participation type and the rules of the country.
    • single sign-on: Signing in once with an organisation's identity provider instead of a PathScribe password. Also written SSO.
    • site agent: A small Windows service installed at a laboratory that prints reports and labels and writes files to shares on the hospital network, on instructions from the API server.
    • SLA: Service level agreement, an agreed time in which work is done.
    • SNOMED CT: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine, Clinical Terms, a large clinical terminology.
    • specimen: A sample taken from a patient, such as one biopsy or one resected organ. A case holds one or more specimens.
    • SSO: Single sign-on. See single sign-on.
    • stain: A dye or antibody applied to a slide so a feature of the tissue can be seen.
    • STAT: Urgent, to be done at once.
    • subspecialty: An area of pathology, such as breast or gastrointestinal, used to route cases. A subspecialty can be switched to pool mode.
    • support reference: A random, non-identifying code of the form SR-XXXX-XXXX that staff quote to support in place of a case number.
    • synoptic: A report built from a fixed set of structured questions, so that each required item is answered in the same form.
    • TAT: Turnaround time, the time from one step to another, such as from receipt to sign-out.
    • tenant: One customer organisation's separate space within a shared PathScribe service.
    • TC: Technical component, the part of a service that covers the laboratory's work, billed apart from the professional component (code 26).
    • TLS: Transport Layer Security, the encryption that protects a web connection and shows as https.
    • tumor board: A multidisciplinary meeting to discuss cancer cases. Also called an MDT.
    • UKAS: The United Kingdom Accreditation Service, which accredits laboratories in the UK.
    • UMLS: The Unified Medical Language System, a US National Library of Medicine collection of medical vocabularies.
    • UTC: Coordinated Universal Time, the time standard in which audit entries are stored and shown.
    • VNA: Vendor-neutral archive, an image store that holds medical images in a neutral form.
    • WCAG: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, the standard for making web content usable by people with disabilities.
    • webhook: A web address that one system calls to push an update to another, such as an LIS sending a status change as JSON.
    • workstation: A registered computer at a facility, with its discipline, area and bound printers.
    • workstation group: A set of scan stations grouped by discipline and area, scoped to a facility and given default action groups.
    • WSI: Whole slide imaging, scanning a glass slide into a digital image that can be viewed on screen.
    • X12: The ANSI standard for electronic business transactions, including healthcare claims in the United States.
    • XML: Extensible Markup Language, a text format used by CAP SDC forms and some registry files.
    • ZPL: Zebra Programming Language, the printer language that describes a label's layout for Zebra-type label printers.
